Sikh Sect.q: Which of the followings Gurus started 'Gurumukhi'?
Sikh Sect.explanation: 'Gurumukhi' originates from Punjabi word 'Gurumukha' that means – from the mouth of Guru. Gurumukhi script was started by second Sikh Guru, Guru Angad.

Sikh Sect.q: The city of Amritsar in Punjab was established by:
Sikh Sect.explanation: Gazzetteer of Amritsar district, mentions that the fourth Guru Ramdas obtained from Akbar the grant of piece of land (around 500 bighas) on the spot where now stands the city of Amritsar and dug the holy tank, and commenced the erection of a temple in its midst. Some sources also state that it was gifted to Bibi Bhani (wife of Guru Ramdas) by Akbar. Ramdas died in 1581 A.D. and his son & successor, Guru Arjan completed the temple.

Sikh Sect.q: To which Sikh Guru, Akbar donated 500 Bighas of land?
Sikh Sect.explanation: See the explanation of above question.

Sikh Sect.q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
options: Guru Amar Das  - Miri and Piri
Sikh Sect.explanation: Fifth Sikh Guru Arjan Dev compiled the holy book of Sikhism "Adi Granth" in 1604 A.D. He was executed by Jahangir for aiding to Prince Khusrau. Guru Amardas divided the religious empire into 22 branches called Manji and appointed a local Sikh preacher at each place. Dal Khalsa was established by Kapur Singh.

Sikh Sect.q: Which Sikh Guru helped rebel prince Khusrau with shelter and wealth :
Sikh Sect.explanation: Prince Khusrau revolted in 1606 A.D. He escaped to Punjab where he received the blessings and some fi nancial help from Guru Arjan Dev. Jahangir was displeased with Guru Arjan Dev. He fi ned Guru Arjan Dev. After the rejection, Guru Arjan Dev was imprisoned and sentenced to death by torture and suff ered the first great martyrdom. He was the 5th  Guru of Sikhs. He constructed Sri Harmandir Sahib in the lake of Amritsar. He established two cities named Tarn Taran and Kartarpur (in Jalandhar doab).

Sikh Sect.q: Who of the following compiled “Adi Granth or Guru Granth Sahib”?
Sikh Sect.explanation: Adi Granth or Guru Granth Sahib was compiled by Arjan Dev, 5th Sikh Guru (1581-1606 A.D.). It contains preachings of six Sikh Gurus, many Hindu/muslim saints like, Kabir, Baba Farid, Namdev and Raidas. Among the first composition of Adi Granth was written by Vaishnav poet Jaydev and the last composition were of Guru Tegh Bahadur.

Sikh Sect.q:
Which of the following Sikh Gurus were penalized with death by the Rulers of the time : 
 1.  Guru Angad
 2.  Guru Arjun Dev
 3.  Guru Har Gobind  
   4.  Guru Tegh Bahadur
 Select the correct answer from the code given below:
 Code :
Sikh Sect.explanation:
Guru Arjan Dev and Guru Tegh Bahadur were awarded death sentence by their contemporary rulers, Jahangir and Aurangzeb respectively.
Guru Arjan Dev  (1581-1606 A.D.)- He was the 5th Sikh Guru. After the revolt against  Jahangir, his rebellious son Prince Khusrau fl ed from Agra to Afghanistan. During his escape Khusrau met Guru Arjan Dev at Tarn Taran city. Guru gave him support and shelter due to which Jahangir got angry with Guru Arjan Dev.  Jahangir accused him of conspiracy and sentenced him to death sentence in 1606 AD. Guru Arjan Dev established Taran Taran and Kartarpur towns. His major work was a compilation of Guru Granth Sahib. 
Guru Tegh Bahadur (1664-1675 A.D.):  Revered as the ninth Nanak, he was the ninth of ten Gurus of the Sikh religion. According to the records written by his son Guru Gobind Singh, the Guru had resisted persecution, observed and promised to protect Kashmiri Hindus. The Guru was summoned to Delhi by Aurangzeb on the protest but when he arrived, he was off ered “to abandon his faith and convert to Islam.” Guru Tegh Bahadur refused, he and his associates were arrested. He was executed on November, 1675 before the public in Chandni Chowk, Delhi.

Sikh Sect.q: At which of the following places is a famous Sikh Gurudwara located?
Sikh Sect.explanation: The famous Sikh gurudwara is located in Hem Kund (Chamoli, Uttarakhand).

Sikh Sect.q: Which Sikh Guru was born in Patna?
Sikh Sect.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth and the last Sikh Guru. He was born in 1666 A.D. in Patna (Bihar). He introduced ‘Khalsa Panth’ and consolidated the Sikh community as a warrior.

Sikh Sect.q: Nanded is considered sacred by Sikhs due to whose Mausoleum?
Sikh Sect.explanation: The 10th Sikh Guru and last Guru, Guru Gobind Singh was assassinated in Nanded (Maharashtra) by an Afghani noble. 'Takhat Sachkhand Sri Hazur Abchalnagar Sahib' Gurudwara of Nanded is situated at his cremation site.

Sikh Sect.q: Guru Gobind Singh’s greatness lies in the fact that :
options: He formed the military order of Sikhs
He was the founder of Sikh state
Sikh Sect.explanation: The 10th Guru and last prophet of Sikhism, Guru Gobind Singh converted Sikhs into a military sect ‘‘Khalsa Panth’’. He called the whole Sikh community as ‘‘Khalsa’’. He ordered Sikhs that each Sikh should have the surname of 'Singh' (male) and 'Kaur' (female) and should hold 5 k's- Kesh, Kangha, Kachha, Kripan and Kada.

Sikh Sect.explanation: See the explanation of above question.

Sikh Sect.q: How many years ago Khalsa Panth started?
Sikh Sect.explanation: Khalsa Panth was established on 13th April, 1699, on the day of  Baisakhi by 10th Sikh Guru Gobind Singh in Anandpur Sahib. Therefore, it has been more than 300 years since Khalsa Panth started.

Sikh Sect.explanation: See the explanation of above question.

Sikh Sect.explanation: See the explanation of above question.

Sikh Sect.q: The original name of Banda Bahadur was
Sikh Sect.explanation: The  other name of  Banda Bahadur was Lachman Dev. This name was given to him by Sikh Guru Gobind Singh.

Maratha State and Confederacy.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1992. All factors are correct for the rise of Marathas. Maratha’s rise was neither specifi c nor the result of unstable circumstances generated in a specifi c period. The reason for Maratha rise was its residents, whose nationalism was on the ground of regional/collective consciousness alogn with religious toleration and integration of diff erent social groups. The geographical conditions of Maharashtra were helpful in fl ourishing the Maratha power. The high leadership quality of Shivaji and other Maratha leaders contributed to the rise of Maratha power.]

Maratha State and Confederacy.q: What was the name of Shivaji’s Guru?
Maratha State and Confederacy.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2016. Samarth Ramdas was the guru of Shivaji. He is remembered for his Advaita Vedantic text ‘Daasbodh.’ He also wrote the poem in praise of King Shivaji by the name of ‘Shivastuti.’]

Maratha State and Confederacy.q: Ashtapradhan was a Council of Ministers :
Maratha State and Confederacy.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2013, I.A.S. (Pre) 1996. 'Ashtapradhan' was a council of eight ministers (reaching 8 in no by 1674) under Shivaji in Maratha administration. The eight ministers were 1. Peshwa, 2. Pandit Rao, 3. Sumant, 4. Amatya, 5. Mantri, 6. Sachiv, 7. Senapati, 8. Nyayadhish. (i) Peshwa- Prime Minister of King (ii) Amatya or Mazumdar- Finance and Revenue Minister (iii) Waqianavis/Mantri- Interior minister, managing internal aff airs, especially intelligence and espionage. (iv) Sachiv/Surnavis-Responsible for all correspondence. (v) Sumant/Dabir- Foreign Minister (vi) Senapati/Sar-i-Naubat - Maintenance of appointments, organization and food supply of military. (vii) Pandit Rao- High Priest (viii) Nyayadhish- Chief Justice]

Maratha State and Confederacy.q: Assertion (A) : In matters of State Shivaji was advised by a Council of Ministers. Reason (R) : Each minister held independent charge of his department. Code:
options: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Maratha State and Confederacy.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1997. The "Ashtapradhan" was a council of eight ministers who administered the Maratha empire during Shivaji reign. They were not working as a cabinet, each minister was the head of his department. It was up to Shivaji whether he accepted or rejected the given advice. Ashtapradhan acted as the secretary of Shivaji. To follow the orders of Shivaji and look after the state widely were the main functions of the Ministers. So, assertion (A) is correct but reason (R) is incorrect.]

Maratha State and Confederacy.q: Below are two statements, one of which is an Assertion (A) and the other is a Reason (R): Assertion (A) : Shivaji had to face opposition from big Deshmukhs. Reason (R) : These Deshmukhs were not in support of the independent Maratha state and wanted to remain as feudal lords of Bijapur. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(c) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Maratha State and Confederacy.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2024. Shivaji had to face opposition from powerful landlords (Deshmukhs) because the landlords wanted to maintain their power and infl uence. Hence, statement (A) is true. The Deshmukhs were not in favour of an independent Maratha state and wanted to remain subordinates of Bijapur, as remaining under Bijapur allowed them autonomy and opportunities to maintain their special privileges. This is why they opposed Shivaji. Thus, statement (R) is also true, and (R) correctly explains (A).]

Maratha State and Confederacy.q: Which of the following coins was NOT a silver coin in the Kingdom of Chhatrapati Shivaji?
Maratha State and Confederacy.explanation: [U.P.R.O./ A.R.O. (Mains) 2016. Lari, Rupaya & Taka were silver coins during the reign of Chhatrapati Shivaji, while Ruka was a coin in Kakatiya dynasty.]

Maratha State and Confederacy.q: Who among the following streamlined the Maratha administration after Shambhaji?
Maratha State and Confederacy.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2000. After Sambhaji, the power of the Maratha Kingdom came into the hands of Balaji Vishwanath who made the administration easy and convenient. November 1713 A.D. was important not only for Balaji but also for whole Marathas as the power was transferred from Chhatrapati to the Peshwas. His main achievement was a temporary agreement between the Mughals and the Marathas by which the authority and region were properly described.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Who succeeded Aurangzeb after his death in 1707 A.D.?
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2012. After the death of the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb, his sixty three year old son Muazzam (Shah Alam) ascended the throne adopting the name of Bahadur Shah in 1707 A.D. He ruled over the duration of 1707-1712 A.D.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: How did the Mughal Emperor Jahandar Shah’s reign come to an early end?
options: (a) He was deposed by his Wazir
(b) He died due to slip while climbing down steps
(c) He was defeated by his nephew in a battle
(d) He died of sickness due to too much consumption of wine.
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2003. Jahandar Shah was the first Mughal emperor who proved to be unfi t for governance. He ascended the throne with the help of contemporary, powerful Amir Zulfi qar Khan. He was defeated by his nephew, Farrukh Siyar and killed on Feb, 1713. People called him ‘’lewd Moron’’.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Which of the following Mughal Emperors granted duty-free trading facilities to the English in Bengal?
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P.P.S.C. (GIC) 2010. Farrukh Siyar issued a decree in which he granted duty-free trading facilities to the Britishers in Bengal in 1717 A.D. It was mentioned in the contract that the East India Company could trade without duty (charge) after paying the annual tax of 3000.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Who among the following were the 'King makers' during Mughal period?
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Mains) 2017. During the later Mughal period, Nobles came to power who were called king-makers. From 1713 to 1720 AD, Sayyid brothers, Hussain Ali and Abdullah were the most powerful. They were leaders of Hindustani group. They were famous as 'King Makers'. They made Farrukh Siyar king in 1713 AD and dethroned him in 1719 AD. After that puppet king Rafi -ud-darjat, Rafi -ud-daula and Muhammad Shah sat on throne with their help. They lost power during Muhammad Shah's regin.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Who was the last Mughal Emperor to sit on Mayur Singhasan?
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [40th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1995. Muhammad Shah (1719 - 1748 A.D.) was the last Mughal emperor to sit on Mayur Singhasan/ Takht-i-Taus during his reign. Nadir Shah attacked India in 1739 A.D. and defeated Mughals in Karnal Battle. The contemporary historian Anand Ram Mukhlis wrote, "Nadir Shah took sixty thousand rupees, many thousands of gold coins, gold worth of one crore rupees, jewels of fi fty crores, Kohinoor and peacock throne with him to Iran".]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: The Mughal Emperor at the time of Nadir Shah’s attack was
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2004. See the explanation of above question]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: In which of the following year did Nadir Shah invade India?
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2023. Nadir Shah invaded India in the year 1739 AD. The invasion culminated in the sack of Delhi, during which the city suff ered widespread destruction, looting and the loss of many lives. This event is known as the Battle of Karnal and it had signifi cant repercussions for the Mughal Empire, contributing to its decline and the subsequent rise of regional powers in India.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: A group of eunuchs and ladies dominated in the Government under
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2004. Muhammad Shah (1719-48 A.D.) spent his most of his time in watching animal fi ghts. People called him ‘’Rangeela’’ due to his obsession with wine and beauty and apathy towards administration. A group of eunuchs and ladies predominated in Mughal Darbar during the regime of Muhammad Shah.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Which Mughal emperor is known by the name of ‘Rangeela’?
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2014. See the explanation of above question.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Arrange the following into chronological order and select the correct answer from the codes given below : A. Muhammand Shah B. Jahandar Shah C. Alamgir II D. Ahmadshah Codes :
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2018. The chronological order of Mughal rulers mentioned above is- Jahandar Shah (1712-13 A.D.) Muhammad Shah (1719 1748 A.D.), Ahmad Shah (1748-54 A.D.) and Alamgir II (1754-1759 A.D.).]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Consider the following Mughal Emperors and arrange them in chronological order : I. Farrukhsiyar II. Jahandar Shah III.Bahadur Shah IV. Muhammad Shah Select the correct answer using the code given below: Code
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2023. The chronological order of Mughal emperors is as follows Bahadur Shah -I (1707-1712 A.D.), Jahandar Shah (1712-1713 A.D.), Farrukhsiyar (1713-1719 A.D.), Muhammad Shah 'Rangeela' (1719-1748 A.D.) Hence, the correct option is option (c).]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Which of the following Mughal emperors was not allowed to enter into Delhi by Wazir Ghaziuddin?
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [44th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2000. Shah Alam- II tenure was from 1759 to 1806 A.D. His real name was Ali Gauhar. He became the victim of conspiracies hatched at the royal court. He reached Delhi with the help of Marathas in 1772 A.D. During his rule only, English captured Delhi in 1803 A.D.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: The last Mughal Emperor was Bahadur Shah. His father’s name was
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2005. The last Mughal Emperor was Bahadur Shah Zafar (1837-57 A.D.). His father’s name was Akbar- II. He was a pensioner of British and head of the royal court of Red Fort of Delhi. He died in 1862 A.D.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Who was last Mughal emperor of India?
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2000. See the explanation of above question.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Which one of the following statements is not correct about Bahadur Shah Zafar ?
options: (a) He was an emperor without an empire
(b) Ibrahim Zauq and Asad Ullah Khan Ghalib were his poetry teachers
(c) Hasan Askari was his spiritual guide
(d) He received less than one lakh rupees as pension from East India Company
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2006. Bahadur Shah Zafar received one lakh rupees per month as a pension, which consisted of Rs. 99000 given in Delhi and one thousand rupees for regular family expenses in Lucknow. So, option (d) is not correct, but other statements are correct.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: About Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar, it was said that his empire extended from :
options: (e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [64th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2018. It was said about last Tughalaq ruler Nasirruddin Mahmud that, "The rule of the Lord of the world extends from Delhi to Palam". BPSC had removed this question from evaluation.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Who among the following was the first Nawab of Oudh?
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2008. The first Nawab of Oudh was Saadat Khan. Turanis established Hyderabad and Iranis established Oudh. In 1722 A.D., Saadat Khan was appointed as the governor of Oudh where he governed through his heir nephew Safdarjung and played high politics in Awadh royal court. After his death, Safdarjung refused to give nominal loyalty to the Mughal Emperor.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: With reference to the Burhan-ul-Mulk Saadat Khan, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. Saadat Khan was the founder of Independent state of Awadh. 2. He took part in the conspiracy against the Sayyid Brothers. Select the correct answer from the code given below : Code
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2023. The independent state of Awadh was formed during reign of Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah. The founder of this state was Saadat Khan. Saadat Khan had taken the side of emperor Muhammad Shah in the conspiracy hatched against the Sayyid brothers. Pleased with his work, Muhammad Shah gave him the title of Burhan-ul-Mulk. Hence both statements are correct.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Who among the following was the founder of independent Kingdom of Hyderabad?
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011. Chin Qilich Khan aka Nizam-ul-Mulk founded the independent kingdom of Hyderabad in 1724 A.D. Nizam became the real king after the death of the Mughal governor Mubarij Khan in the battle of Sakhar-Kherda of Deccan, 1724 A.D.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Which of the following is/are not true? (i) Kilich Khan was also known as Mubariz Khan. (ii) Nizam-ul-Mulk defeated Mubariz Khan in Battle of Shakar Kheda. (iii) Julfi kar Khan gave Nizam-ul-Mulk with the title of Asaf-Jah.
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2022. Qilich Khan was called as Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah. The Battle of Sakhar Kherda was held in 1724 AD between Nizam-ul-Mulk and Mubariz Khan. He defeated and killed Mubariz Khan. Mughal emperor Mohammad Shah gave Nizam-ul-Mulk the title of Asaf-Jah.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: With reference to Indian history, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. The Nizamat of Arcot emerged out of Hyderabad state. 2. The Mysore Kingdom emerged out of Vijayanagara Empire. 3. Rohilkhand Kingdom was formed out of the territories occupied by Ahmad Shah Durrani. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre.) 2021. Nizamat of Arcot was established by Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb and was the legal dependency of the Nizam of Hyderabad, it did not emerge from the Hyderabad state. Hence, statement 1 is not correct. Mysore kingdom emerged as a powerful state under the Wodeyar dynasty, which initially served as a vassal of the Vijayanagar empire. Hence statement 2 is correct. Ali Muhammad Khan took advantage of the collapse of authority in north India following Nadir Shah's invasion (1739 A.D.), to set up a petty kingdom, Rohilkhand. Ahmad Shah Durrani started invading India in 1748 A.D. Hence, statement 3 is not correct.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: Among the following who had constructed an astronomical observatory popularly known as Jantar- Mantar in Delhi?
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2005. Jai Singh- II constructed an astronomical observatory Jantar Mantar in Delhi. Rajput King of Amber’s Kachhwaha, Jai Singh had an interest in Astronomy. He established observatories in Ujjain, Mathura, Varanasi, Jaipur also besides Delhi.]

Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.q: The book’ Jiz Muhammad Shahi’ related to knowledge of Astrology produced in 1773 is written by :
Disintegration of the Mughal Empire.explanation: [R.A.S./R.T.S.(Pre) 2007. Sawai Jai Singh (Jai Singh II) of Amber was a great Rajput king of the 18th century. He established "Jaipur" city and made it a centre of science and art. He was a great renowned astronomer. He constructed well-equipped observatories in Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Mathura and Varanasi. He prepared a set of chart named Jiz Muhammad Shahi for ease in astronomical observation journals. He conducted Euclid's "Geometry" in Sanskrit. He conducted two Ashwamedh sacrifi ces during his reign.]

III. Modern History of India The Advent.q: In which year Vasco-da-Gama arrived at Calicut ?
III. Modern History of India The Advent.explanation: [Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2004. Vasco da Gama arrived at western coast port of Calicut on May 20, 1498 A.D. He discovered a new and alternative sea route to India and he was welcomed by Zamorin (Zamorin was the ancestral title of the rulers of Calicut), the then king of Calicut. The voyage of Vasco da Gama opened the new trade dimensions of the Indo-Portuguese (Europe) alliance. Vasco da Gama earned 60 times more profi t as compared to the cost of expeditions in Europe from black pepper trade with India, which encouraged other Portuguese traders. The Portuguese merchants established their commercial fi rms in India at the ports of Calicut, Goa, Daman, Diu and Hooghly. Francisco de Almeida came to India in 1505 AD as the first Portuguese Viceroy. The ‘Blue Water’ policy is attributed to Francisco de Almeida, the first Viceroy of Portuguese possessions in India. According to Blue water policy, “The Portuguese should be the sole trade power in the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean”. Portugese were the first to build trade relation with India, among the European nations, who came by discovering new sea route to India. Albuquerque came to India in 1509 A.D. after him, as a new Viceroy. He annexed Goa in 1510 A.D.from Bijapur Adilshahi Sultanate. The Portuguese maintained Goa as the epicentre of their culture and entity.]

(ii) In his first trip Vasco da Gama stayed for approximately one year in India. (iii) Vasco Da gama revisited India in 1501.
III. Modern History of India The Advent.explanation: [Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2022. In 1498, Vasco da Gama reached Calicut. At that time, Calicut was ruled by Zamorin (Samuthiri), who welcomed Vasco da Gama. He stayed in India for about three months and returned to Portugal with ships loaded with Indian goods. Vasco da Gama revisited India in 1502 A.D. and 1524 A.D. The Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission has identifi ed option (c) at the correct one in its model answer key.]

The Columbus, a traveler originally from Italy and fi nanced by Spain discovered America, while Holland voyager Tasman explored Van Diemen’s land (now Tasmania) and New Zealand. The first European to reach Australia was English navigator Willem Janszoon (1712-1780), while the British Navigator Captain Cook arrived at Australia in 1770 A.D. III. Modern History of India The Advent.q: Who were the first Europeans to come to India for trade?
III. Modern History of India The Advent.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2007, U.P. P.C.S. (Spl.) (Mains) 2004, U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2000, U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1993, U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1990. The Portuguese were the first Europeans, who came to India during medieval period for trade. The first Portuguese and European voyager Vasco da Gama reached the coast of Calicut in 1498 AD after a long voyage with the help of a Gujarati route guide. The sequence of the arrival of the European trade powers in India is as follows: Portuguese, the Dutch, the English, the Danes and French. Portuguese came to India in 1498 and returned in 1961 (longest period).]

III. Modern History of India The Advent.q: Who was the real founder of Portuguese power in India?
III. Modern History of India The Advent.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2003. The real founder of Portuguese power in India was Albuquerque (1509-15 A.D.). He established Portuguese State as a powerful regional power in India. The annexation of Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur in November, 1510 was the first signifi cant achievement of Albuquerque. The victory at Goa consolidated the Portuguese monopoly on the southern-western naval coast and established a regional Portuguese State in India. He encouraged Portuguese men to marry Indian women for enhancement of the Portuguese presence in India and the formation of permanent colonies.]

III. Modern History of India The Advent.q: With reference to the entry of European powers into India, which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: (b) The English opened their first factory in South India at Masulipatnam
(c) In Eastern India, the English company opened its first factory in Orissa in 1633
(d) Under the leadership of Dupleix, the French occupied Madras in 1746

III. Modern History of India The Advent.q: Who were the first Europeans to set up sea trade centres in India?
III. Modern History of India The Advent.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2004. Among all European powers in India, the Portuguese traders were the first to establish maritime trade centers in India. The first Portuguese Viceroy Francisco de Almeida annexed Diu in 1509 A.D. The victory of Diu made Portuguese most powerful in the Indian Ocean. During the battle of Diu in 1509 A.D. Portugese defeated the combined forces of Mamluk sultanate of Egypt, Gujarat sultanate (at western coast) and Zamorin of Calicut. The Portuguese established their monopoly over the Indian Ocean and levied a tax on ships passing through their area.]
III. Modern History of India The Advent.topic: III. Modern History of India The Advent of European Companies

III. Modern History of India The Advent.q: Among the following factories in Bengal, the one established by the Portuguese was :
III. Modern History of India The Advent.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2004. In 1579 A.D., after receiving permission from the Mughal Emperor Akbar, Portuguese in Bengal laid the foundation for their settlements in Hooghly. They built forts and warehouses along the banks of River Hooghly. This led to the town of Hooghly, near Chuchchada, emerging as a major European trading center. In 1599 A.D., as the Portuguese settlements in Chuchesra Hooghly increased, the Portuguese arrived in the area of Bandel (Presently located in Hooghly district of West Bengal state), where they also established a Chruch named as ‘Bandel Church’ (also named as Basilica of Holy - Hojri). In 1535 A.D. Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah, the ruler of Bengal, promised the portugese to establish the forts in Chittagong and Satgaon, in return for their assistance of the ruler during the Sher Shah Suri’s invasion of Bengal. After that, Portuguese colonies were set up through Bengal. Chatgaon, known as the great port of Portuguese maritime, was used by them but in the 16th century Satgaon declined and was replaced by Hooghly. Dutch built a fort named Fort Gustavus in Chinsurah. Shrirampur was a major centre of Danes. Therefore, Hooghly and Bandel, under the Hooghly itself, both were the important major trade centre for Portuguese.]

The Britishers also occupied Pondicherry in 1793 but handed it over to France in 1814 as per the Treaty of Paris. Thus, only statement (1) is correct.]

III. Modern History of India The Advent.q: With reference to the Captain Hawkins, which of the following statements is correct? (1) He came to India in 1611 as an envoy of James-I. (2) He was very well versed in Turkish language.
III. Modern History of India The Advent.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2023. William Hawkins sailed from the East India Company’s ship and reached to Surat in 1608 A.D. from Hector. After initial resistance from Portuguese, Hawkins arrived at the Mughal Court of Jahangir in Agra in April, 1609 A.D. Hawkins arrived at the Mughal Court with a letter signed by King James I of England, having introduction about Hawkins and the request of Mughal emperor’s favourable treatment for British traders. Therefore, Hawkins mission was a combination fo both, an imperial embassy and a commercial endeavour. He was sent by company, but with the credentials from the King, which made him representative of both– the King and the company, in the eyes of Mughal court. Hawkins was a good speaker of Turkish language. Jahangir was impressed by his knowledge of Turkish language and bestowed Hawkins, with the title of ‘English Khan’. Jahangir also granted Hawkins a mansab of 400. Therefore, statement (I) is false and the statement (II) is true.]

The British Commodore Bernett captured some French ships which became the immediate cause of the war. Nawab Anwaruddin sent an army under the command of Mahfooz Khan to besiege the French in Madras during the first Carnatic War. The French Army (under the command of Captain Paradise) defeated Nawab’s Army at the Battle of St. Thome near Adyar river. Treaty of Aix-La-Chapelle (18 Oct, 1748 A.D.) ended the War of Austrian succession and with it first Carnatic War ended and the Britishers reoccupied Madras. The first Carnatic War is memorable for the War of St. Thome.]

III. Modern History of India The Advent.explanation: [70th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2024. The triangular trade between India, China, and England in the 18th and 19th centuries was centered on opium. The British East India Company established their monopoly in the cultivation of opium in the region of Bengal and Bihar etc., they forced the farmers to cultivate opium and exported it to China, where it was in high demand despite government bans. Profi ts from the opium trade were used to purchase Chinese goods like tea, silk, and porcelain for England, while manufactured goods from England were exported to India, completing the trade cycle. This exploitative system had severe social and economic consequences, including the Opium Wars between Britain and China. While commodities like silk and black pepper were also traded, opium was the chief economic foundation of this triangular commerce.]

East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2010. On 23 June 1757 AD, the troops of the British East India Company led by Robert Clive defeated Nawab of Bengal Sirajuddaula, in the historic Battle of Plassey.]

East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.q: Which of the following shifted his capital from Murshidabad to Munger?
East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2005, U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2003. Mir Qasim was the most effi cient successor among the successors of Nawab Alivardi Khan. He demonstrated his capability as Fauzdar of Poornia and Rangpur. He transferred his capital from Murshidabad to Munger. The reason was to secure himself from constant interference from Calcutta and intrigues of Murshidabad. He organized his Army on the European model. He managed the factory of arms and ammunition at Munger for manufacturing of tanks and matchlock guns. Besides, Mir Qasim had made efforts to reform state’s fi nancial condition.]

East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.q: The most decisive battle that led to the establishment of supremacy of the British in India was :
East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S.(Pre) 2003, U.P. U.D.A./ L.D.A. (Pre) 2002, U.P.P.C.S.(Pre) 1990. On 22/23 October, 1764 A.D. British Army defeated allied forces of Mir Qasim, Nawab of Oudh Shuja-ud-Daula and Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. British Army’s command was in the hands of Major Hector Munro in the Battle of Buxar. The battle of Buxar assured the result of Plassey battle and established British supremacy on Banaras and Allahabad (Prayagraj) across the Ganges. The battle of Buxar made way for British and proved that there was no strong competitor before the British. The battle of Buxar completed what Plassey had begun. During the battle of Buxar Nawab of Bengal was Mir Jafar. According to Sir James Stephen, ‘’The battle of Buxar deserves more credit than the battle of Plassey as the origin of British power in India”. If the results of both signifi cant battles are analyzed, it can be said that the battle of Plassey was won by treachery, but the battle of Buxar showed the supremacy of English armies and military skills. Plassey made the English the only controllers of Bengal while Buxar raised the political prestige of the Company throughout India.]

East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.q: Which one of the following rulers had granted Diwani to the East India Company?
East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.explanation: [U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2006, U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2003. As per the first Treaty of Allahabad (August 1765 A.D.), the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II was taken under the Company’s protection and was to reside at Allahabad. The Emperor issued an order dated 12th August, 1765 granting Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. During this time Robert Clive was Governor of East India Company in Bengal. The emperor’s order legalized the political authority of Company in Bengal and British rule expanded all over India including Delhi. Successors of Shah Alam II i.e. Akbar II (1806-37 A.D.) and Bahadurshah II (1837-57 A.D.) became pensioners of East India Company.]

East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.q: Who was appointed Deputy Diwan of Murshidabad by Robert Clive after the Allahabad Treaty?
East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.explanation: [45th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2001. According to the Treaty of Allahabad (August, 1765 A.D.), Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II was taken under the Company’s protection and had to reside at Allahabad. Shah Alam II conferred Diwani (fi scal revenue collection authority) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the Company by issuing ‘Farman’ on 12 August, 1765 A.D. Nazm-ud-duala (son of Mir Jafar) was accepted as Nawab of Bengal. In return, the company had to pay the emperor an annual sum of Rs 26 Lakhs as pension. At that time, the Company was neither interested in taking responsibility for tax revenue collection nor was it capable of doing so. Therefore, the Company appointed two Diwans- Mohammad Raza Khan for Bengal and Raja Shitab Rai for Bihar. Thus, all business of Diwani and Nizamat was conducted by Indians but authorized by the British Company.]

East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.q: With reference to the Hindu Nayab Wazirs of Oudh Sultanate, which of the following statements(s) is/are correct? 1. East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.explanation: [U.P.R.O. / A.R.O. (Mains) 2016. Raja Tikait Rai was Artha Mantri or diwan of Nawab Aasafudaullah of Oudh. Usually certain Hindu castes were placed in high positions in the state of Nawabs of Oudh. E.g. Arth Mantri of Nawab Aasafudaullah Raja Tikait Rai, Raja Jhaulal and Nawab Safdar Jung appointed Raja Naval Rai as ‘Bakshi’ and ‘Deputy Governor of Bengal’. Hence, the option (c) is correct.]

East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.q: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the battles fought in India in the 18th Century?
options: (a) Battle of Wandiwash - Battle of Buxar - Battle of Ambur- Battle of Plassey
(b) Battle of Ambur - Battle of Plassey - Battle of Wandiwash - Battle of Buxar
(c) Battle of Wandiwash - Battle of Plassey - Battle of Ambur-Battle of Buxar.
(d) Battle of Ambur - Battle of Buxar - Battle of Wandiwash-Battle of Plassey.
East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2005. Battle of Ambur (August, 1749 A.D.):- The combined armies of Muzaffar Jung, Chanda Sahib and the French defeated and Killed Anwar-ud-din at the Battle of Ambur near Bellore in August, 1749. Muzaffar Jung became the Subedar of Deccan. Duplex was appointed Governor of all the Mughal territories south of the river Krishna. The Nizam surrendered some districts in the Northern Circars to the French. A French army under Bussy was stationed in Hyderabad. Battle of Plassey (June, 1757 A.D.):- Fought between Nawab of Bengal Sirajuddaula and the British Army. Bengal was in control of the British after Plassey. Mir Jafar was placed on the throne by Robert Clive. In exchange, Mir Jafar ceded an area of the south of Calcutta known as 24 Pargana to the British for their services and gifted 2,34,000 pounds to Clive as personal gift reward. Battle of Wandiwash (January, 1760 A.D.) :- It occurred between French and British. French were defeated by the British. Sir Eyre Coote was the leader of the British Army while French troops were led by Count de Lally. Battle of Buxar (October, 1764 A.D.) :- Fought between allied forces of Mir Qasim, Shujauddaula, Shah Alam II and the British. British led by Hector Munro defeated the allied forces badly. Thus, option (b) will be the correct answer.]

East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.q: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
options: (a) Battle of Buxar – Mir Jafar Vs. Clive
(b) Battle of Wandiwash – French Vs. East India Company
(c) Battle of Chillianwala – Dalhousie Vs. Marathas
(d) Battle of Khurda – Nizam Vs. East India Company
East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1995. Battle of Buxar (October, 1764 A.D.), was fought between Allied Forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II, and British force. British force led by Hector Munro defeated the Allied forces badly. The battle of Buxar is regarded as the first decisive military success of the English East India Company in India. Battle of Wandiwash was fought between French and East India Company in 1760 A.D. By this defeat, the power of French in India came to an end. Battle of Chillianwala was fought on 13 January 1849 A.D. Lord Gough commanded the British Army, and the Sikh army was under the command of Sher Singh. The battle ended undecided. Lord Dalhousie was the Governor-General of India at the time of the battle. Battle of Khurda/Kharda (1795 A.D.) was fought by Marathas against Nizam in which Nizam was defeated. Therefore, other pairs are wrong excluding option (b).]

East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.q: Which of the following opposed British in India vigorously?
East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1993. Marathas opposed the British vigorously in India. Maratha were suppressed after three Anglo-Maratha Wars. On the ruins of Mughal Empire, Maratha laid down their foundation and British also took advantage of these circumstances. British lost first Anglo-Maratha war badly and this war ended with the Treaty of Salbai. Lord Wellesley trapped Peshwa in the cage of Subsidiary Alliance in 1802. Lord Hastings established British supremacy after the devastation of remnant strength of Marathas in 1818.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2004. Ranjit Singh was born on 13 November, 1780 in the home of Maha Singh, the chief of Sukerchakia Misl. On 25th April 1809, the treaty of Amritsar took place between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and British. The terms of the treaty prevented Singh from any further territorial expansion south of the Sutlej but on the other hand, as Cunningham said, Ranjit Singh occupied authority to spread kingdom in the West. He annexed Multan (1818), Kashmir (1819) and Peshawar Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (1834). Thus, among given options, Sri Nagar was included in the kingdom of Ranjit Singh.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre.) 2021. Maharaja Ranjit Singh set up the Adalat-i-Ala at Lahore which heard appeals from the district and provincial courts.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: The Treaty of Amritsar was concluded between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2023. Treaty of Amritsar was signed by Mr. Charles Metcalfe on behalf of British Governor general Lord Minto I and Maharaja Ranjit Singh at Amritsar on April 25, 1809 AD. According to this treaty, Ranjit Singh was to recognize the river Sutlej as the boundary and to accept the British suzerainty over his vassals across the river, and the English were to recognize the Maharaja as the sole sovereign on his side of River Sutlej.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Ranjeet Singh got famous Kohinoor diamond from
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [41st B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1996. Punjab was part of Ahmad Shah Abdali’s territory, but in 1772 A.D. after his death, most of the area of his empire was occupied by Sikh misls leaving Multan, Kashmir and some other smaller regions. Ranjit Singh got the opportunity to consolidate his empire as Afghans were engaged in internal fi ghts. In 1803 AD, Shah Shuja (the grandson of Ahmad Shah Abdali) sat on the throne of Kabul but Shah Mahmud (brother of Shah Shuja) along with powerful Barekzay chieftain Fateh Khan and Dost Muhammad dethroned him and occupied Kashmir and Peshawar. On that occasion, Shah Shuja asked Ranjeet Singh for help and presented him with the Kohinoor diamond.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Who among the following has said, ‘God intended me to look upon all religions with one eye, that is why he took away the light from the other’?
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2007. The above statement was made by Maharaja Ranjit Singh. Ranjit Singh was born on 13 Nov. 1780 A.D. at Gujranwala. When he was only 12 years old, his father Maha Singh died. A council of regency governed administration from 1792 A.D. to 1797 A.D. which included his mother, mother-in-Law and Diwan Lakhpat Rai. He assumed the powers directly in 1797. Ranjit Singh annexed Lahore (1799 A.D.), Amritsar (1802 A.D.).]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in the context of the Treaty of Lahore (1846)? I. The Maharaja left all his territories beyond the river Satluj forever. II. The Maharaja left his rights over all the forts between the Satluj and Beas rivers in favour of the Company. III. The English army could no longer pass through the Sikh State. Select the correct answer from the codes given below :
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P. R.O/A.R.O (Re. Exam) (Pre) 2025. The British army occupied Lahore and in March 1846, forced the Sikhs to sign the Treaty of Lahore with following terms –– The Maharaja, ceded all his territories across the Sutlej river forever. – Maharaja completely relinquished his control over all the forts situated between Sutlej & Beas Rivers in favour of company.– They promised not to interfere in the administration.– The Sikhs were required to pay one and a half crore ruppes as war indemnity etc.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: The successor of Maharaja Ranjit Singh was :
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2003. Khadag Singh (Kharak Singh) ascended the throne after the death of Ranjit Singh in 1839 A.D.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Who was the last King of Sikh empire?
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2013. Maharaja Duleep Singh was the last king of Sikh empire. He reigned from 1843 to 1849 A.D.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Who was last king of Sikh empire?
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2010. See the explanation of the above question.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Which one of the following statements is correct about Dalip Singh, the ex-Maharaja of Punjab?
options: (a) He died in Paris on 23 October, 1893
(c) He never renounced the Sikh faith.
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2013. Former King of Punjab, Maharaja Duleep Singh died in Paris (France) on 22 October or from some sources 23 October, 1893. Remaining all statements are false. He accepted Christianity in 1853 A.D. but later in 1886 A.D. he was re converted into Sikh religion. He also visited to Russia. He was cremated in England.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Regarding Punjab Merger, which of the following statement is false?
options: (a) On 29th March, 1849, the Governor General announced that the state of Punjab had come to an end.
(b) All the territories of Maharaja Duleep SIngh became part of the Indian British Empire.
(c) Duleep Singh was given an annual pension of Rs. 2,50,000.
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2023. By Lord Dalhousie's proclamation of March 29, 1849 A.D., the whole of Punjab was merged into the British Empire. All the territories of Maharaja Duleep Singh became part of the Indian British Empire and he was exiled to England in 1854 for study. For his relatives and also the maintenance of states’ employees, his pension was decided not less than four lakh rupees and not more than fi ve lakh rupees (minimum £40,000 and maximum £50,000) per annum.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Who among the following was not a member of ‘Board of Three’ to administer the State of Punjab after its annexation?
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2013. Lord Dalhousie appointed a set of triumvirs (Board of Three) to manage affairs in Punjab after its annexation in 1849 A.D. in which Henry Lawrence was named as President; John Lawrence and Charles Grenville Mansel were included as members of the council. H.M. Elliot and Robert Montgomery were not part of this council.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Who emerged victorious in the first Anglo-Mysore War (1767-69)?
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2015. First Anglo-Mysore War (1767-69 A.D.) was fought between British and Haidar Ali. He fought bravely and captured Mangalore in 1768 and reached Madras in 1769, where English in helplessness had to sign the “Treaty of Madras’ in April 1769 on the conditions of Haidar Ali.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Who among the following established a modern armoury in Dindigul Mysore in 1755?
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2020. In 1742 A.D., Mysore army under Venkata Raya's leadership conquered Dindigul. There were eighteen Palayams (Pallayakkars) during his reign and all these Palayams were under Dindigul Semai with Dindiguls capitals. These Palayams wanted to be independent & refused to pay taxes to Venkata Raja. In 1755 A.D., Mysore king sent Haidar Ali to Dindigul to handle the situation. Haidar Ali controlled Dindigul and became de-facto ruler & converted this fort into sepoy post. Later on he became the ruler of Mysore. In 1777, Haidar Ali appointed Purshana Mir Saheb as governor of Dindigul.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: British general who defeated/beat Haidar Ali in War of Porto Novo :
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2003. Before this war, Haidar Ali made a front against the British with the Marathas and Nizam. In July 1780, Haidar Ali attacked Carnatic and on 10 September 1780 Colonel Baillie was defeated by the combined forces of Haidar Ali and Tipu in the Battle of Pollilur. The British segregated Nizam and Marathas from Haidar. Haidar Ali faced this complex situation fi rmly. Haidar Ali fought with General Eyre Coote in 1781 during the second Anglo-Mysore War, and British defeated Haidar Ali in War of Porto Novo (1st July, 1781)]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Tipu Sultan set up his capital at
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [38th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1992. Tipu Sultan set up his Capital at Srirangapatna and became member of ‘Jacobin Club’ (it was founded by France offi cials, as a branch of Jacobian club of France) and also planted “the tree of liberty” as a symbol of the alliance between France and Mysore in Srirangapatna. He sent his delegates for maintaining fruitful relations with contemporary foreign states and getting help against the British. He established embassies in foreign countries on the modern line.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Who among the following Indian rulers established embassies in foreign countries on modern lines?
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2001, U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2011. Tipu Sultan established embassies in Iran, Istanbul, Afghanistan, France etc. on modern lines.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Tipu Sultan defeated the British Army in 1780 at
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2009. Siege of Arcot was done in 1780 A.D. by Haidar Ali. After that, a British Army led by Co. William Baillie was defeated at Pollilur.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Englishmen made the Treaty of Srirangapatna with
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [42nd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1997. Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92 A.D.) ended with the Treaty of Srirangapatna (1792 A.D.). The treaty of Seringapatam (Srirangapatna) was signed in March 1792 A.D. between Tipu Sultan of Mysore and Lord Cornwallis on behalf of British East India Company. The agreement also included representative of the Nizam of Hyderabad and Maratha Empire, requiring Tipu to Cede half of his Kingdom. According to the treaty, Half of the territories of Tipu were snatched away from him and divided among Marathas, British, and Nizam. Tipu had to pay Rs. 330 lakhs as war indemnity to British as his two sons were kept hostage. These was a terms and condition in the treaty that until Tipu wouldn’t provide 3 crore rupees, his two sons will be under British protection.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: When did Tipu Sultan die at war with the British?
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [M.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2000. The fourth and fi nal war was fought between British and Mysore in 1799 A.D. which ended the glorious history of Mysore, Srirangapatna was captured and Tipu was killed in its defence.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Which of the following is correctly matched?
options: (a) First Anglo-Mysore War - Haidar Ali was defeated
(b) Second Anglo-Mysore War - Haidar Ali defeated the British
(c) Third Anglo-Mysore War - Tipu Sultan won the battle and did not cede his territory to British.
(d) Fourth Anglo-Mysore War -Tipu was defeated and was killed in the thick of battle
Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2014. (i) First Anglo-Mysore War was held in 1767-1769 A.D. and ended with Treaty of Madras on 4 April, 1769 AD. British Governor of Bengal was Harry Verelst during the war. (ii) Second Anglo-Mysore War was fought in 1780-1784 A.D. and ended with the Treaty of Mangalore. Warren Hastings was the British Governor-General during the war. (iii) Third Anglo-Mysore War occurred in 1790-92 A.D. under commands of Lord Cornwallis and ended with Treaty of Srirangapatna. Tipu requested support from Kustuntunia and France by sending his ambassador but his effort was worthless. (iv) 4th Anglo-Mysore War was fought in 1799 A.D., led by Governor General Lord Wellesley. On 4 May 1799, British annexed Srirangapatna Fort and Tipu got martyrdom in the battle. Family members of Tipu were imprisoned in Vellore.]

Regional States : Punjab and Mysore.q: Which one of the statements is not correct?
options: (a) Ali Mardan Khan introduced the system of revenue farming in Bengal
(b) Maharaja Ranjit Singh set up modern foundries to manufacture cannons at Lahore

Tipu Sultan provided money for the construction of the idol of Goddess Sharda in Shringeri temple. Credit for introducing revenue farming in Bengal goes to Murshid Kuli Khan, not Ali Mardan Khan.]

Tipu Sultan was killed in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War in 1799 A.D. During the war of Plassey (1757 A.D.), Mir Jafar conspired against Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah supporting Britishers.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Robert Clive was the first Governor-General of Bengal. 2. William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2007. Under Regulating Act, 1773 the British parliament provided the system of colonialist government in Bengal. The government consisted of a Governor-General and four members (four chancellors). Warren Hastings was appointed as the first Governor-General of Bengal. Thus statement 1 is incorrect. Charter Act of 1833 was an attempt by the British government to centralize the Indian administration. The Governor-General of Bengal was made Governor-General of India by this Act. Lord William Bentinck was appointed as the first Governor-General of India. Thus, statement 2 is correct.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Which one of the following statements is not true?
options: (a) The foundation of the system of civil administration, was fi rmly laid down by Warren Hastings on which the superstructure was raised by Cornwallis.
(b) Clive was responsible for reforming the East India Company’s Civil and Military Services.
(c) Lord William Bentinck was one of the greatest British rulers as he consolidated the British Empire in India
(d) Lord Dalhousie added rich semitones to the British Empire on the basis of the Doctrine of Lapse.
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P.P.S.C. (GIC) 2010. Clive led both civilian and military reforms. Under civil reforms, he banned gifts and private businesses. He made internal tax compulsory. Under military reforms, he ordered to ban dual allowance system (double batta for european offi cers). From 1766 A.D. it was given only to those soldiers who worked outside the borders of Bihar and Bengal (except Allahabad). The foundation of the system of civil administration was fi rmly laid down by Warren Hastings which was outlined by Cornwallis. His rule lasted from 1786 A.D. to 1793 A.D. and from 30 July, 1805 A.D. to 5 October, 1805 A.D. remembered for two events, the introduction of the permanent settlement into Bengal and the Third Mysore War. Lord Dalhousie (1848-56 A.D.) merged Satara in 1848, Jaitpur and Sambalpur in 1849, Bhagat in 1850, Udaipur in 1852, Jhansi in 1853 and Nagpur in 1854 under the doctrine of Lapse. Lord Dalhousie placed Awadh under British Rule in 1856 on the ground of alleged misgovernance.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Who was the founder of Empire in India?
options: (e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [66th B.P.S.C. Re-Exam (Pre) 2020. Robert Clive is widely considered as the founder of British India. He arrived in Madras as a clerk for East India Company in 1744 AD. Through his leadership he was able to consolidate company's commercial & territorial position in India. In 1757 A.D. company troops defeated nawab of Bengal in Plassey which led to creation of British Raj in India.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Who led the 'Banaras Rebellion' against the Britishers?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2021. The Banaras Rebellion was led by Raja Chet Singh in 1781 AD. In this rebellion, the Governor General Warren Hastings ran away with his soldiers and took refuge in Chunar Fort.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: At the time of the establishment of Asiatic Society in Calcutta, who was the Governor-General of Bengal?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P.P.S.C. (R.I.) 2014. Warren Hastings was the Governor-General of Bengal at the time of the establishment of Asiatic Society on 15 January, 1784 A.D. in Calcutta.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: The policy of ‘Security cell’ is related with
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2006. The policy of ‘Security Cell” is related to Warren Hastings and Wellesley. Warren Hastings fought with Mysore and Marathas to achieve status equivalent to other Indian states. During this time the company tried to form buffer state (also known as Ring Fence) with an aim to protect its state from Afghans and Marathas. Thus, they agreed to protect Oudh on the condition that the Nawab of Oudh would bear the expenses. The main aim of Wellesley was to enforce Indian states to rely on his army power. The British policies towards Indian states were 1. Company’s struggle for equality with Indian provinces. (1740-1765 AD) 2. ‘Security cell’ or the policy of siege. (1765-1813 AD) 3. Subordinate separation policy. (1813-1857 AD) 4. Subordinate union policy. (1858-1935 AD) 5. The policy of equal union. (1935-1947 AD)]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: ‘Ring Fence’ policy is associated with
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2013. See the explanation of the above question.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Who among the following abolished ‘Dual Government’ system in Bengal?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [41st B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1996, 47th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2005. The court of directors took the decision in 1772 A.D. to abolish the dual government system during the tenure of Warren Hastings and ordered council of Calcutta and its chiefs to serve as Diwan and offi ciate the administration of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa. Warren Hastings dismissed both the deputy Diwans Muhammad Raza Khan and Raja Shitab Roy.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: The dual system of governance in Bengal was enforced by :
options: (e) None of the above/ More than one of the above
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [66th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2020. Dual system of governance in Bengal was enforced by Robert Clive in 1765. Under this system, the administration of Bengal was divided into Diwani and Nizamat.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Which Governor- General was prosecuted for impeachment?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [M.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1992. Warren Hastings was prosecuted from 1788 to 1795 A.D. for impeachment for unjust and arbitrary functions, but British parliament dropped all the charges against him after considering his service. It was said that Warren Hastings had done all this for the benefi t of the empire.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Who among the following was prosecuted for impeachment by the British Parliament?

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Who established the judicial organization in India?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1991. Lord Cornwallis introduced criminal and judicial regulations to a signifi cant degree which is still underpins the Indian Judicial system. Cornwallis gave limited judicial powers to the company’s revenue collectors, who already served as civil magistrates. In 1790 AD the company took over the administration of justice from Nawab and Cornwallis introduced a system of circuit courts with a superior court that met in Calcutta and had the power of review over the circuit court decision.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Who among the following Governor-Generals created the Covenanted Civil Service of India which later came to be known as the Indian Civil Service?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2010. Cornwallis reformed and reorganised Civil Services in India. After becoming the Governor-General of Bengal, Cornwallis restructured the administration and abolished the revenue boards and laid down new laws for them. He introduced new policies regarding the personal business of British offi cers. He exclusively divided the jurisdiction of civil and judicial administration through “Cornwallis code” which later, in turn, transformed into civil services in India.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2004. See the explanation of the above question.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: In the second half of 18th century, who was often called the local representative of "Aura and Authority of Company Bahadur"?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2021. In 1793 A.D., Lord Cornwallis separated the landlords from their police duties and established a police station in every twenty to thirty square miles and appointed a police offi cer called Daroga. The appointment and supervision of the Daroga were done by the Magistrate. The farmer regarded the Daroga as the local representative of "The Pride of Company Bahadur".]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: The Tomb of Lord Cornwallis is situated at
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011. Lord Cornwallis was the Governor-General of Bengal during 1786-1793 A.D. and from July 30, 1805 A.D. to October 5, 1805 A.D.. He is known for Istamarari or permanent settlement, judicial code and as promoter of Indian administration services. He died on October 5, 1805 A.D. at Ghazipur. His grave is situated at Ghazipur (U.P.).]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Which one of the following statements does not apply to the system of Subsidiary Alliance introduced by Lord Wellesley?
options: (a) To maintain a large standing army at other’s expense
(b) To keep India safe from Napoleonic danger
(c) To secure a fi xed income for the company
(d) To establish British paramountcy over the Indian States
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2018. Governor-General Lord Wellesley came to India in 1798 A.D. at a time when the British were locked in a life and death struggle with France all over the world. The fear of Napoleon haunted the Britishers everywhere. To achieve his political aims, Wellesley relied on the system of Subsidiary Alliance. While the practice of helping Indian rulers with a paid British force was quite old, it was given shape by Wellesley who used it to sub-ordinate the Indian states to the paramountcy of the company. Under the subsidiary Alliance system, the ruler of the allying state was compelled to accept the permanent stationing of a British force within his territory and to pay a subsidy for its maintenance. However, to secure a fi xed income for the company was not under the agenda of the Subsidiary Alliance.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: First Maratha Sardar to accept the subsidiary alliance of Lord Wellesley was
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [41st B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1996. The subsidiary alliance system was introduced in India by Lord Wellesley. The Nizam of Hyderabad was the first to enter into such an alliance. Maratha ruler Bajirao II (1802 A.D.) also accepted a subsidiary alliance. Several states like Hyderabad (1798 A.D.), Tanjore and Mysore (1799 A.D.), Awadh (1801 A.D.), Bhonsle (1803), Sindhiya (1804 A.D.), Holkar (1818 A.D.) etc. adopted this system.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Between whom was the ‘Treaty of Bassein signed in 1802?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2012. The Treaty of Bassein (Now called Vasai) was a pact signed on December 31, 1802 A.D. between the English East India Company and Bajirao II, the Maratha Peshwa of Pune (Poona) in India after the Battle of Poona. In this treaty, Bajirao-II was restored as Peshwa in Pune with around 6 thousand English forces were permanently stationed with the Peshwa to protect him for which 26 lakh was to be paid to East India Company.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: The first Indian ruler who joined the Subsidiary Alliance was
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1994. Lord Wellesley (1798-1805) cleverly used a subsidiary alliance as a tool to make Indian provinces puppets of Britishers. He did not discover this method. This method was in practice earlier also but it gradually evolved and the fi nal shape was provided by Wellesley. Dupleix was the first European to give his army to an Indian ruler on the promise of a fi xed payment to the Company. Britishers used these tactics too. First Subsidiary Alliance was signed in 1765 with Awadh where Company promised to protect the boundaries of Awadh on a fi xed payment to the Company. Note : Hyderabad will be the answer if it is asked first state to join Wellesley's subsidiary alliance.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Subsidiary Alliance was implemented during the reign of

The states to adopt the subsidiary alliance of Lord Wellesley were- Hyderabad (1798 A.D. and 1800), Mysore (1799 A.D.), Tanjore (1799 A.D.), Awadh (1801 A.D.), Peshwa (1802 A.D.), Bhonsle of Barar (1803 A.D.), Sindhiya (Scindia) (1804 A.D.), Holkar (1818 A.D.), Jodhpur, Jaipur, Machheri, Bundi and Bharatpur etc.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2016. He also adopted a policy of non-intervention in the princely state but later adopted the policy of Subsidiary Alliance. The Nizam of Hyderabad was the first to enter into such an alliance.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: At a time when empires in Europe were crumbling before the might of Napoleon, which one of the following Governors-General kept the British fl ag fl ying high in India?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1999. Lord Wellesley moved to India in 1797 A.D., which was the darkest period of British history. The front made of European powers against France had been disbanded. Napoleon had conquered Egypt and Syria and was seriously thinking about attacking India. In that condition, Lord Wellesley used a subsidiary alliance in India, which helped him to establish the sovereignty of the British power and the fear of Napoleon was averted.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Anglo-Nepal War took place during the reign of
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2010. The Anglo-Nepal (1814-16 A.D.) War took place during the reign of Lord Hastings which came to an end by the Treaty of Sugauli. Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Which of the following sites were obtained by the British East India Company under the Treaty of Sugauli in 1816 ? 1. Kathmandu 2. Shimla 3. Ranikhet 4. Nainital Select the correct answer from the code given below : Code :
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S (Pre) 2025. As a result of the Treaty of Sugauli (1816), Nepal ceded to the British East India Company Kumaon, the eastern part of Garhwal, and some parts of the Terai. The areas included in Kumaon came under British rule. Kathmandu: It remained the capital of Nepal; the treaty only provided for the appointment of a British Resident. Kathmandu was not handed over to the British. Shimla: British control was established over the hill tract in which Shimla is located; however, the actual transfer of land for the “Shimla station/town” took place in 1830 from Keonthal/Patiala. Ranikhet: Ranikhet is located in the Kumaon region (present-day Uttarakhand). After the Treaty of Sugauli, Kumaon came under British control. Nainital: Nainital is also a part of Kumaon; once Kumaon came under British rule, this area too came under Company administration.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Third Anglo-Maratha war is related to
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2013. Third Anglo-Maratha (1817-18 A.D.) war is related to Lord Hastings.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Sir Thomas Munro was Governor of Madras during years
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2016. Sir Thomas Munro was governor of Madras during 1820 1827 A.D. He is regarded as the father of Ryotwari System in India in which the taxes of agriculture land were directly collected from the ryots (owner of the land).]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: On the basis of alleged maladministration which Governor-General had taken the administration of Mysore state?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2004, U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2003. Lord William Bentinck took charge of Governor-General in July, 1828. He made effective efforts to abolish Sati system, infanticide and established peace in the country by ending the social evils. According to the wishes of the ‘Court of Directors,’ he adopted the policy of neutrality towards the Indian States. The chaos took such an ugly turn in Jaipur that there was an attack on British residents. But Lord Bentinck did not accept to interfere in that. Like this, he did not accept to interfere in Jodhpur, Bundi, Kota and Bhopal because of certain reasons. Excluding this policy, he annexed Mysore in 1831 A.D., State of Kurg (1834 A.D.), Kachhar in 1832 A.D.and Jayantia in 1835 A.D. because there was too much chaos in those states.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Who among the following Governor Generals of Bengal was associated with Third Anglo-Mysore War?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2013. Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-1792 A.D.) is associated with Lord Cornwallis. Cornwallis himself took charge of the army in this war. Tipu Sultan had made the treaty of Srirangapatna (1792 A.D.) in this war under which he had to give up almost half of his state.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Who among the following was associated with suppression of thugs?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1997. The thugs included the followers of both Hindu and Muslim religions. They used to worship Kali, Durga or Bhavani. They used to cut the head and offer it as a sacrifi ce in the feet of the goddess. Lord William Bentinck appointed Captain Sleeman to take action against these thugs. He arrested 1562 thugs between 1826 and 1835 A.D.; many of them were hanged, and rest of them were banished for a lifetime. By 1837 A.D., the organized thuggery came to an end.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Under whose leadership was the suppression of Thugs achieved?
options: (e) None of the above/More than one of the above

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Which of the following were the social reforms introduced by William Bentinck? 1. Abolition of Sati 2. Abolition of slavery 3. Removal of disabilities due to change of religion 4. Suppression of the organized bands of Thugs. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below.
options: (e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [67th B.P.S.C. (Pre) (Re. Exam) 2022. Lord William Bentinck became the Governor General of Bengal presidency in 1828 A.D. In 1829 A.D., he declared the 'practice of sati' a crime and abolished it. Bentick tried to suppress thugs by running a campaign against the gang of thugs. Bentinck also worked on education and freedom of the press. In the time period of Bentinck, Charter Act, 1833 was passed which abolished slavery. In 1835 he went back to England. The provision of disqualifi cation due to change of religion was removed in 1850 A.D. Hence, statements (1), (2) and (4) are correct, so option (c) will be the answer.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Sati system was abolished by
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2012, M.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1998, M.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1993, U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1990. The meaning of Sati is ‘holy and virtuous woman.’ In Hindu rituals, the marriage is considered as Sanskar which means ‘relation of spirits.’ The Brahmins of the 18th century used to believe that if a woman became Sati, seven generations of his husband will achieve heaven. It was quite famous among highly reputed Brahmins, Kshatriya and Rajputs. Few conscious rulers of India also tried to abolish this system, Akbar was one of them. Marathas entirely abolished this system in the state. Portuguese and French also tried to abolish this system in Goa and Chandranagar respectively. It was Raja Ram Mohan Roy who started his campaign against Sati practice. The Bengal Sati Regulation, or Regulation XVII (17), A.D. 1829 of the Bengal Code was a legal act promulgated in Bengal Presidency. In 1830, this regulation was also implemented in Madras and Bombay Presidencies. Then Governor-General Lord William Bentinck which banned the practice of sati system.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Who declared 'Sati' illegal?
options: (e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [63rd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2017. See the explanation of the above question.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: In which year Sati System was abolished by William Bentinck?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2015. See the explanation of the above question.]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: ‘Hill Assembly Plan’ was set up for the development of Adivasi by

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Which of the following statements about Lord Mayo's Resolution of 1870 are correct? 1. It was the first step that bifurcated Central and Provincial fi nances. 2. Provincial Governments were empowered to administer certain services. 3. It attempted to rectify existing imparity. 4. It focused on the actual needs of the Provinces. Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [69th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2023. The Indian Council Act of 1861 implemented the strategy of legislative devolution, and the probable outcome of this was Mayo's Resolution of 1870, focusing on fi nancial decentralization. The Imperial Government, prompted by administrative effi ciency and fi nancial constraints, opted to transfer the control of certain administrative departments – including education, medical services, and roads– to provincial governments. This marked the inception of local fi nancial management. To ensure fi scal stability, provincial governments were granted the authority to rely on local taxation for balancing their budgets. Lord Mayo's resolution had delineated. "Local interest, supervision, and care are necessary to success in the management of the funds devoted to education, sanitation, medical relief, and local public works. The operation of this resolution in its full meaning and integrity will afford opportunities for the development of self-government, for strengthening municipal institutions, and for the association of Natives and Europeans to a greater extent than heretofore in the administration of affairs".]

Governor/Governor General Viceroy.q: Lord Lytton is not associated with which of the following?
Governor/Governor General Viceroy.explanation: [69th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2023. Lord Lytton was an English politician who served as the Viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880. His tenure as Viceroy was marked by a controversial policy known as the Vernacular Press Act of 1878, which aimed to regulate the Indian vernacular press and limit its freedom of expression. The policies introduced included the Indian Arms Act of 1878, according to which, it was a criminal offence for Indians to carry arms without a license. The Act was discriminatory as it did not apply to the British, Anglo-Indians, Europeans, and certain government personnel. Famine Codes were given by the Famine Commission that was set up in 1878 under the Chairmanship of Sir Richard Strachey (Strachey Commission) during the tenure of Lord Lytton only. The infamous 'Famine Codes,' have been criticized for their handling of the 1876-1878 famine in India, which resulted in signifi cant loss of life. Ilbert Bill on the other hand was introduced in 1883 by Lord Ripon that allowed Indian Judges and Magistrates to try British Offenders in criminal cases at the district level.]

The historic resolution was issued on May 18, 1882 A.D. Ripon wanted to develop the municipalities in the country. According to him, the political education of the country begins with this. Under this proposal, local boards were established in rural territories. The resolution was passed to build district sub-division, Tehsil or Taluka in every district. The municipalities were established in the cities. These institutions were given several tasks and sources of income.]

Economic Impact of British Rule on India.q: Who introduced Ist-e-Marari settlement?
Economic Impact of British Rule on India.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1991. The Permanent Settlement (1793 AD) was introduced by Lord Cornwallis. This system was launched in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Varanasi (U.P.) etc. It is also known as Istimarari Maalguzari, Bishwedari etc. The Permanent Settlement stood on the following features It recognized the landlords as the proprietors of the land. It also recognized the rights of a hereditary successor or lawful successors of the landlords. The government believed that these landlords would remain faithful to the British. The landlords were given the right to transfer or sell their land. All the rights of the landlords depended on their payment of the fi xed revenue on the fi xed date at the treasury of the government. All their rights ended if they failed to pay. This was one reason for increased litigation. An increase in intermediaries between farmers and landlords was another reason for increased litigation. The total amount of revenue to be paid by each landlord for his Zamindari was fi xed once and for all. It was agreed that the tax rate would not increase in the future.]

Economic Impact of British Rule on India.q: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R) : Assertion (A) : The British Government introduced different land revenue system in different part of India. Reason (R) : It led to create different classes in Indian peasantry. Select the correct answer from the codes given below. Codes :

(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Economic Impact of British Rule on India.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2020. British government followed different land revenue systems in different parts of India. These systems were: Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari & Mahalwari. Permanent Settlement was introduced in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha & Varanasi of U.P. Under this system around 19% area of entire British India was included. Ryotwari (approx. 51% area) system was in Madras, some parts of Mumbai, Assam, Coorg. Mahalwari (around 30% of the area) system around was in U.P, Central Province, Punjab. Hence, it is clear that because of this, different classes were created in Indian peasantry. Hence, option (a) is correct.]
