Teachings of this society are compiled in ‘Devshastra.’ The popularity of this movement ended in 1913 after Shiv Narayana appointed his 2nd son as the spiritual successor.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: In 1873 who founded Satya Shodhak Samaj?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1997, 40th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1995. Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule in 1873. He was born in 1827 as a gardener’s son. He operated a powerful movement of non-Brahmins. The main objectives of the Samaj were to redeem the Shudras from the infl uence of Brahmanical scriptures and make them conscious of their human rights and liberate them from mental and religious slavery. He also wrote a book ‘Gulamgiri’.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Whose main aim was to uplift the backward classes?

He composed critical books “Sarvjanik Satyadharm Pustak” and ‘Gulamgiri’ to spread his anti-Brahmin activities.]

The main objective of the organization was to liberate the Shudras and Ati Shudras and to prevent their exploitation by Arya-Brahmins. It was an anti-caste Movement in Maharashtra. Savitribai became head of women section who worked for lower caste girls. Deenbandhu played an important role in Satyashodhak Samaj in spreading the Movement to the remotest parts of Maharashtra.]

Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2008. Dharma Sabha was an orthodox society, founded in 1830 A.D.by Raja Radhakant Deb (1784-1867 A.D.). He opposed the abolition of Sati and also played an active role in promoting Western education among girls.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Who was the founder of Radha Swami Satsang?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2002. Radha Swami (Soami) Satsang was founded in 1861 also known as Shivdayal Sahab or Swamiji Maharaj. Seth Shivdayal Ji started his faith on “Satnaam” and “Anami”.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Which reformer of Maharashtra is also known as ‘Lokahitvadi’?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1995. Gopal Hari Deshmukh (1823–1892 A.D.) was a social reformer and intellectual thinker from Maharashtra, India. He was born in Pune. At the age of 25, Deshmukh started writing articles aimed at social reform in Maharashtra in the weekly ’Prabhakar’ under the pen name ’Lokahitvadi.’ In the first two years, he penned 108 articles on social reform. That group of articles has come to be known in Marathi literature as ’Lokahitawadinchi Shatapatre.’ He became a member of the Council of Governor-General in 1880 A.D. He appeared in the court of Delhi wearing hand-woven Khadi clothes, as a supporter of the national self-reliance.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Who was known by the nickname “Lokahitvadi”?

Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2024. In the 19th century, the great Parsi social reformer Behramji Malabari campaigned against child marriage and advocated for widow remarriage, publishing editorials to support these causes. The Age of Consent Act, 1891, was passed due to his efforts. Bal Gangadhar Tilak opposed this Act.]

It is known that the Social Reform Association was an organization established by Ranade's Indian National Social Conference (1887 A.D.). Before this in 1878 A.D. Veeresalingam founded the Rajahmundry Social Reform Association.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: The Rajamundry Social Reform Association to encourage widow re-marriage was founded in 1871 by
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre.) 2021. The Rajahmundry Social Reform Association was formed by Raj Bahadur Kandukuri Veeresalingam Pantulu. He was a social reformer from Madras Presidency of British-India. He is considered as the father of the Telugu Renaissance movement. Through the association he fought against hiring nautch girls and spearheaded a compaign for widow remarriage.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: During the Indian Freedom Struggle, the National Social Conference was formed. What was the reason for its formation?
options: (a) Different social reform groups or organizations of Bengal region united to form a single body to discuss the issues of larger interest and to prepare appropriate petitions/representations to the Government
(b) Indian National Congress did not want to include social reforms in its deliberations and decided to form a separate body for such a purpose
(c) Behramji Malabari and M.G. Ranade decided to bring together all the social reform groups of the country under one organization
(d) None of statement (a), (b) and (c) given above is correct in this context
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2012. Indian National Congress did not want to include social reforms in its deliberations as it felt that the Congress platform should be devoted to political affairs only. So it was suggested to form a separate body for such purposes.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Consider the following statements: 1. Arya Samaj was founded in 1835 2. Lala Lajpat Rai opposed the appeal of Arya Samaj to the authority of Vedas in support of its social reform programme. 3. Under Keshab Chandra Sen, the Brahmo Samaj campaigned for women’s education 4. Vinoba Bhave founded the Sarvodaya Samaj to work among refugees. Which of these statements are correct?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2001. Arya Samaj was founded on April, 1875 A.D., at Bombay by Dayanand Saraswati. Thus statement 1 is incorrect. Lala Lajpat Rai was one of the members of Arya Samaj and he did not oppose the appeal of Arya Samaj to the authority of Vedas in support of its social reform programme. Thus, statement 2nd is also incorrect. Brahmo Samaj launched the movement for the education of women in the society under Keshav Chandra Sen. Vinoba Bhave founded the Sarvodaya Samaj to raise the living standard of the Indians and to promote the principles of Mahatma Gandhi and work among refugees. Thus, statements 3 and 4 are correct.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Which of the following Act was passed in 1856? (i) Religious Disabilities Act (ii) Sati Prohibition Act (iii) Hindu Widow Remarriage Act (iv) Policy of Annexation Choose the correct option from the codes given below:
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2001. Religious Disabilities Act was never passed in India. The Hindu Widows Remarriage Act of 1856, enacted in response to the campaign of Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, provided legal safeguards against loss of certain forms of inheritance for a remarrying Hindu widow. Vishnushastri and D.K. Karve were the leaders connected to widow welfare. D.K. Karve founded Hindu widows home in 1896 A.D. in Pune and also established the first Women University in 1916 A.D. in Bombay. The Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829, was passed during the period of William Bentinck, the Governor General of Bengal. Dalhousie’s policy of annexation was presented in 1848 A.D.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: In which year was “The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act’ passed?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2019. See the explanation of the above question.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: The name of D.K. Karve of Western India fi gures in the context of which of the following?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2016. Dhondo Keshav Karve was an Indian social reformer and educator from Western India. He worked in the fi eld of women’s welfare. He worked in promoting widow’s education. He started a shelter and school for widows. He established first University for women in India in 1916.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Who among the following prominently fought for and got widow remarriage legalized ?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2012. The Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act of 1856 was enacted in response to the campaign of Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar. The act provided legal safeguards against loss of certain forms of inheritance for a remarrying Hindu widow.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Who among the following was associated as Secretary with Hindu Female School which later came to be known as Bethune Female School?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2021. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was the first secretary of Bethune College.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: (a) In 1829, William Bentinck declared Sati System an offence by law.
(b) The Government had passed an Act in 1856 under which Hindu widows could remarry.
(c) Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded Arya Samaj in 1875.
(d) Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a supporter of Sati System.
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [M.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1994. Statement (d) is incorrect. Raja Ram Mohan Roy strongly opposed Sati system. He appealed to William Bentinck, the then Governor General of Bengal to ban Sati practice in British India and Sati System was banned under provision 17th rule of The Bengal Sati Regulation 1829, and ordered the court to fi le a case as culpable homicide and punish those involved.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: What did the Act V of 1843 make illegal?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2007. Act V of 1843 made slavery illegal in India during the tenure of Governor-General Lord Ellenborough. A clause in the Charter of 1833, asked to end slavery at the earliest. Finally, in 1843, slavery was declared illegal all over India, and all the slaves were freed without giving any compensation to the owners.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Who among the following had played an important role in passing the Native Marriage Act of 1872?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2011. Keshab Chandra Sen had played an important role in passing the Native Marriage Act of 1872. This act fi xed the minimum age of marriage to 14 years for girls and 18 years for boys. This Act is also known as Brahmo Marriage Act.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: In which year was the ‘Native Marriage Act’ passed?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2019. See the explanation of the above question.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: The Civil Marriage Act of 1872 had sought to curb the practice of child marriage by placing the minimum age of girls at:
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2000. K.C. Sen adopted a programme of social reforms such as the abolition of child marriage, polygamy, widow remarriage and inter-caste marriage. Finally, the Native Marriage Act was passed in 1872 A.D. This Act legalized unorthodox inter-caste marriages and banned polygamy. Age of Consent Act (1891), which forbade the marriage of girls below the age of 12 was enacted by the efforts of a Parsi reformer, B.M. Malabari. Bal Gangadhar Tilak opposed the Age of Consent Act.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Consider the following passage: “Born in 1853 he was a Parsi from Western India. He was the editor of “Indian Spectator” and “Voice of India.” He was a social reformer and was the chief crusader for the Age of Consent Act 1891. Who is being described in the above paragraph?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2016. Behramji Malabari, a Parsi Zoroastrian who became a prominent Indian poet, author and social reformer, was born in Baroda Gujarat. He served as editor of the Indian Spectator and the Voice of India. He was a social reformer and his activism resulted in the Criminal Law Amendment Act of 1885 and the Age of Consent Act in 1891.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: What was the minimum marriageable age fi xed under Sharda Act for boys and girls?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Mains) 2013, U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2012. The Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929, passed in 1929, fi xed the age of marriage for girls at 14 years and boys at 18 years. It is popularly known as the Sharda Act, which is based on the name of Har Bilas Sharda, best known for having introduced the The Child Marriage Restraint Act, (1929).]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Sharda Act related to
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Mains) 2002. See the explanation of the above question.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Who founded the ‘Theosophical Society’?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [53rd to 55th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2011. The Theosophical Society was founded in the year 1875 in New York City by Russian (Now-Ukrainian) noblewoman Helena Petrovna Blavatsky and American Colonel Henry Steel Alcott, along with William Quan Judge and some other individuals. In 1879, the principal founders, Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Col. Alcott moved to India where the Society spread rapidly. In 1882, they established the Society’s International Headquarter in Adyar, a suburb of Madras (currently Chennai). Brahmo Sabha was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 and Ramkrishna Mission was founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1897, Thus, option (a) is correct.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: The success of the Theosophical Society in India was mainly due to –
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Mains) 2010. In 1879, the principal founders, Madam H.P. Blavatsky and Colonel Alcott, moved to India, where Theosophical Society spread rapidly. In 1882 A.D., they established the society’s international headquarters in Adyar, a suburb of Madras (currently Chennai). In 1889 A.D., Annie Besant joined the society, and after coming to India in 1893 A.D., she played an active role in society. She considered Hinduism to be the world’s most esoteric and spiritual religion. She used to believe in the principles of rebirth.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
options: (a) Raja Ram Mohan Roy - Brahmo Samaj
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011. Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded Brahmo Sabha in 1828, which was later called Brahmo Samaj. Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 in Mumbai. Swami Vivekananda founded Ramakrishna Mission in 1897. Prarthana Samaj was founded by Aatma Ram Pandurang by the inspiration of Keshav Chandra Sen in 1867 in Bombay and Mahadev Govind Ranade was a member of this society. Annie Besant was related to Theosophical Society.]

Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2003. Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded Brahmo Samaj in 1828, at Calcutta. Manav Dharma Sabha was founded in Surat. It played an important role in the fi elds of Muslim social reforms.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Which one the following social reformers strongly opposed Jury Act of 1826’?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2017. The Jury Act of 1826 was the manifestation of the idea of religious superiority of the British government that introduced the nation of religious distinctions in the judicial system of the country. According to the act, only Christians had the right to sit as Jurors involving trials of Christians (whether Indian or European). He can also judge cases of the natives (Hindu and Muslims). The natives (Hindus and Muslisms) could sit as Jurors in the cases of trails of Hindus and Muslims but not of Christians. Ram Mohan Roy strongly opposed this act and the fl agrant injustice contained under the act.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Match the following A. Prarthana Samaj B. Ramakrishna Mission C. Satyashodhak Samaj D. Muhammad-Anglo Oriental College Aligarh. 1. Swami Vivekananda 2. Mahadev Govind Ranade 3. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan 4. Jyotiba Phule. Code :

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Justice Party: 1. The Justice Party opposed the Congress by calling it an organization dominated by Brahmins. 2. It claimed the same communal representation for non-Brahmins, similar to the communal representation granted to Muslims through the Morley-Minto reforms. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2024. The Justice Party was formed in 1916 AD in the Madras Presidency. It was a non-Brahmin organization, particularly representing the interests of lower castes and backward classes. This party accused the Congress of being dominated by Brahmins and demanded social justice, educational opportunities, and caste-based representation. In the Morley Minto reforms, the Justice Party advocated for caste-based representation for non-Brahmins. Thus, both the given statements are correct.]

Fresh vigour and energy were infused into the sabha in November 1871 AD with the entry of M.G. Ranade.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Which one of the following is correctly matched?

Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2004. He also chaired the 21st session of Indian National Congress in 1905 held in Banaras (Varanasi). He is also known as a political guru of Mahatma Gandhi. Brahmo Samaj was divided into two parts, Adi Brahmo Samaj under Devendra Nath Tagore and Bhartiya Brahmo Samaj under Keshav Chandra Sen. Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Rao Phule. He also wrote a book named ‘Gulamgiri.’]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded Servants of India Society in the year
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [Raj. P.C.S. (Pre) 2023. The 'Servants of India Society' was founded by Gopal Krishna Gokhale at Fergusson Hill on June 12, 1905 A.D., in the Pune district of Maharashtra. Gokhale founded the society along with three of his friends – Natesh Appaji Dravid, Gopal Krishna Deodhar and Anant Vinayak Patwardhan, all of whom became lifelong members of the society. Socio-Religious Movements.q: K.M. Panikkar referred to whom as 'the first diplomat of modern India'?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2024. K.M. Panikkar referred to Gopal Krishna Gokhale as 'the first diplomat of modern India.' Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a prominent political leader, social reformer, and an important fi gure in India's struggle for independence. Panikkar praised Gokhale's political perspective, especially his peaceful methods and efforts to gain international support for India's cause, which laid the foundation for modern India's diplomatic strategies.]

Socio-Religious Movements.q: Who was the founder of Bahujan Samaj?
Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Spl) (Pre) 2010. Mukund Rao Patil and Shankar Rao Jadhav founded Bahujan Samaj to oppose the exploitation of the lower castes by upper castes including Brahmins, moneylenders, and landlords. It also opposed the Indian National Congress Party. Later, it became a supporter of the British Government.]

Ramabai Ranade was also an inspiration of the women’s movement in Modern India. She was the wife of Mahadev Govind Ranade. She founded an organization called ‘Seva Sadan’. Socio-Religious Movements.q: Which of the following statement is not correct?

Socio-Religious Movements.explanation: [M.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1995. Mahatma Gandhi was born on October 2, 1869 A.D., at Porbandar. Hence option (d) is incorrect. Annie Besant became the chairman of the Theosophical Society after the death of Colonel Alcott in 1907 A.D. She came into the contact with this society in 1882 A.D. and became the offi cial member in 1889 A.D. In 1879 A.D., the principal founders, Madam H.P. Blavatsky and Col. Alcott moved to India, where the Society spread rapidly. In 1882, they established the Society’s International Headquarters in Adyar, a suburb of Madras (currently Chennai). Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded Arya Samaj in 1875 A.D. in Bombay.]

(Pre) 2024] During the Moderate Phase (1885-1905 AD) of the Indian National Movement, there was support for the rich democratic and scientifi c culture of modern Europe. The moderate leaders advocated for constitutional reforms, political participation and the expansion of modern education. They supported English education, as they believed it would help develop a modern outlook and social progress in India. However, the growing masses viewed British colonial policies with increasing resentment. Notably, Dadabhai Naoroji strongly criticized the economic aspects of British colonialism. His book, "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India," highlighted issues related to the economic drain, heavy taxation, and the decline of Indian industries. The moderates attempted to address such concerns through constitutional means rather than direct confrontation.

While the moderates had infi nite faith in the effi cacy of constitutional agitation and in appealing to the British sense of justice and fair play, in holding an annual conference, making speeches, passing elaborate resolutions and sending deputations to England. The extremists had no faith in the benevolence of British public or Parliament, nor were they convinced of the effi cacy of merely holding conferences. Extremists had faith in the concept of passive resistance.

The moderates opposed the resolutions on Swaraj (self-governance), Swadeshi National Education and boycott of foreign goods but extremists were not in favour of these. Hence, the difference of opinion between moderates and extremists fi nally reached to split in the Congress at the Surat Session (1907).

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Which of the following international events infl uenced the course of the national movement in India before the advent of Mahatma Gandhi? (1) Italian-Abyssinian War, 1898 (2) Boxer Movement in China (3) Revolutionary Movement in Ireland (4) Victory of Japan in the Russo-Japanese War
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1994. The Italian-Abyssinian War (in which the Italian colonial power was defeated), the Boxer movement against the imperialists in China during 1899-1901 A.D., and Japan's victory over Russia, infl uenced the direction of the national movement in India before the advent of Mahatma Gandhi, but among these, Japan's victory over Russia in the year 1905 A.D. had the most impact. Japan had proved itself militarily superior to a powerful European country by defeating Czarist Russia in the year 1905 A.D. This dispelled the false illusion that the people of the white race were invincible.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Read the following statements regarding the liberal phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1905 A.D.): 1. Supported the rich democratic and scientific culture of modern Europe. 2. Strongly criticized the economic aspects of British imperialism. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [Rajasthan P.C.S. (Pre) 2024. During the Moderate Phase (1885-1905 AD) of the Indian National Movement, there was support for the rich democratic and scientifi c culture of modern Europe. The moderate leaders advocated for constitutional reforms, political participation and the expansion of modern education. They supported English education, as they believed it would help develop a modern outlook and social progress in India. However, the growing masses viewed British colonial policies with increasing resentment. Notably, Dadabhai Naoroji strongly criticized the economic aspects of British colonialism. His book, "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India," highlighted issues related to the economic drain, heavy taxation, and the decline of Indian industries. The moderates attempted to address such concerns through constitutional means rather than direct confrontation.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: The protest method of moderate leaders of the Congress was ?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [48th to 52nd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2008. The methods employed by the two groups (Moderates and Extremists) of Congress were different in their tempo and approach. Congress split into two different groups at Surat Session of Congress in 1907 A.D. While the moderates had infi nite faith in the effi cacy of constitutional agitation and in appealing to the British sense of justice and fair play, in holding an annual conference, making speeches, passing elaborate resolutions and sending deputations to England. The extremists had no faith in the benevolence of British public or Parliament, nor were they convinced of the effi cacy of merely holding conferences. Extremists had faith in the concept of passive resistance.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Which one of the following movements has contributed to a split in the Indian National Congress resulting in the emergence of ‘moderates’ and ‘extremists’?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2015. Surat split (1907 A.D.), refers to the split in the Congress party into two groups : ‘Moderates’ and ‘Extremists.’ Moderates believed in the policy of settlement of minor issues with Government by deliberation, strikes, and boycotts to force their demands. The moderates opposed the resolutions on Swaraj (self-governance), Swadeshi National Education and boycott of foreign goods but extremists were not in favour of these. Hence, the difference of opinion between moderates and extremists fi nally reached to split in the Congress at the Surat Session (1907).]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Most of the moderate leaders hailed from :
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [43rd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1999, U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2016. During the era of liberal politics Dadabhai Naoroji, Pherozeshah Mehta, Dinshaw Wacha, Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee and Surendranath Banerjee were the moderate leaders who hailed from urban areas. The domination of prosperous and middle-class scholars like barristers, doctors, engineers, journalists and literary people was found during this period. The title and high designation charmed them. These representatives of Congress hailed from metropolitan cities and had no connection with common people.]

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Who of the following continuously from 1904 onwards emphasized on the grant of ‘self-rule’ to India?

In his presidential address in 1906 he demanded ‘Swaraj’ (Self Rule) at INC session.]

They had a sense of confi dence in British justice and their generosity. Their aim was not aggressive nationalism for attaining independence. Its objective was to obtain a share in Government for educated Indians, to create a platform for civil and political dialogue between educated Indians in British Raj. The first meeting was scheduled to be held in Poona, but due to an outbreak of Cholera, it was shifted to Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay. The first session of Indian National Union was held on 28-30 December, 1885 A.D.. In this session on the advice of Dadabhai Naoroji, the organization was renamed as ‘Indian National Congress.’]

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Which of the following was not an objective of the Indian National Congress as pointed out by W.C. Bonnerjee in 1885?

(b) To promote the feeling of nationalism among fellow countrymen by removing the feeling of casteism, communalism and regional biases
(c) To express the viewpoint on the necessary social issues with due consent of the educated class
(d) To determine on which direction and on which basis the work has to be done in the coming years for the Indian public interest
(e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [66th B.P.S.C. (Pre) (Re-Exam) 2020. In 1885 AD, the following objectives were stated in the first session of the Indian National Congress indicated by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee 1. To inculcate the feeling of national unity among countrymen, by removing the feeling of caste, sect and regional biases among them. 3. To unite all the classes and communities of India and create a sense of one nation among them; 4. Formulation and presentation of public demands; It is known that initially there was a provision or arrangement for not raising social issues from the Congress platform.]

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: In the first stage of the National Movement, which one among the following was not a demand of the Congress?
options: (a) To increase the number of members of the Legislative Councils
(b) To increase the number of members of the public representatives in the councils
(d) Unifi cation of Executive and Judiciary
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2023. During the first stage of National Movement, Congress demanded a greater voice for Indians in the government and in administration. It wanted the legislative councils to be made more representative, given more power and introduced in provinces where none existed. It demanded that Indians be placed in high positions in the government. Other demands included the separation of the judiciary from the executive, the repeal of the Arms Act and the freedom of speech and expression.]

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2011, I.A.S. (Pre) 2004. The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay, not in Calcutta. Although, first it was scheduled to be held in Poona, but due to an outbreak of Cholera, it was held in Bombay. Thus, the first statement is false. The second session was held in 1886 A.D. at Kolkata under the presidentship of Dadabhai Naoroji. Indian National Congress session and the Muslim League session both were held in Lucknow in 1916 A.D. Consequently, the pact was signed between Congress and the Muslim League which is known as ‘Lucknow Pact.’ In this session extremist who were excluded from the Congress party for 9 years were reintroduced to Congress. Ambica Charan Mazumdar served as the President in Lucknow Session, 1916.]

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: In which one of the following sessions, Congress declare its policy towards the Indian States for the first time?

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Which of the following statements is/are true? A. After the Nagpur Session (1920) of Congress, the provincial Congress Committees were constituted on linguistic basis. B. Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Who was the President of Gaya Session of the Indian National Congress held in 1922?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [56th to 59th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2015. Chittaranjan Das was the President of Gaya Session of Indian National Congress held in 1922 A.D. He was an eminent lawyer who distinguished himself by successfully defending Aurobindo Ghosh in famous Alipore Bomb Case. Along with Motilal Nehru, he formed the Swaraj Party within the INC, with the declared policy of entering the councils and disrupting their functioning. He is also known as Deshbandhu.]

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: The Haripura Session of Indian National Congress, 1938 was presided over by:
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2008. Between 19-21 February, 1938 AD, 51st session of Congress was held at Haripura in Gujarat, under the presidentship of Subhas Chandra Bose. National Planning Committee was constituted in this session and Jawaharlal Nehru was elected as President of the Committee. Rajendra Prasad was elected as President in 1934 AD. Later on, Abul Kalam Azad was elected as President of Congress in 1940-1946 AD. While J. B. Kripalani was President of the Meerut Session which was held in 1946 AD.]

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Who among the following was the youngest person to become the President of the Indian National Congress?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [M.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2017. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (1888-1958 AD) was made the President in the special session of the Indian National Congress held in Delhi in the year 1923 A.D. He was the youngest person to hold the post of President of the Indian National Congress for six consecutive years from 1940-46 A.D. This was the longest tenure before independence. Jawaharlal Nehru (1889-1964 AD) presided over the Lahore session of the Congress in the year 1929. Ananda Mohan Bose (1847-1906 AD) presided over the Madras session of the Congress in 1898, while Bhupendra Nath Bose (1859-1924 AD) presided over the Madras session of the Congress in 1914 A.D..]

Abul Kalam Azad was the president of Indian National Congress for six consecutive years from 1940-46 during the Quit India Movement. He also became the youngest person to serve as president in 1923 A.D. in Delhi special session. After Independence, the longest-serving president of INC is Sonia Gandhi 1998 to 2017 A.D. and 2019 to 2022 A.D.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: President of Indian National Congress at the time of Independence was?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2010, Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Mains) 2006. J. B. Kripalani was the President of Indian National Congress at the time of Independence. Elected in November 1946 A.D. at Meerut Session, Acharya (scholar) Jivatram Bhagwandas Kripalani was a Gandhian Socialist, environmentalist, mystic and freedom fi ghter and was noted for his incorruptibility and determination. Kriplani was prominently involved over a decade in top Congress party affairs and the organization of the Salt Satyagraha and the Quit India Movement.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress at the time of partition of India?

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: On which occasion was ‘Jana-Gana Mana,’ first sung?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [U.P.P.S.C. (GIC) 2010. “Jana Gana Mana” is the national anthem of India. Originally written in Bengali, it is the first of fi ve stanzas of a Brahmo hymn composed and scored by Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore. It was first sung during Calcutta Session of the Indian National Congress on 27 December, 1911. “Jana Gana Mana” was offi cially adopted by the Constituent Assembly as the Indian National Anthem on 24 January, 1950.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: The last session of Indian National Congress attended by Bal Gangadhar Tilak was :
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2014. The last session of Indian National Congress attended by Bal Gangadhar Tilak was Amritsar Session,1919. He had mellowed sufficiently to oppose Gandhi’s policy of boycotting the elections to the legislative councils established as part of the reforms that followed from the Montagu-Chelmsford Report to Parliament in 1918. Instead, Tilak advised the delegates to follow his policy of ‘responsive cooperation’ in carrying out the reforms, which introduced a certain degree of Indian participation in regional Government. He died on 1st August, 1920.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Which of the following international events infl uenced the course of the national movement in India before the advent of Mahatma Gandhi? (1) Italian-Abyssinian War, 1898 (2) Boxer Movement in China (3) Revolutionary Movement in Ireland (4) Victory of Japan in the Russo-Japanese War
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1994. The Italian-Abyssinian War (in which the Italian colonial power was defeated), the Boxer movement against the imperialists in China during 1899-1901 A.D., and Japan's victory over Russia, infl uenced the direction of the national movement in India before the advent of Mahatma Gandhi, but among these, Japan's victory over Russia in the year 1905 A.D. had the most impact. Japan had proved itself militarily superior to a powerful European country by defeating Czarist Russia in the year 1905 A.D. This dispelled the false illusion that the people of the white race were invincible.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Read the following statements regarding the liberal phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1905 A.D.): 1. Supported the rich democratic and scientific culture of modern Europe. 2. Strongly criticized the economic aspects of British imperialism. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [Rajasthan P.C.S. (Pre) 2024. During the Moderate Phase (1885-1905 AD) of the Indian National Movement, there was support for the rich democratic and scientifi c culture of modern Europe. The moderate leaders advocated for constitutional reforms, political participation and the expansion of modern education. They supported English education, as they believed it would help develop a modern outlook and social progress in India. However, the growing masses viewed British colonial policies with increasing resentment. Notably, Dadabhai Naoroji strongly criticized the economic aspects of British colonialism. His book, "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India," highlighted issues related to the economic drain, heavy taxation, and the decline of Indian industries. The moderates attempted to address such concerns through constitutional means rather than direct confrontation.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: The protest method of moderate leaders of the Congress was ?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [48th to 52nd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2008. The methods employed by the two groups (Moderates and Extremists) of Congress were different in their tempo and approach. Congress split into two different groups at Surat Session of Congress in 1907 A.D. While the moderates had infi nite faith in the effi cacy of constitutional agitation and in appealing to the British sense of justice and fair play, in holding an annual conference, making speeches, passing elaborate resolutions and sending deputations to England. The extremists had no faith in the benevolence of British public or Parliament, nor were they convinced of the effi cacy of merely holding conferences. Extremists had faith in the concept of passive resistance.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Which one of the following movements has contributed to a split in the Indian National Congress resulting in the emergence of ‘moderates’ and ‘extremists’?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2015. Surat split (1907 A.D.), refers to the split in the Congress party into two groups : ‘Moderates’ and ‘Extremists.’ Moderates believed in the policy of settlement of minor issues with Government by deliberation, strikes, and boycotts to force their demands. The moderates opposed the resolutions on Swaraj (self-governance), Swadeshi National Education and boycott of foreign goods but extremists were not in favour of these. Hence, the difference of opinion between moderates and extremists fi nally reached to split in the Congress at the Surat Session (1907).]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Most of the moderate leaders hailed from :
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [43rd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1999, U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2016. During the era of liberal politics Dadabhai Naoroji, Pherozeshah Mehta, Dinshaw Wacha, Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee and Surendranath Banerjee were the moderate leaders who hailed from urban areas. The domination of prosperous and middle-class scholars like barristers, doctors, engineers, journalists and literary people was found during this period. The title and high designation charmed them. These representatives of Congress hailed from metropolitan cities and had no connection with common people.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Who of the following continuously from 1904 onwards emphasized on the grant of ‘self-rule’ to India?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2016. In 1904 A.D., first time Dadabhai Naoroji demanded ‘Swaraj,’ (Self Rule) or Self-Government in International Socialist Congress, for India and continuously emphasized the grant of Self Rule in India. In his presidential address in 1906 he demanded ‘Swaraj’ (Self Rule) at INC session.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Which one of the following was not an extremist ?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [44th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2000. Gopal Krishna Gokhale was a prominent social reformer of India who founded an organization to work for the relief of underprivileged. He led the moderate nationalists in the early years of the Indian Independence Movement. As an infl uential and respected member of the Indian National Congress, the leading Nationalist organization in the pre-independent India, Gokhale advocated moderate and Constitutional methods of agitation and gradual reform.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Who among the following was not an outstanding leader of extreme Nationalism?

He was a senior leader of INC, founder of the Servants of India Society. He was not a leader of extreme nationalism.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Who among the following was not an extremist nationalist leader ?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: See the explanation of above question.

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Who accused Indian National Congress of practising ‘politics of prayer, petition and protest’?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2002, U.P. Lower Sub. (Spl) (Pre) 2002. The first two decades are INC are described in history as a moderate era. Among some of the prominent moderate leaders were Dadabhai Naoroji, Surendra Nath Banerjee, Mahadev Govind Ranade, Pherozeshah Mehta, Gopal Krishna Gokhale and Anand Mohan Bose. They had a sense of confi dence in British justice and their generosity. Their aim was not aggressive nationalism for attaining independence. Leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal, raised extremist ideology. B.G. Tilak accused moderates of believing in constitutional method and favouring the policy of protest, prayer, and petition.]

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Who accused Indian National Congress of practising politics of, pray and petition and protest?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2005, U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2002. See the explanation of above question.]

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: The Congress policy of prayer and petition ultimately came to an end under the guidance of:
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1999. Congress policy of prayer and petition ultimately came to an end or reduced to minimum under the leadership of Bal Gangadhar Tilak. He was one of the strongest opponent of the British Empire. He strongly recommended a method of agitation. Many intellectual Congressmen became his followers. Leaders like Lala Lajpat Rai of Punjab and Bipin Chandra Pal of Calcutta turned into staunch followers of him. They strongly opposed the moderate policies of Congress.]

Pal called the Indian National Congress as a “Begging Institute.”]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Which statement is true regarding Bipin Chandra Pal? 1. He was a Brahmo Samaj Leader and Social Reformer. 2. A weekly magazine named New India was published. Select the correct answer using the code given below: Code
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2023. Bipin Chandra Pal was associated with Brahmo Samaj and was a social reformer. In 1901, he published a weekly magazine 'New India'.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Indian National Movement came to be dominated by the extremists after
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [43rd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1999. After the year 1906 A.D., the effect of extremism had increased on the Indian National Movement. The Congress split at Surat came in December 1907 A.D., around the time when revolutionary terrorism had gained momentum. The extremists were aggressive nationalist members of Indian National Congress. The important extremist leaders were Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghosh. Tilak announced that ‘’ Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it’’.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Which one of the following leaders belonged to the Extremist wing of the Congress?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [45th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2001. Aurobindo Ghose was an extremist of Congress. He was one of the four pillars (Lal, Bal, Pal, Ghose) of extremists. He was arrested in 1908 A.D. by British Police in Maniktalla garden raid. He got the punishment of one-year imprisonment, but he was released due to the lack of evidence. Finally, he became sage, secluded himself from revolutionary activities and moved to Pondicherry (Puducherry).]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Who among the following was an extremist?

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: He wrote biographies of Mazzini, Garibaldi, Shivaji and Shrikrishna; stayed in America for some time; and was also elected to the Central Assembly. He was :
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2018. Along with being a politician, he was also a prolifi c writer. He also wrote brief biographies of Lord Krishna, Shivaji, Swami Dayanand Saraswati, Mazzini and Garibaldi. 'Unhappy India' and 'The Story of My Deportation' are his other important works.]

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Who of the following was not a moderate:

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Which one of the following defi nes extremist ideology during the early phase of Indian freedom movement?
options: (a) Stimulating the production of indigenous articles by giving them preference over imported commodities.
(b) Obtaining self-government by aggressive means in place of petitions and constitutional ways.
(c) Providing national educational according to the requirements of the country.
(d) Organizing coups against the British empire through military revolt.
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: Moderates believed in constitutional methods of British Laws, adopting proposals and delegations to London for negotiation and discussion. On the other hand, extremists believed in aggressive protests, self-sacrifi ces and determination at the beginning of the Indian Independence Movement. Independence meant for extremists as Complete Independence from foreign control, while moderates meant Independence as self-governance under colonial rule.

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: Which amongst the following statements is/are true about V.D. Savarkar? (i) He founded Abhinav Bharat - A revolutionary organization. (iv) He jumped into the sea from the sailing ship in order to escape British captivity? Choose the correct answer :
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [R.A.S./R.T.S. (Re. Exam) (Pre) 2013. During his college education in Pune, Vinayak Damodar Savarkar founded the 'Abhinav Bharat Society'. Savarkar wrote the book 'The Indian War of Independence 1857'. He analysed the circumstances of 1857 A.D. uprising and assailed British rule in India as unjust and oppressive. It was via this book that Savarkar became one of the first writers to allude the uprising as India’s 'First War for Independence'. To inspire Indian nationalist, he wrote the biography of Mazzini. Savarkar was arrested and was deported to India from England through the ship. He made a plan to escape by ship and told his friend to keep track of the ship. He escaped and jumped into the sea from the sailing ship but was re-arrested as the alarm was raised. Thus all the given options are correct.]

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.q: When did Bal Gangadhar Tilak get the title Lokmanya?
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2012. It was alleged that the Brahmins of Poona, under the leadership of Tilak, had conspired in the murder of Rand and Ayerst. In July 1897 A.D., Tilak was arrested on charges of sedition under section 124-A of the Indian Penal Code for inciting murder through his writings. He was prosecuted and sentenced to 18 months imprisonment, which caused huge protests across the country. For this reason Tilak became popular as an all India leader and the public gave him the title of 'Lokmanya'.]

Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki watched the usual movements of Kingsford and prepared a plan to kill him. On the evening of April 30, 1908 A.D., the duo waited in front of the gate of European club for the carriage of Kingsford to arrive. When a vehicle came out of the gate, they threw bombs and blew up the carriage. Unfortunately, the vehicle was not carrying Kingsford and instead, two innocent British ladies- Mrs. and Miss Kennedy (the wife and daughter of barrister Pringle Kennedy) were killed. The revolutionary duo fl ed. Prafulla committed suicide and Khudiram was later arrested and hanged.]

Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2022. No Organisation by the name of Hindustan Socialist Democratic Union has existed in history. Gopen Chakravarti and Dharani Goswami were members of the Calcutta Anushilan Samiti associated with the communist movement and accused in Meerut conspiracy. Rash Behari Bose was an immigrant Indian living in Japan. On 28-30th March 1942, Bose convened a conference in Tokyo (Japan) to discuss political issues with Indians. Bose decided to establish the Indian Independence League. It was structured during the Bangkok Convention which took place in June, 1942 where Subhash Chandra Bose was invited. During this Conference, Ras Bihari Bose established Indian Independence League.]
Revolutionary Movements In and Outside I.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Which of the following occurred last:
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2000. In the above-mentioned events, the event of Permanent Settlement of Bengal was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793 A.D. Subsidiary Alliance was a system of the rulers which was introduced by Lord Wellesley in India. The Doctrine of Lapse was an annexation policy purportedly devised by Lord Dalhousie, who was the Governor-General of India from 1848-56 A.D. From the above options, the partition of Bengal was the last event announced in July, 1905 by Lord Curzon.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Anti partition movement of Bengal was initiated on:
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1994. On 20 July, 1905 A.D., Curzon issued an order to divide Bengal (resolution was signed on July 19, 1905). One of the main objectives of the partition of Bengal was to divide the unity among the people of Bengal. Lord Curzon divided the territories of Bengal in such a way that the western part formed the Hindu majority area and the eastern part formed the Muslim majority area. The partition of Bengal fi nally took place on 16th October, 1905 A.D. On 7 August, 1905 A.D., one of the first mass protests was organized in Calcutta’s Town Hall, also known as Anti-partition Movement.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: When did the Anti-Partition Movement begin with a massive demonstration at the Town Hall, Calcutta?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P. R.O/A.R.O (Re. Exam) (Pre) 2025. See the explanation of above question.]

However on 19th July 1905 A.D. the resolution of the declaration of partition of Bengal signed. Because of this BPSC had given (a) as correct option.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Name the Viceroy of India concerned with Bengal partition
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [42nd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1997, Uttarakhand U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2003. The partition of Bengal was announced on July 20, 1905 A.D., by the then Viceroy of India, Lord Curzon (1899-1905 A.D.) and came into effect on October 16, 1905 A.D. Later on, the decision of partition of Bengal was suspended during Delhi Durbar in 1911 A.D.]

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: The partition of Bengal was carried out by Lord Curzon in 1905. In which year was this partition annulled?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2024. See the explanation of above question.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: The Governor-General who partitioned Bengal?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011. See the explanation of above question.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: The Lieutenant Governor of Bengal at the time of Partition of Bengal was :
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2014. Sir Andrew Henderson Leith Fraser, was an Indian Civil Servant who served as Lieutenant Governor of Bengal between 1903 and 1908. Sir Andrew Fraser was very actively involved in framing the Bengal partition.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Who among of the following led the agitation against the partition of Bengal (1905)?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2011. Surendranath Banerjee led the agitation against the partition of Bengal (1905).]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Who has said about Bengal Partition. "The partition announcement fell like a bomb shell"?
options: (e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [67th B.P.S.C. (Pre) (Re. Exam) 2022. Regarding the partition of Bengal, Surendranath Banerjee had said, "Partition fell on us like a bomb". Partition of Bengal was happened during the tenure of Lord Curzon.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Who among the following were the critics of Swadeshi' movement and pleaded for a better understanding between the East and the West?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2009. Rabindranath Tagore’s political acumen exhibited a marked ambivalence. On the one hand, he denounced European imperialism, occasionally voicing full support for Indian nationalist. On the other hand, he also shunned the Swadeshi movement, denouncing it in his acrid September, 1925 A.D. essay “The Cult of the Chakra” (an allusion to elements of Gandhism and the Non-cooperation Movement). In addition, he viewed British control of India as a “Political symptom of our social disease.” Urging Indians to accept blind revolution but of steady and purposeful education.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Who was the first to suggest the boycott of British goods in Bengal?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011, U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2004. Krishna Kumar Mitra was an Indian freedom fi ghter, journalist, and leader of Brahmo Samaj. He was an active leader and was against the partition of Bengal. On 13 July, 1905 AD, In his Nationalist Bengali weekly Magazine titled ‘Sanjibani’ he boldly advocated for the freedom of the press. In his opinion, the manufacturing of British goods should be abolished. He called for a boycott of foreign goods, government offi cials and organisations by breaking all connections, people should mourn etc. His ideas were supported by a gathering in District Bagerhat (Division-Khulna) on 16 July, 1905 A.D.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Boycott of British goods was adopted as a national policy in
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P.R.O. /A.R.O. (Pre) 2014. Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal on July 20, 1905 A.D. As a result, Swadeshi Movement was announced in Townhall, Kolkata on August 7, 1905 A.D., and ‘Boycott Proposal’ was passed. The boycott of British goods was adopted as a national policy in this meeting.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Who painted the famous image of Bharat Mata to visually associate the identity of India, as a Nation?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [Rajasthan P.C.S. (Pre) 2024. To visually represent India as a nation, Abanindranath Tagore created the famous image of Bharat Mata (Mother India). This painting was made in 1905 A.D. during the Swadeshi Movement against the partition of Bengal. In the painting, Bharat Mata is depicted as a goddess with four hands, wearing a saffron-colored sari. Abanindranath Tagore’s portrayal of Bharat Mata became a symbol of nationalism and unity among Indians during the freedom movement.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Partition of Bengal was done mainly for :
options: (a) To divide the Hindu and Muslims
(c) To weaken the growth of Nationalism in Bengal
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 1998. “The Partition of Bengal, said Lord Curzon, was a mere readjustment of administrative boundaries.” The argument advocated for the partition was that it would improve the administration of the two provinces. The main motive was to strike at the roots of Bengali Nationalism which was growing in solidarity form. At that time Bengal was considered to be “the nerve-centre” of Indian Nationalism. Curzon decided to ruin the new spirit by dividing the politically advanced communities into separate provinces.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q:
The following programmes were launched by the nationalist against the partition of Bengal : 
1. Boycott 
2. Swadeshi
3. Non-cooperation 
4. National education
Select the correct answer :
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2014. The partition of Bengal in 1905 A.D. led to Swadeshi and Boycott Movement. Swadeshi Movement was complementary to ‘Boycott Movement.’ With the boycott of foreign goods, the use of ‘Swadeshi’ or indigenous goods increased. ‘Swadeshi’ was not altogether a noble idea. The movement spread to all classes and groups of people, including women and children, school and college students. This made the British to reverse the order of partition of Bengal. The boycott and Swadeshi Movements helped in the establishment of Swadeshi industries - textile mills, banks, chemical works and insurance companies. Swadeshi Stores were opened. National education and Indian languages were encouraged.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: The ‘Swadeshi’ and Boycott’ were adopted as methods of struggle for the first times during the
options: (a) agitation against the Partition of Bengal
(d) visit of the Simon Commission to India
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2016. The Swadeshi and Boycott were adopted as methods of struggle for the first time during the agitation against the partition of Bengal. It was an economic strategy aimed at the British Empire against the partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon on 16 October, 1905 A.D.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: The Swadeshi and Boycott were adopted the methods of struggle for the first time during the?
options: (b) visit of the Simon Commission to India
(d) More than one of the above
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [68th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2022. Swadeshi and Boycott were adopted as the methods of struggle for the first time during the Bengal partition. After the formal proclamation of partition of Bengal on 20 July 1905 AD by Lord Curzon, Swadeshi movement was formally started on 7 August 1905 AD with the passing of the 'Boycott' resolution in a meeting at Calcutta Townhall.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Which movement was started as a reaction to the Partition of Bengal?
options: (e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [66th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2020. See the explanation of above question.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q:
Consider the following statements :
 Statement-I :
 7 th August is declared as the National Handloom Day
 Statement II:
It was in 1905 that the Swadeshi Movement was launched on the same day.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: (a) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
(b) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
(c) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
(d) Statement I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2023. In India, 7th August is celebrated as National Handloom day every year. It is celebrated in memory of Swadeshi Movement that was launched on 7th August, 1905 A.D. Hence, both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: What was the immediate cause for the launch of the Swadeshi Movement?
options: (a) The partition of Bengal done by Lord Curzon
(b) A sentence of 18 months rigorous imprisonment imposed on Lokmanya Tilak
(c) The arrest and deportation of Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh; and passing of the Punjab Colonization Bill
(d) Death sentence pronounced on the Chapekar brothers
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2010. The Swadeshi movement was the outcome of Bengal partition. This concept was mainly presented by Aurobindo Ghosh, Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal and Lala Lajpat Rai. They wanted to implement Swadeshi Movement in whole of India, but Moderates were against it.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: The Swadeshi Movement took place in India during -:
options: (c) the protest against the Rowlatt Act
(e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [63rd B.P.S.C (Pre.) 2017. See the explanation of above question.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Bengal was partitioned in 1905, but due to opposition it was again divided in
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [46th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2003. A ceremonial welcome was organized on the arrival of King George V and Queen Mary at the Delhi Durbar in 1911 AD, where they were presented to an assembled audience of Indian dignitaries and princes as the Emperor and Empress of India on 12 December, 1911 AD. During Delhi Durbar on December 12, 1911 A.D., the King abolished the partition of Bengal and declared the transfer of the Indian capital from Calcutta to Delhi. As declared, Bengal was reorganized as the new province. Orissa and Bihar were separated from Bengal.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: The Partition of Bengal made by Lord Curzon in 1905 lasted until
options: (a) The First World War, when Indian troops were needed by the British and the partition, was ended

(d) The Partition of India in 1947 when East Bengal became East Pakistan
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2014. See the explanation of above question.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: In which year partition of Bengal made by Lord Curzon was cancelled ?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [48th to 52nd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2008, U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1993, U.P. P.C.S (Pre) 1991. See the explanation of above question.]

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: When was Bengal reunited due to the protests by Indians?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2010. See the explanation of above question.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Who was the leader of the Swadeshi Movement in Madras?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2008. The Swadeshi Movement had its genesis in the anti-partition Movement which was started to oppose British decision on the partition of Bengal. The formal proclamation of the Swadeshi Movement was made on August 7, 1905 AD, at a meeting held at the Town Hall in Calcutta. In 7 August 1905 A.D. meeting, the famous Boycott resolution was passed which was first suggested by Krishna Kumar Mitra. Lokmanya Tilak led the Presidency of Mumbai and Pune, Ajit Singh and Lala Lajpat Rai in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh, Syed Haider Raja led the Presidency of Delhi. Chidambaram Pillai in Madras Presidency.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Who among the following led the Swadeshi Movement in Delhi?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2011. See the explanation of above question.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q:
Which of the following classes was mainly unaffected by the Swadeshi Movement of 1905?
 (i) Women (ii) Farmers
 (iii) Muslim (iv) Intellectuals
 Select your answer from the following codes
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [40th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1995. On 20 July, 1905 A.D., Curzon issued an order for partitioning of Bengal. On 7 August, 1905 A.D., one of the first mass protests was organized in Calcutta’s Town Hall, which was known as ‘Swadeshi Movement’. From this Movement, people started opposing the British offi ce, institute, and boycott foreign goods. A remarkable aspect of the Swadeshi Movement was seen in the active participation of women. To collect the public support, Aswani Kumar Dutt organized the committee which is known as (Swadesh Bandhav Society). Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai and Aurobindo Ghosh played leading role in the fabrication of the Movement's character. In this Movement, women actively participated but farmers and Muslims were very limited involved in this Movement. They separated themselves from this Movement. Thus, option (c) is the correct answer.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Vande Mataram became the theme song of the Indian National Movement during
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P.P.S.C. (GIC) 2010, Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Mains) 2006, U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2005, U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2002. During Swadeshi Movement, the actual day of partition, October 16, 1905 A.D., was declared a day of mourning throughout Bengal and the hearths in the houses were kept unlit. People tied rakhis on each other wrists as a symbol of brotherhood. In Calcutta, most of the offi ces were kept closed, and a strike was observed in some jute mills and railway workshops. The streets reverberated with Vande Mataram which became the overnight National Song of Bengal and later, the Theme ralley cry or anthem of the National Movement.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: With reference to the period of extremist nationalist movement in India with its spirit of Swadeshi, which one of the following statements is not correct?
options: (a) Liyakat Hussain led the Muslim peasants of Barisal in their agitations
(b) In 1889, the scheme of national education was formulated by Satish Chandra Mukherjee
(c) The Bengal National College was founded in 1906 with Aurobindo as the Principal
(d) Tagore preached the cult of Atmasakti, the main plank of which was social and economic regeneration of the villages
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2002. Statement (a) is not correct. Liyakat Hussain did not lead the Muslim peasants of Barisal in their agitation. It was lead by Ashwani Kumar Dutta.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Which of the statements is not correct regarding ‘Swadeshi Movement’?
options: (a) Some specifi c Muslims were joined in it.
(b) Women’s actively participated in this movement
(c) Neither this movement affected Bengal farmers and nor did they join
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2002. The Swadeshi Movement influenced only some specific Muslims of society. For the first time, women took part in any movement actively. They came outside their houses, demonstrated in rallies and sat to protest. But this movement did not influence the farmers of Bengal. Barisal was an exception to it. This movement affected only high and middle class people of the society. Swadeshi Movement was not only limited to Bengal but also leaders like Lala Lajpat Rai, Tilak and Aurobindo Ghosh actively participated and they started to spread it all over the country. In this way, option (d) is incorrect.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q:
With reference to Swadeshi Movement, consider the following statements :
1. It contributed to the revival of the indigenous artisan crafts and industries.
2. The National Council of Education was established as a part of Swadeshi Movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2019. Swadeshi Movement was complementary to 'Boycott' movement. With the boycott of foreign goods, the use of 'Swadeshi' or indigenous goods increased. The Swadeshi and Boycott Movement contributed a lot to the revival of the 'indigenous artisan crafts and industries. It promoted the establishment of Swadeshi industries - Textile mills, banks, chemical works and insurance companies, Swadeshi stores were opened. National education and Indian languages were encouraged. The National Council of Education was established as a part of Swadeshi Movement.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: The British journalist H.W. Nevinson was associated with:
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2014. Henry Woodd Nevinson was a British journalist and was related to the Swadeshi Movement. Nevinson’s brief was to “discover the causes of the present discontent and to report, without prejudice the opinions of leading Indians as well as offi cials.” Nevinson travelled across India for four months, and his reports were carried by Manchester Guardian, Glasgow Herald, and Daily Chronicle. He re-edited these pieces into a book. 'The New Spirit in India'.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.q: Who among the following had founded the ‘Indian Society of Oriental Art’ to revive ancient art traditions of India?
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2007. First Indian artist to gain international recognition, Abanindranath Tagore (which was initiated by E.B. Havell) was the principal artist and founder of ‘Indian Society of Oriental Art’. His elder brother Gaganendranath Tagore was also artists. He was a major exponent of Swadeshi values in Indian art and inspired the new life in Indian School of Art.]
Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movemen.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.q:
“A graduate at 18, professor and associate editor of the Sudharak at 20, Secretary of the Sarvajanik Sabha and of the Provincial Conference at 25, Secretary of the National Congress at 29, leading witness before an important Royal Commission at 31, Provincial legislator at 34, Imperial legislator at 36, President of the Indian National Congress at 39. a patriot whom Mahatma Gandhi himself regarded as his master”.
This is how a biographer describes:
Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1997] Gopal Krishna Gokhale was born on May 9, 1866 A.D., in Ratnagiri (Maharashtra). He graduated from Elphinstone College in 1884 A.D. and was appointed a professor of Political economy and History at Ferguson College in Poona. Gokhale became as a protege of social reformer Mahadev Govind Ranade. He was a member of the Deccan Education Society. Gokhale fought for decades to obtain greater political representation and power over public affairs for common Indians. He first joined Congress in 1889 A.D. at the Bombay session. Gokhale became a member of the Bombay Legislative Council and then the Imperial Legislative Council. Gandhiji often referred to Gokhale as ‘Mahatma.’ He was the political mentor of Gandhiji.
Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.topic: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.q: Gopal Krishna Gokhale presided over the session of Congress in
Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2004, U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2003] Benaras Session of INC in 1905 A.D. was presided over by Gopal Krishna Gokhale. He founded Servants of India Society in 1905 A.D.
Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.topic: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.q: Who presided over the Benaras Session of the Indian National Congress in 1905:
Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1999] See the explanation of above question.

Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.q: Which of the following leaders presided over the Congress Session at Calcutta in 1906?
Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.explanation: [44th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2000] In 1906 A.D., Congress was in real danger of splitting into two groups. The extremists were more popular than the moderates. Before this session, the extremists would have taken over Congress had they elected a leader among them. But it was not done. The moderates were politically intelligent. In 1906 A.D., the session at Calcutta was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji. The moderates had chosen Naoroji to preside Congress. Naoroji, 'the Grand old man of India,' was respected by both moderates and extremists alike. In this session, the Congress adopted Swaraj as the goal of Indian people. Moderates toned down the resolution in a compromised state and made it self-Government meant obtaining the self-governing British colonies.”
Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.topic: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.q: At the Calcutta Session of the Indian National Congress (INC) held in 1906, the Flag of Swaraj for India was unfurled by
options: More than one of the above

Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.q: Congress passed the ‘Swaraj’ resolution in the year 1905. The purpose of the resolution was
options: right to make a constitution for themselves but it was not done
Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat S.explanation: [53rd to 55th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2011] The Indian National Congress took up the Swaraj call in its Benaras Session, 1905 AD and later in 1906 AD Calcutta session it was fully passed. The main purpose of the resolution was “to serve self-rule’ and boycotting British products and the revival of domestic products and production process of Indian industrialization and better education policy for India.
