It was led by Mahatma Gandhi after the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre and lasted from 1920 A.D. to February 1922 A.D. The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched on 1 August 1920 A.D. and withdrawn in February 1922 A.D. after the Chauri Chaura incident. The factors leading to this movement were Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh massacre and question of Khilafat. The salt march, also known as the Dandi March, lasted from 12th March 1930 A.D. to 6 April 1930 A.D.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Who was the President of the special session of Indian National Congress held in Calcutta in September, 1920 in which the resolution of Non-cooperation Movement was passed?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [Raj. P.C.S. (Pre) 2023. The Special session of the Indian National Congress was held at Calcutta in September, 1920 A.D. under the presidency of Lala Lajpat Rai. Instigated by the British Governments attitude towards the Khilafat movement and the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, a special session was organized specifi cally to pass the resolution of the Non-Cooperation Movement with a demand for Swaraj. It was attended by most of the national leaders of the freedom struggle at the time and almost 300 other delegates from Bihar. The resolution was passed with a great majority. Under the resolution, people were advised to resign from administrative bodies and give up honorary titles, withdraw children from Government Schools and College, refuse to attend offi cials events by the Government; boycott British courts and foreign goods and adopt Swadeshi goods and garments. Gandhi predicted that Swaraj would be attained in a year if the Non-cooperation movement was successful. The movement created ripples within the nation and provided the impetus to the nationalist movement.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Gandhiji launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [48th to 52nd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2008. The Movement was formally inaugurated on the 1st of August, 1920 A.D. by Gandhiji. Non-Cooperation Movement achieved unprecedented success in Western India, Bengal and Northern India. Many distinguished persons like Rajendra Prashad, Motilal Nehru, Lala Lajpat Rai, Vallabhbhai Patel and Rajendra Prasad left their lucrative legal practice and joined the Movement with Gandhiji. At that time, Gandhiji Promised Swaraj within one year (if the movement is implemented effectively).]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: When did Gandhiji give the slogan of ‘Swaraj in a year’?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2012. See the explanation of above question.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: With the failure of 1919 reforms to meet the aspirations of the Indians, the Indian National Congress sought 'Swaraj' or 'Self-government' under the leadership of :
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2017. See the explanation of above question.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: ‘To attain Swaraj in a year’ was the aim of :
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S.( Mains) 2010. See the explanation of above question.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of the Non-Cooperation Movement :
 I. The Congress declared the attainment of 'Swaraj' by all legitimate and peaceful means to be its objective.
 II. It was to be implemented in stages with civil disobedience and nonpayment of taxes for the next stage only if 'Swaraj' did not come within a year and the Government resorted to repression.
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2025. In the Nagpur Session of the Congress in 1920, the Congress changed its objective and declared that ‘Swaraj’ would be achieved through peaceful and legitimate means. Gandhiji said that if non-cooperation was effectively carried out, India would win swaraj within a year. Gandhi planned to run the movement in phases–first through non-cooperation and boycott, and if Swaraj was not achieved or if the government resorted to repression, the movement was to be extended to civil disobedience and non-payment of taxes. Since both statements are factually correct, the correct hence option is (c).]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Which one of the following statements is not correct about Non-Cooperation Movement?
options: (a) The period of the Movement was from 1920 to 1922.
(b) Attainment of Swaraj within a year was its motto.
(c) It comprised the programme of the boycott.
(d) M.A. Jinnah had supported this Movement.
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Main) 2013. The Non-cooperation movement was started on August 1, 1920 AD by Gandhiji. M.A. Jinnah had not supported this movement.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q:
Which of the following statements are not correct regarding the Non-Cooperation Movement in the towns?
 1. Only the upper caste and the rich took part in the movement.
 2. The council elections were boycotted even by the Justice Party of Madras.
 3. Thousands of students left government controlled schools, headmasters and teachers resigned and lawyers gave up their practice.
options: (d) More than one of the above
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation:
[68th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2022. • During the years 1919-1922 A.D., two mass movements emerged in India as a means to oppose British rule: the Khilafat movement and the Non-Cooperation Movement. The non-cooperation Movement marked the beginning of the Gandhian Movement against British colonialism.
• The movement saw significant participation from students, who left government-established schools and colleges in large numbers to join the cause. However, as the movement progressed, some of them began to harbour reservations about Gandhi's program. Hence statement 3 is correct.
• Indian business groups, benefi ting from the emphasis on Swadeshi (indigenous production and boycott of foreign goods) by the nationalists, supported the economic boycott called for during the movement.
• Peasants also actively participated in the movement, but it did lead to confrontations between different castes, particularly between the lower and upper castes.
• Initially, the movement was led by individuals from the middle classes, but as time passed, many of them expressed reservations about Gandhi's approach. Hence statement 1 is incorrect.
• The Non-Cooperation Movement provided an opportunity for the oppressed masses to express their grievances against both the British and their Indian oppressors.
• Women played a crucial role in the movement, participating in large numbers, giving up purdah (seclusion) and contributing their ornaments to the Tilak Fund.
• The movement faced violent reprisals from the police, resulting in the loss of many lives.
• Regarding the Justice Party, which was active in the Madras Presidency, it did not support the Non-Cooperation Movement. The party sought to work within the existing political system and preferred continued British presence. They disagreed with Mahatma Gandhi, particularly due to his praise for Brahminism. Hence statement 2 is incorrect.
• In summary, the Non-Cooperation Movement saw widespread participation from various sections of society, but as it progressed, some segments showed reservations, and it also faced opposition from political groups like the Justice Party.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Gandhiji's Non-Cooperation Movement urged people to avoid alcohol. This resulted in a serious loss of revenue for the government. The government of a province circulated a list of prominent individuals who drank alcohol as a device to persuade people to start drinking again. Name the province.
options: (e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [64th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2018. As a result of Gandhiji's Non-Cooperation Movement, there was a huge decrease in the revenue of the government due to people abstaining from alcohol. Therefore, the Government of Bihar and Odisha released list of great and famous people who used to consume alcohol to publicize and disseminate the benefi cial effects of alcohol on health. This list include Alexander, Julius Caesar, Napoleon, Shakespeare etc.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q:
Consider the following statements:
The Non-Cooperation Movement led to the:
1. Congress becoming a mass Movement for the first time
2. Growth of Hindu-Muslim unity
3. Removal of fear of the British might come from the minds of the people
4. British Government’s willingness to grant political concessions to Indians
Of these statements:
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1996. There are so many achievements of Non-Cooperation Movement. The Non-Cooperation Movement led by Gandhi was a mass Movement which was never seen before. The popularity of the Congress and the Movement increased among the masses. The Non-Cooperation Movement certainly demonstrated that the Indian National Congress commanded the support and sympathy of vast sections of the Indian people. Participation of Muslims in the Movement and the maintenance of communal harmony was also a great achievement. Muslim participation gave the Movement a mass character. People became conscious of their political right. People lost their trust in British Government. They became confi dent of self-reliance. The Government failed to create fear in the mind of the public.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: The title given by the British Government to Mahatma Gandhi which he surrendered during the Non Cooperation Movement was:
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2004, I.A.S. (Pre) 1993. The Kaisar-i-Hind Medal for public service in India was a medal awarded by the British monarch to civilians of any nationality who rendered distinguished service in the advancement of the interests of the British Raj. Mahatma Gandhi was awarded the Kaisar-i-Hind title in 1915 A.D. by Lord Hardinge II. Gandhi returned the medal in 1920 A.D. during the Non-cooperation Movement. Jamnalal also surrendered the title of ‘Rai Bahadur’ during the Non Cooperation Movement.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Who among the following gave up his legal practice during the Non-Cooperation Movement:
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1999. During the Non-Cooperation Movement C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru, Rajendra Prasad, Jawahar Lal Nehru, Vithalbhai Patel and Vallabhbhai Patel gave up their legal practice.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Which of the following statements regarding the Indian freedom struggle is not correct?
options: (a) Mahatma Gandhi was arrested in the year 1921.
(b) Gandhiji withdrew from the Non-Cooperation Movement due to the Chauri-Chaura Incident.
(c) Gandhiji gave his first major public speech at Banaras Hindu University.
(d) More than one of the above
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [68th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2022. Gandhiji was arrested on 10 March, 1922 A.D. after withdrawal of non-Cooperation movement due to the Chauri Chaura incident. Hence only option (a) is not correct, (b) and (c) are correct.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Who of the following supported Non-Cooperation Movement, but could not see it’s result
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2010. The Non-Cooperation Movement started in 1920 A.D. under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi and lasted till 1922 A.D. Bal Gangadhar Tilak supported Non-Cooperation Movement (although he was skeptical about the boycott of Legislative councils elections), but due to his death on the first day of the Movement, he could not see its result.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: In which area was Rahul Sankrityayan active in the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1920?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [56th to 59th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2015. Rahul Sankrityayan, original name Kedar Nath Pandey was active in Chhapra in the Non-cooperation Movement. Local leaders like Rahul Sankrityayan and Nagnarayan spread the message of Non-cooperation in Chhapra, Bihar. Mahapandit Rahul Sankrityayan was born Azamgarh (1893 – 1963 A.D.) UP, who is also called the Father of Hindi Travel literature, was one of the most widely travelled scholars of India, spending forty-fi ve years of his life on travels away from his home.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: The Chauri-Chaura episode took place on:
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2006, U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2002. The Chauri-Chaura incident occurred at Chauri-Chaura in the Gorakhpur district of the then United Province, British India on 4 February, 1922 A.D., when a large group of protesters participating in the Non-cooperation Movement turned violent, leading to police opening fi re. In retaliation the demonstrators attacked and set fi re to a police station, killing all of its occupants. The incident led to the deaths of three civilians and 23 policemen.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: In which state is 'Chauri Chaura', where in February 1922 AD a police station was set on fi re?
options: (e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [67th B.P.S.C. (Pre) (Re. Exam) 2022. See the explanation of above question.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: In which district is Chauri Chaura situated?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2013, U.P. P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2008. See the explanation of above question.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Who provided legal defence to the people arrested in the aftermath of Chauri Chaura incident?
options: (b) Madan Mohan Malaviya and Krishna Kant
(c) Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Khwaja Hasan Nizami
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2025. In Sitaram Chaturvedi’s biography “Madan Mohan Malaviya (Builders of Modern India)”, published by the Publications Division, it is described that after the Chauri-Chaura incident 225 persons were arrested, and the Sessions Judge of Gorakhpur sentenced 170 of them to death. As no local lawyer was coming forward to defend them, all eyes turned to Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya when the cases came up for hearing before the Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court. Though he had been away from the legal profession for nearly a decades, he readily took up the case, prepared the brief, and pleaded on behalf of the accused, as a result of which 151 accused were saved from the gallows (although 19 were executed). He was aided by Krishna Kant.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Due to which of the event, Mahatma Gandhi halted the Non-Cooperation Movement?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [46 th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2004. The infamous Chauri- Chaura incident took place in a small town by the same name near Gorakhpur in Uttar Pradesh in February, 1922 A.D.. This painful event led to the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement by Mahatma Gandhi.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Mahatma Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement because :
options: (a) The support of public was not satisfactory.
(b) Muslims set themselves apart from the movement.
(c) Repressive measures adopted by the British Government.
(d) The violent incident at Chauri- Chaura.
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1990. See the explanation of above question.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Why did Mahatma Gandhi withdraw the Non cooperation Movement in 1922?
options: (a) Most of the leaders were arrested and they were in prison.
(b) Britishers were ready to accept the demands partly.
(c) Because of the violence in Chauri-Chaura.
(d) There was not any chance of success of the movement.
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2006. See the explanation of above question.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Which of the following was the major cause to withdraw the Non-cooperation Movement in 1922 by Mahatma Gandhi?
options: (a) Most of the leaders were arrested and were in prison
(b) British agreed to fulfi ll the demand of the party
(c) He did not see any chance of success of the movement
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P. B.E.O. (Pre) 2019. See the explanation of above question.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: In February 2021 Prime Minister inaugurated which Centenary Celebration?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [M.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2020. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the Chauri Chaura centenary celebration at Chauri Chaura, Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh on 4th February 2021 via video conferencing.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: After which incident, Mahatma Gandhi had called Non-cooperation Movement as his “Himalayan Blunder?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [56th to 59th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2015. Satyagrah in Nadiyad on 14 April during Marshal law after Jallianwala Bagh Massacre was considered by Mahatma Gandhi as his "Himalayan Blunder".]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: During which movement did Gandhiji call for the boycott of Prince Wales?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2024. During the Non-Cooperation Movement, Mahatma Gandhi called for the boycott of Prince Wales' visit to India in 1921 A.D. This movement was a non-violent method of opposing British colonial rule. Under this movement, Gandhi encouraged Indians to boycott British goods and institutions and also protested against the visit of Prince of Wales to India, as he was seen as a symbol of British power.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Where was Mahatma Gandhi when Chauri-Chaura episode took place?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011. The Chauri-Chaura episode took place on February 4,1922 AD, and after hearing of this incident, Gandhiji called up a meeting of Congress Working Committee on February 12, 1922 AD and passed a resolution, which is popularly known as Bardoli resolution, in which Gandhi announced the withdrawal of the Non-cooperation Movement. At the time of Chauri-Chaura incident, Gandhiji was at Bardoli (Gujarat) where he was about to start a mass Civil Disobedience Movement which was also suspended after the Chauri-Chauri incident.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in 1920. Explain when it was ended?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2006, U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1990. See the explanation of above question.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Who tabled a vote of censure against Gandhiji for calling off the Non-Cooperation Movement at the meeting of All India Congress Committee held on February 24, 1922, at Delhi?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2002. The Non-Cooperation Movement was started on August 1, 1920 A.D. and ended on February 12, 1922 A.D. just after the incident of Chauri-Chaura. On February 24, 1922 A.D. the Working Committee met at Delhi which decided to limit all such activities, which is considered as violation of the law although individual movements of violating law can be continued after some permission. The sudden suspension of Non-Cooperation Movement by Gandhi caused a profound shock to his followers. In the same meeting, Dr. Moonje tabled a vote of censure against Gandhi for calling off the Non-Cooperation Movement.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q:
Indicate true sequence of events concerning the postponement of Non-Cooperation Movement :
(1) Police fi ring in Chauri-Chaura
(2) Police station set fi red by violent crowd
(3) Postponement of Movement by Gandhiji
(4) Arresting of Gandhiji
Select your answer of the following code
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [40th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1995. On 4th February, 1922 A.D., the angry residents of Chauri Chaura village gathered in front of the police station to protest against the arrest of their leader, while campaigning against the sale of liquor. However the police opened fi re on the villagers, which angered them to such an extent that they set the police station on fi re killing twenty-three policemen and three civilians. Gandhi, worried about the increasing use of violence, immediately withdrew the Movement. The working committee of the Congress met in February, 1922 A.D. and decided to withdraw the Movement and urged the party workers to get involved in constructive works, such as popularizing khadi, establishing National schools and working towards Hindu-Muslim unity. Gandhi was arrested on 10th March, 1922 A.D. for six years. The Non-cooperation Movement ended. Thus, option (a) is the correct answer.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Who led cultivators in Bihar during the Non cooperation Movement?
options: (e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: Swami Vidyanand was a peasant leader who led several agitations for the redressal of peasants grievances in Bihar. Swami Vidyanand while campaigning for the Non cooperation movement linked up peasant issue with it.

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: A pleader of Bihar who left his lucrative practice during Non-Cooperation Movement was :
options: (e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [60th to 62nd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2016. Rajendra Prasad was a pleader who left his lucrative practice to support Non-cooperation movement. He wrote a book named 'India Divided'.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q:
Choose the correct sequence of the events with the help of codes given below
(1) Chauri-Chaura incident 
(2) Suspensi on of Non-Cooperation Movement
(3) Bardoli Resolutions
 Code :
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation:
[U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2001. The correct sequence of the events is:
(i) Chauri-Chaura incident- February 4th, 1922 A.D.
(ii) Bardoli Resolutions - February 12th, 1922 A.D. 
(iii) Suspension of Non-Cooperation Movement - In February 1922, a meeting of Congress working Committee was held in Bardoli in which Gandhiji decided to terminate the Non-cooperation Movement.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: During 1923-28, the repetition of revolutionary activities in Indian politics was due to :
options: (a) Rising infl uence of leaders like Hardayal and Lajpat Roy
(b) Postponement of Non-Cooperation Movement by Gandhiji
(d) Refusal of Indian demand by Britishers
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [41st B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1996. The suspension of Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922 and the absence of any political activity in the country disappointed the many Nationalistic peoples of the country. They were dissatisfied with the political leadership of Mahatma Gandhi and the way of Non-violence in the freedom struggle. They were inspired by the violent revolutionary activities in Russia, China, Ireland and Turkey and they accepted the violent Revolutionary Movements to overthrow the British rule from India. Thus, this period is considered as the repetition of revolutionary activities in Indian politics.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q:
Consider the following subjects with regard to Non Cooperation Programme :
 I. Boycott of law-courts and foreign cloth
 II. Observance of strict non-violence
 III. Retention of titles and honours without using them in public
 IV. Establishment of Panchayats for settling disputes
 How many of the above were parts of Non-Cooperation Programme?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2025. The Non-Cooperation Programme was officially accepted by the Indian National Congress at the Calcutta Special Session in 1920 and then at the Nagpur Session in December 1920. The Non-Cooperation Programme accepted at the Nagpur Session included the following points – Renunciation of titles and honours; Boycott of law courts and foreign cloth; Establishment of panchayats to settle disputes; and the expectation that people strictly adhere to non-violence. The Congress and Gandhiji had called for a complete renunciation of the titles and honours given by the British government; there was no question of keeping them while merely avoiding their public use. Therefore, Statement III is incorrect. Hence, three out of the four statements are correct, and the correct option is (c).]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Who wrote to Mahatma Gandhi that it was 'a ruthless waste' when foreign clothes were burnt during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2002, U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2003, U.P. P.C.S. (Spl.) (Mains) 2004, U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2010. Rabindranath Tagore gave special importance to constructive program as opposed to agitation and protests, due to which he spoke in his letter to Gandhiji about adopting a constructive program as opposed to burning Holi of foreign clothes during the Non-Cooperation Movement. Rabindranath Tagore called the burning of foreign cloth an 'indiscriminate or callous waste'.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Who among the following had opposed the burning of foreign clothes during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2013. See the explanation of above question.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q:
Which of the following institutions were founded during the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22)
 1. Kashi Vidyapith
 2. Gujarat Vidyapith
 3. Jamia Millia Islamia
 4. Kashi Hindu Vishva Vidyalaya
 Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
 Code :
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2005. The following Institutions were established during the Non Cooperation Movement (1920-22 A.D.):- Kashi Vidhyapith (Varanasi) in 1921 A.D., Gujarat Vidhyapith (Ahmedabad ) in 1920, and Jamia Millia Islamia (Aligarh) in 1920 A.D., which was later transferred to Delhi. Madan Mohan Malviya founded Banaras Hindu Vishva Vidhyalaya in Varanasi in 1916 AD.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Who led cultivators in Bihar during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
options: (d) More than one of the above
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [68th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2022. Swami Vidyanand was a peasant leader who led several agitations for the redressal of peasants grievances in Bihar. Swami Vidyanand while campaigning for the Non-Cooperation Movement linked up peasant issue with it.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: The main outcome of 1921-22 Non-Cooperation Movement was
options: (c) Increase in elected members to the Central Legislative Assembly
(d) Division in the Indian National Congress
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2005. The Non-Cooperation Movement demonstrated that the people were ready to participate in National Movements, with the courage to sacrifi ce and resilience to face adversity and repression. The desire for freedom had developed in the common people. The Movement also demonstrated the involvement of all the sections of society.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q:
With reference to the E.V. Ramaswami Nayakar, which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
 (1) He participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement.
 (2) He left the congress in 1925.
 Select the correct answer using the code given below
 Code
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2023. Erode Venkatappa Ramasamy revered as Periyar, was an Indian social activist and politician who participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement. He left congress in 1925.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Which of the following pairs in is not correctly matched?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1996. Non-Cooperation Movement started in 1920 A.D. under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi and was suspended in 1922 A.D. after the Chauri-Chaura incident. The Civil Disobedience Movement was started in 1930 A.D. Remaining options are correctly matched.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
options: (a) 1940- Lahore Session of Indian National Congress
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation:
[U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2004. The correctly matched list is as follows :
December, 1929 - Lahore Session of Indian National Congress
23 March, 1931 - Execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru
1 August, 1920 - Commencement of Non-Cooperation Movement
April, 1919 - Rowlatt Satyagrah
Thus, only option (b) is correctly matched.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q:
Consider the following statements :
 Assertion (A) : Mahatma Gandhi postponed the Non Cooperation Movement in 1922.
 Reason (R) : The postponement was opposed by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru. 
 Select the correct answer from the code given below: 
 Code :
options: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Mains) 2010. Mahatma Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922, after the violent incident of Chauri-Chaura. The suspension of this movement was strongly opposed by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru. Thus, both assertion and reason are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Who left Patna College with just 20 days remaining for his examination during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
options: (e) None of the above/More than one of the above
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation: [56th to 59th BPSC (Pre) 2016. Born in Sitab Diyara; Saran, Bihar, freedom fighter Jayaprakash Narayan dropped out of Patna College during the Non-Cooperation Movement, with only 20 days left for his exams. After this, he took admission in congress-run Bihar Vidyapeeth.]

Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.q: Who among the following established anti-non-co operation movement assembly?
Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement.explanation:
[Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2019. The Anti-Non-Cooperation Association was started by big businessmen in 1920 AD against the Non-cooperation Khilafat Movement. It was established by Jamnadas Dwarkadas, Purshottamdas Thakurdas, Cowasji Jehangir, Pheroze Sethna and M.C. Setalvad. The businessmen of Bombay felt that the movement would encourage the labour strikes, which in Bombay Presidency turned out to be violent at earlier occasion. 
Secondly, Gandhi did not have that acceptance in Maharashtra region which at that time was still remembered Bal Gangadhar Tilak. CGPSC has deleted the answer in his final answer key.]

Formation of Swaraj Party (1923),Simon C.q:

Civil Disobedience Movement,Gandhi-Irvin.explanation: [Rajasthan P.C.S. (Pre) 2024] The Bijolia Peasant Movement began in 1897 A.D. in the Mewar state of Rajasthan, led by the local farmers. This movement is considered one of the longest peasant movements in India, lasting approximately 44 years. The first phase of the movement was led by Sadhu Sitaram Das, while the second phase was led by Vijay Singh Pathik. Vijay Singh Pathik was a renowned freedom fi ghter and peasant leader. He organized the farmers of Mewar against the excessive taxes imposed by the rulers and raised his voice against these injustices. However, it is not true that Vijay Singh Pathik went to Mahatma Gandhi to provide information about the Bijolia Peasant Movement. On the other hand, newspapers such as Prayag’s Abhyudaya and Calcutta’s Bharat Mitra regularly published news related to the Bijolia Peasant Movement. Therefore, statement (1) is incorrect, while statement (2) is correct.

options: To stop to give rent to the Government
To protect the rights of landlords
Civil Disobedience Movement,Gandhi-Irvin.explanation: [39th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1994] The grassroot leadership of the Eka Movement was Madari Pasi and other low-caste leaders and many small Zamindars. Towards the end of 1921 A.D., peasant discontent resurfaced in some northern districts of the United Provinces—Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur etc. The issues involved were: (i) High rents—50 per cent higher than the recorded rates; (ii) Oppression by Thikedars in charge of revenue collection; and (iii) The practice of share-rents. The meetings of the Eka or the Unity Movement involved a symbolic religious ritual in which the assembled peasants vowed that they would: i. Pay only the recorded rent but would pay it on time; ii. Not leave when evicted; iii. Refuse to do forced labour; iv. No help to the criminals; v. Abide by Panchayat decisions. Consider the following statements regarding the Workers and Peasants Party:
1. The Workers and Peasants Party was formed in 1927 and was given the form of an all India organization.
2. The aim of this party was to work within the Congress so that it could be made a more revolution inclined party and an organisation of the common people.

Civil Disobedience Movement,Gandhi-Irvin.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2024] Labour Swaraj Party was formed in Bengal in 1925 A.D. under congress, which was transformed into Workers and Peasants Party of Bengal in 1926 A.D. Thereafter, in 1927 A.D. Workers and Peasants Party of Bombay Province was formed from Congress Labour Party which emerged within Congress in Bombay Province in 1926 AD. After this, Workers and Peasants Party was formed in United Province in 1928 A.D. and in Punjab by name of Kirti Kisan Party. In the conference of these Workers and Peasant parties of different provinces held in Calcutta in December, 1928 A.D., 'All India Workers and Peasant Party' was formed as pan India organisation. Hence statement 1 is incorrect. The purpose of this party was to work within the Congress to make it a more revolutionary party and to organize the general public. Thus, the second statement is correct. Hence, the correct answer is (d).

The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress (1929) is very important in history, because 
 1. The Congress passed a resolution demanding complete independence.

Consider the following statements regarding the Congress Socialist Party:
 1. In January 1934, the Congress Socialist Party was formed.
 2. Due to his sympathy for socialism, Jawaharlal Nehru formally joined this party.
 Which of the above statements is/are correct?
Individual Satyagraha (1940),Crips Missi.explanation:
[U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2024] In 1934 AD, during the Congress Committee meeting in Patna, the formation of the All India Congress Socialist Party was formally recognized. In October 1934 AD, in Bombay, the party's policies and working principles were determined. In the same year, in Patna, Jayaprakash Narayan was one of the conveners of the All India Congress Socialist Party. Jayaprakash Narayan was elected as the party's General Secretary, and Narendra Dev was chosen as its President.
Jawaharlal Nehru never formally joined this party.

Individual Satyagraha (1940),Crips Missi.q:
With reference to Congress Socialist Party, consider the following statements:
 1. It advocated the boycott of British goods and evasion of taxes.
 2. It wanted to establish the dictatorship of the proletariat.
 3. It advocated a separate electorate for minorities and oppressed classes.
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Individual Satyagraha (1940),Crips Missi.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2015] The Congress Socialist Party was founded in 1934 A.D. as a socialist caucus within the INC. Its members rejected what they saw as the anti-rational mysticism of Gandhi as well as the sectarian attitude of the Communist Party of India towards the Congress party. Infl uenced by Fabianism as well as Marxism, the CSP advocated armed struggle as well as non-violent resistance. The CSP advocated decentralized socialism in which cooperation, trade unions, independent farmers and local authorities would hold a substantial share of economic power. As secularists, they hoped to transcend communal divisions through class solidarity. Hence, option (d) would be the correct answer.

Quit India movement began on 9th August, 1942 A.D. The Committee asserted India’s right to freedom and decided to start a mass struggle with non violent means on the widest possible scale. Addressing the conference, Gandhiji gave the call “Do or Die,” either to get India free or to die in this attempt.  1. Asked Government servants to resign.

2-  Soldiers should refuse to fi re on their countrymen.
3-  Students should leave their study only if they stay fi rm on their decision until freedom is achieved.
4-  The Princes of the Princely States should accept the Sovereignty of their people and people living in their States should declare them as a part of the Indian Nation and accept the leadership of the king only when they take their future linked with the public.
Thus, only 3rd statement is correct.

Individual Satyagraha (1940),Crips Missi.q: Which one of the following observations is not true about the Quit India Movement of 1942?
options: It was led by Mahatma Gandhi.
It did not attract the labour class in general.
Individual Satyagraha (1940),Crips Missi.explanation:
[I.A.S. (Pre) 2011] Quit India Movement of 1942 A.D. was not so non-violent. According to offi cial assessments, in first week 250 railway stations were either damaged or destroyed, and more than 500 post offi ces and 150 police stations were attacked. Heavy violence was used for the suppression of the movement from the ruling party. Mahatma Gandhi himself in 1942 A.D. refused to condemn the violence. He said it was an answer to the huge violence of the rulers. The arrest of the main leaders  (including Gandhiji) before even start of movement had made the movement more aggressive and spontaneous. The movement did not attract the labour class in general (due to reasons like monetary constraints, fear of repression, effect of trade unions etc.) in comparison to other sections of society like students, farmers etc.
Thus, options (a) and (b) are individually not correct.

Individual Satyagraha (1940),Crips Missi.q: After Quit India Movement, C. Rajagopalachari issued a pamphlet entitled “The Way Out.” Which one of the following was a proposal in this pamphlet?
options: The establishment of a “War Advisory Council” composed of representatives of British India and the Indian States
Reconstitution of the Central Executive Council in such a way that all its members, except the Governor General and the Commander-in-Chief, should be Indian leaders
Fresh elections to the Central and Provincial Legislatures to be held at the end of 1945 and the Constitution-making body to be convened as soon as possible
A solution to the Constitutional deadlock

Rajagopalachari devised a proposal in 1944 A.D. called ‘The way out’ for Congress  to offer the league the Muslim Pakistan based on plebiscite (the direct vote of all the members of an electorate on an important public question such as a change in the Constitution). Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Congress Socialist Party:
 1. In January 1934, the Congress Socialist Party was formed.
 2. Due to his sympathy for socialism, Jawaharlal Nehru formally joined this party.
 Which of the above statements is/are correct?
Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.explanation:
[U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2024] In 1934 AD, during the Congress Committee meeting in Patna, the formation of the All India Congress Socialist Party was formally recognized. In October 1934 AD, in Bombay, the party's policies and working principles were determined. In the same year, in Patna, Jayaprakash Narayan was one of the conveners of the All India Congress Socialist Party. Jayaprakash Narayan was elected as the party's General Secretary, and Narendra Dev was chosen as its President.
Jawaharlal Nehru never formally joined this party.

Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.q:
With reference to Congress Socialist Party, consider the following statements:
 1. It advocated the boycott of British goods and evasion of taxes.
 2. It wanted to establish the dictatorship of the proletariat.
 3. It advocated a separate electorate for minorities and oppressed classes.
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2015] The Congress Socialist Party was founded in 1934 A.D. as a socialist caucus within the INC. Its members rejected what they saw as the anti-rational mysticism of Gandhi as well as the sectarian attitude of the Communist Party of India towards the Congress party. Infl uenced by Fabianism as well as Marxism, the CSP advocated armed struggle as well as non-violent resistance. The CSP advocated decentralized socialism in which cooperation, trade unions, independent farmers and local authorities would hold a substantial share of economic power. As secularists, they hoped to transcend communal divisions through class solidarity. Hence, option (d) would be the correct answer.

Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.q: Which one of the following observations is not true about the Quit India Movement of 1942?
options: It was led by Mahatma Gandhi.
It did not attract the labour class in general.
Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.explanation:
[I.A.S. (Pre) 2011] Quit India Movement of 1942 A.D. was not so non-violent. According to offi cial assessments, in first week 250 railway stations were either damaged or destroyed, and more than 500 post offi ces and 150 police stations were attacked. Heavy violence was used for the suppression of the movement from the ruling party. Mahatma Gandhi himself in 1942 A.D. refused to condemn the violence. He said it was an answer to the huge violence of the rulers. The arrest of the main leaders  (including Gandhiji) before even start of movement had made the movement more aggressive and spontaneous. The movement did not attract the labour class in general (due to reasons like monetary constraints, fear of repression, effect of trade unions etc.) in comparison to other sections of society like students, farmers etc.
Thus, options (a) and (b) are individually not correct.

‘Quit India Movement’ was reaction of
 (1) The disappointment of Indians against Cripps Mission.
 (2)  The threat of Japanese attack on India.

 (4)  Due to passing the proposal of August, 1942 by AICC.
 Choose the answer using  the given options
Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.explanation: [Uttarakhand U.D.A/L.D.A. (Pre) 2003] After the failure of Cripps Mission in March, 1942 A.D., it seemed clear that the British Government wanted to continue the partnership with India in Second World War without their consent but was not ready for any sacred agreement. Gandhiji declared in his ‘Do or Die’ speech ‘ that “I do not want to make the instrument either of Russia’s defeat or of  China’s.” But it seemed by spring 1942 A.D. that the struggle was inevitable. Thus, Congress passed Quit India Resolution in August, 1942 A.D. Gandhiji had never provoked to adoption of violent means in his articles. Thus, statement 3 is not correct while the other statements are correct about ‘Quit India Movement.’

 Reason (R)   : There was a massive upsurge of the peasantry in certain areas.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct explanation of A.
Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1999] The involvement of peasants in Quit India Movement made the struggle more violent. This forced Linlithgow to describe the Quit India Movement launched on 9th August, 1942 A.D. as the most serious rebellion since Sepoy Mutiny of 1857. Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Gandhi and Sarojini Naidu were kept in Aga Khan Palace at Pune and the other members of Congress Working Committee (Nehru, Abul Kalam Azad, Govind Vallabh Pant, Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramaiyya, Dr. Syed Mahmud, Acharya Kriplani) were kept in the fort of Ahmednagar. Dr. Rajendra Prasad, a member of Congress Working Committee, was not in Bombay thus, he was arrested in Patna under Bharat Security Rules and sent to Patna (Bankipur) jail.

Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.q: With the news of Gandhi and other Congress leaders arrest in 1942, a riot in Bihar took place, leading to a total breakdown in the rail services. The most affected area was :
Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.explanation: [43rd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1999] On August 9, 1942 Gandhiji and other main leaders of Congress were arrested. Police launched a  suppression cycle to crack down on the Movement. Outraged by the suppression of the police, the public attacked at several places. Police stations, Railway stations and post offi ces were on their targets. Rail lines were uprooted at several places . As a result, rail services were disrupted completely. Medinipur district of Bengal, Baliya district of Uttar Pradesh and Munger district of Bihar were the centers of public anger. The incident of uprooting railway tracks had mostly happened in Bihar. Munger was the most affected district which remained cut off from the outside world for 2 weeks.

All the main leaders of Congress were arrested in the start of the movement. Congress leaders who couldn’t be arrested started to consolidate public secretly. Jaya Prakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, and Aruna Asaf Ali were the main leaders among them.

Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.q: Who among the following women freedom fi ghters was not associated with 'Quit India Movement'?
Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.explanation:
[U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2023] Matangini Hazra was 73 years old when she fell to British bullets, leading a protest March in 1942 A.D. in Tamluk, Bengal during the Quit India Movement.
Kanaklata Barua was an Indian freedom fi ghter and AISF leader. She joined the Mrityu Bahini ('Death Army'), a death squad comprising group of youth from the Gohpur sub-division of Assam in line with Gandhiji's 'Do or Die' call during 'Quit India Movement'. She was shot dead in September 1942 while bearing the National fl ag at age of about 17 in Borangabari, Gohpur, Assam.
Aruna Asaf Ali was an Indian educator, political activist and publisher. An active participant in the Indian Independence movement, she is widely remembered for hoisting the Indian National Flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan (now August Kranti Ground), Bombay (Mumbai) during Quit India Movement in 1942 A.D.
Shanti Ghosh was an active member of the revolutionary group, Yugantar. On 14th December, 1931 A.D. Shanti Ghosh along with Suniti entered the bungalow of a District Magistrate  with a pistol and shot him dead at point-blank range. Hence, option (d) is correct answer.

Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.q:
Assertion(A) : Quit India Movement succeeded in awakening and encouraging people.
Reason (R)  :  People have assimilated the slogan of ‘Do or Die.’
In above context, which of the following is correct?
options: (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.explanation: [Uttarakhand U.D.A/L.D.A. (Pre) 2003] On August 8, 1942 A.D. Gandhi gave the call for Quit India Movement (Bharat Chhodo Andolan). Soon after the arrest of Gandhi, rioting broke out immediately throughout the country and many violent demonstrations took place. Quit India became the most powerful movement in the freedom struggle. Thousands of freedom fi ghters were arrested. He called on all Congressmen and Indians to maintain discipline via non-violence and Do or Die (Karo Ya Maro) to achieve ultimate freedom. Thus, Quit India Movement succeeded in awakening and encouraging people, assimilating the slogan of ‘Do or Die.’

Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.q: After Quit India Movement, C. Rajagopalachari issued a pamphlet entitled “The Way Out.” Which one of the following was a proposal in this pamphlet?
options: The establishment of a “War Advisory Council” composed of representatives of British India and the Indian States
Reconstitution of the Central Executive Council in such a way that all its members, except the Governor General and the Commander-in-Chief, should be Indian leaders
Fresh elections to the Central and Provincial Legislatures to be held at the end of 1945 and the Constitution-making body to be convened as soon as possible
A solution to the Constitutional deadlock
Subhas Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2010] C. Rajagopalachari’s formula was a proposal formulated by Chakravarthi Rajagopalachari to solve the political deadlock between INC and All India Muslim League regarding Independence of India from the British. Rajagopalachari devised a proposal in 1944 A.D. called ‘The way out’ for Congress  to offer the league the Muslim Pakistan based on plebiscite (the direct vote of all the members of an electorate on an important public question such as a change in the Constitution). The formula was opposed even by Congress. Jinnah also rejected the proposal and the talks failed.

Constitutional Development of India.explanation: [39th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1994] Regulating Act, 1773, was passed by the British Parliament for the regulation of the British East India Company’s Indian Territories, mainly in Bengal. The main provisions of the Act were the appointment of a Governor-General of Fort William in Bengal with supervisory powers over the Presidencies of Madras (now Chennai) and Bombay (now Mumbai). The Governor-General had a Council of four who were given the power to cast a vote but no veto. Warren Hastings was appointed the first Governor General of Bengal.

Constitutional Development of India.q: By a Regulation in 1793, the District Collector was deprived of his judicial powers and made the collecting agent only. What was the reason for such regulation?
options: Lord Cornwallis felt that the District Collector’s effi ciency of revenue collection would enormously increase without the burden of other work.
Lord Cornwallis felt that judicial power should compulsorily be in the hands of Europeans. While Indians could be given the job of revenue collection in the districts.
Lord Cornwallis was alarmed at the extent of power concentrated in the District Collector and felt that such absolute power was undesirable in one person.
The judicial work demanded a deep knowledge of India and a good training in law and Lord Cornwallis felt that District Collector should be only a revenue collector.
Constitutional Development of India.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2010] Cornwallis judicial reforms took their fi nal shape in 1793 AD and were embodied in the famous Cornwallis Code. The new reforms were based on the principle of Separation of Powers. Under the infl uence of the eighteenth-century French philosophers Cornwallis sought to separate the revenue administration from the administration of justice. The Collector was the head of the revenue department in a district and also enjoyed extensive judicial and magisterial powers. Cornwallis believed that concentration of all powers in the hands of the Collector in the District retards the improvement as a judge of the Diwani Adalat redress the wrongs done by him as collector or assessor of revenue? Thus, neither the landlords nor the cultivators could regard the Collector as an impartial Judge in revenue cases. The Cornwallis Code divested the Collector of all judicial and magisterial powers and left him with the duty of administration of revenue. A new class of offi cer called the District Judge was created to preside over the District Civil Court. The District Judge was empowered with magisterial and police functions.

Constitutional Development of India.q: The real intention of the British to include the Princely States in the Federal Union proposed by the India Act of 1935 was to
options: Exercise more direct political and administrative control.
Involve the princes actively in the administration of the colony.
Finally effect the complete political and administrative take-over of all the princely States by the British
Use the princes to counter-balance the anti-imperialist doctrines of the nationalist leaders.
Constitutional Development of India.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2002] The real intention of the British to include the Princely States in the Federal Union proposed by the India Act of 1935 was to use the princes to counter balance the anti-imperialist doctrines of the nationalist leaders. Princely States represented approx 25% of the population of India while under the Government of India Act, 1935 out of 260 members 156 were to represent the provinces and 104 to the Princely States in the Upper House and the Lower House consisted of 375 members out of whom 250 were to represent the provinces and 125 to represent the Princely States. In both Houses of the Federal Legislature, the states were given their quota of representation. But the members from the State were not to be elected. Despite such a wide range of provisions, the princely states however refused to join the Federation. They were alarmed by the changing situation in the country caused by the rapid spread of the National Movement. The British Government miserably failed to overcome the opposition of the Indian National Congress, the Muslim League and the princes against the Federal Scheme. So the Federal Scheme was withheld except the establishment of the Federal Court and the Provincial scheme was introduced on 1st April, 1937 causing a drastic change in the pattern of provincial politics.

[I.A.S. (Pre) 2004] First Anglo-Maratha War (1775-82 AD) - The internal problems of the Marathas and the growing ambition of the English brought the beginning of the Anglo-Maratha struggle. The primary cause of the first Maratha war was the interference of the English Government at Bombay in the internal affairs of the Marathas. The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with the Treaty of Salbai signed between the Mahadaji Scindia and the Warren Hastings in 1782 AD. In the Treaty of Salbai, status quo was maintained which gave the British 20 years of peace with the Marathas.
Third Anglo- Mysore War (1790-92 AD)– It was fought between British and Tipu Sultan. British attacked Srirangapatnam with the help of Nizam and Marathas. Under the leadership of William Medows, British defeated Tipu Sultan and they had a treaty in Srirangapatnam in March, 1792 AD. According to this treaty, Tipu Sultan was to give away half of his kingdom and he had to pay 3 crores to British for damages done in the war.
The First Anglo-Burmese War (1824-26 AD) – The first of three wars fought between the British and Burmese Empires in the 19th century. The war which began primarily over the control of northeastern India, ended in a decisive British victory, giving the total British control of Assam, Manipur, Cachar and Jaintia as well as Arakan Province and Tenasserim. The Burmese were also forced to pay an indemnity of one million pounds, and sign a commercial treaty ‘Treaty of Yandabo’.
Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-49 AD)-The Second Anglo Sikh War took place in 1848 and 1849 between the Sikh Empire and the British East India Company.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S.  (Pre) 1990] Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar is considered one of the pillars of the Bengal Renaissance. In other words, he managed to continue the reforms movement that was started by Raja Rammohan Roy. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar initiated the concept of Widow Remarriage and he also opened the doors of colleges and other educational institutions to lower caste students, which were earlier reserved only for Brahmins. For his immense generosity and kind-heartedness, people started addressing him as “Daya Sagar” (ocean of kindness). Major General Sir William Henry Sleeman was a British soldier and administrator in British India, best known for his work on suppression of thuggee. Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade was a judge, politician, writer and reformer of India. He was also an active reformer. He set up the Social Conference Movement, which worked against child marriage, Widows Remarriage, spending heavily in marriages and other social functions. Ranade advocated for widow remarriage and female education. Lord Hastings became Governor-General in 1813. Lord Hastings fi nally decided to suppress the Pindaris. Hastings planned vigorous military preparations to surround the Pindaris from all sides - on the north and east from Bengal, on the west from Gujarat and the south from the Deccan. A massive army of 113,000 men and 300 cannons was divided into two parts - on the northern side under Hastings’ command and the southern under the control of Thomas Hislop. By the end of 1817, the British troops were successful in expelling the Pindaris from Malwa and across the Chambal. In January, 1818 the Pindaris were practically exterminated.
