During one of the interviews for this biography, above statement was said by Mahatma Gandhi to him on the issue of communalism.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Which two leaders visited India and served for social regeneration:
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1992] Both Gandhi and Tilak toured extensively in India for the cause of social development. Tilak was the first national leader who tried to establish a close relationship with the public. Hence, he was a precursor to Gandhi.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
With reference to Lala Lajpat Rai which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. At first he was not in favour of the policy of Non-cooperation but later he joined in favour of Gandhi.
2. Lala Lajpat Rai also participated in the formation of Swaraj Party.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. B.E.O. (Pre) 2019] Initially Lala Lajpat Rai was not in favour of the non-cooperation movement, because he was not satisfi ed with the policies of prayer, persuasion and humility of the Congress. But later in September 1920 AD, the Congress held a special session in Calcutta under the leadership of Lala Lajpat Rai and a resolution was passed to run the Non-cooperation Movement. Hence statement 1 is true. The Non-cooperation Movement was called off by Gandhiji on February 4, 1922 AD after Chauri Chaura incident. Angered by incident C.R. Das and Pandit Moti Lal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party in January 1923 AD. Lala Lajpat Rai also joined this party but in June 1925 AD after death of C.R. Das, Lala Lajpat Rai and Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya left the party. Hence both statements are true.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who was the first Speaker to discard the offi cial wig and presided over the house wearing the Gandhi cap?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2010] G.V. Mavalankar who became the President of Central Legislative Assembly in 1946 AD, was the first speaker who discarded the wig hitherto regarded as mandatory for formal occasions and to presided over the House, wearing a Gandhi cap. When asked by the Britishers in this context, he said: “Your wig is not suitable for this warm climate.” He also became the first Speaker of Lok Sabha.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The first lady, Prime Minister in the world, was :
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Spl) (Pre) 2004] The first lady Prime Minister in the world was Sirimavo Bhandaranaike of Sri Lanka. She became PM of Sri Lanka in July, 1960.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Among the following which is named the official residence of the British Prime Minister :
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [Uttarakhand U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2007] 10 Downing Street is the offi cial residence of British Prime Minister. The Prime Minister of United Kingdom is also known as the ‘First Lord of the Treasury.’ It is located in the city of Westminster.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option :
(i) J.B. Kripalani formed the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party in July, 1952
(ii) P.C. Ghosh and T. Prakasam were associated with Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [In 1951 AD, J.B. Kripalani formed the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party. P.C. Ghosh and T. Prakasam were associated with Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party. In 1952 AD, the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party merged with the Socialist Party and formed the Praza Socialist Party with J.B. Kriplani as the Chairman and Asoka Mehta as the general secretary.]

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: On which of the following date the maker of the constitution of India Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar had died?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1990] Bhimrao Ambedkar was born to Bhimabai Sakpal and Ramji Sakpal on April 14, 1891 AD in Mhow (now Dr. Ambedkar Nagar) Madhya Pradesh. On December 6, 1956 AD he died at his home in New Delhi. He was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna, India’s highest civilian honour in 1990 AD.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who among the following Indian is known as Gurudev?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [38th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1992-93] Rabindranath Tagore was an icon of Indian culture. He was a poet, philosopher, musician, writer, and educationist. He was popularly called as Gurudev. He also became the first Asian to become a Nobel laureate when he won Nobel Prize for 'Song Offerings', the English translation of his collection of poems, Gitanjali, in 1913 AD; he was awarded knighthood by the British King George V. He established Visva Bharati University in 1921 AD.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: In which year, did Rabindranath Tagore die?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Mains) 2006] Rabindranath Tagore was born on May 7, 1861 AD in a wealthy Brahmin family in Kolkata (West Bengal). He was the 14th child of Debendranath and Sharda Devi (They had a total of 14 children of which 13 survived). He passed away on August 7, 1941 AD at his ancestral home in Calcutta (Kolkata).

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who amongst the following had called Rabindranath Tagore as ‘the Great Sentinel’?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Mains) 2010] Mahatma Gandhi called Rabindranath, “The Great Sentinel.” Gandhi believed that he was providing moral support for India’s freedom struggle.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Which one of the following statements is not correct about Rabindranath Tagore?
options: He sang the glories of ancient India and its culture.
He considered Shivaji and Guru Govind Singh as nation builders.
Many of his songs refute the heroism of Marathas.
He favoured the economic aspects of Swadeshi Movement
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2013] Rabindranath Tagore did not favour the economic aspects of the Swadeshi Movement. He portrayed the side effects of the economic aspects of the Swadeshi Movement in his novel ‘Ghare Baire’ with depicting the sourness of Muslim businessmen. Remaining statements are correct.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
Which revolutionary made this statement:
“Avenge the blood of Indian Martyrs. Use your sword to liberate your motherland. Stand up against the entire Anglo-American enemy”.
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2019] "Avenge the blood of Indian Martyrs. Use your sword to liberate your motherland. Stand up against the entire Anglo-American enemy" was the statement of Ras Behari Bose. Ras Behari Bose was an Indian revolutionary leader against British Raj. He was one of the key organizers of the Indian National Army (INA).

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who gives the slogan ‘Jai Jawan’, Jai Kisan’ ?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [38th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1992] ‘Jai Jawan Jai Kisan’ (English: Hail the Soldier, Hail the Farmer) was a slogan given to India by the then Prime Minister of India, Lal Bahadur Shastri in 1965, at a public gathering at Ramlila Maidan, New Delhi.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The present day calendar is based on :
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Spl) (Pre) 2004] Most prevalent calendar in the present-day is Gregorian Calendar. It is used worldwide.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Bhartiya Kisan Sangh was established in which year?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2004] Bhartiya Kisan Sangh was established on 4th March 1979 AD at Kota, Rajasthan by Dattopant Thengdi.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who said, “Freedom is almost within reach, we have to seize it ?”
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation:
[U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2004
U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2002] At the time of Quit India Movement which was started on August 9,1942 AD, Mahatma Gandhi said: “Freedom is almost within reach, we have to seize it.” On the same occasion, Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan of “Do or Die.”

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who of the following had written, “India’s salvation will not be achieved under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi”?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2014] Writing in his much-acclaimed book ‘The Indian Struggle’, Subhash Chandra Bose stated, “Mahatma Gandhi has rendered and will continue to render phenomenal service to his country.” “But,” he added, “India’s salvation will not be achieved under his leadership.”

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Most of the early nationalists considered British rule as an act of providence destined to bring modernisation.
Reason (R): They complained only against "Un-British rule" in India.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2024] A signifi cant portion of the early nationalist leaders viewed British rule in India as a tool ordained by divine will (Providence), which was necessary to bring modernization to India. They believed that British rule facilitated industrialization, education, administrative facilities, and other reforms that paved the way for the development of Indian society. However, their criticism was limited to the "Un-British rule" in India, rather than British rule as a whole. Thus, both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) also correctly explains Assertion (A).

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: “Everything else can wait, but not agriculture.” The above statement is attributed to :
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2006] After Independence, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru stated that “Everything else can wait, but not agriculture.”

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: In which year was the first cloth mill established in Bombay?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2015] The first Indian cotton cloth mill was established in 1818 AD at Fort Gloaster (Kolkata), but it failed. The first successful modern cloth mill was established in Bombay (Mumbai) in the year 1854 AD, was the first cotton textile mill of Bombay. It was established by a Parsi cotton merchant Cowaszee Nanabhoy Davar.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: "Kings are made for Public; Public is not made for the King." Who among the following made this statement during the National Movement?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2015] “Kings are made for Public; Public is not made for the King”. This statement was made by the Grand Old Man of India, the well-known industrialist, educationist and thinker Dadabhai Naoroji.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The founder of Boy Scouts and Civil Guides Movement in India was
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1993] On 1 August, 1907 AD, Robert Baden-Powell took a diverse group of 20 adolescents to Brown Sea Island in Dorsetshire where they set up camp for a fortnight. It was a great success and the start of Boy Scouts and Civil Guides Movement in the United Kingdom. Just after that, in 1908 AD the Boy Scouts Movement began in all over the world with the publication of the first installment of Robert Baden-Powell’s 'Scouting for Boys.' Thus, Baden Powell is considered the founder of Boy Scouts and Civil Guides Movement in India. In India scouting was introduced in 1909 and guiding in 1911.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
In the context of Indian history, the Rakhmabai case of 1884 revolved around 
1.women's right to gain education
2. age of consent
3. restitution of conjugal rights
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2020] Rakhmabai was one of the first practicing women doctors in colonial India. She was also involved with a landmark legal case involving her marriage as a child bride between 1884 AD and 1888 AD. This case led to the enactment of the Age of Consent Act in 1891.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: With reference to Indian freedom struggle, which one of the following statements in not correct?
options: The Rowlatt Act aroused a wave of popular indignation and led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre
Subhash Chandra Bose formed the Forward Bloc
Bhagat Singh was one of the founders of Hindustan Republican Socialist Association
In 1931, the Congress Session at Karachi opposed Gandhi-Irwin Pact
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2003] The First Round Table Conference could not produce any fruitful result. The main reason was the absence of Congress from the Conference. The Government started to convince the Congress to participate in the Second Round Table Conference in 1931 AD. Finally, Gandhiji was convinced to negotiate with the Viceroy Lord Irwin. So Gandhiji and Lord Irwin met on February 19th, 1931 and after discussion of fi fteen days, they signed an agreement on March 5 th, 1931 known as “Gandhi-Irwin Pact.” In 1931, the Congress session at Karachi, approved the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. Thus, statement (d) is incorrect.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
Consider the following statements about Jawaharlal Nehru:
1. He was the president of the Congress Party in 1947
2. He presided over the Constituent Assembly 
3. He formed the first Congress Ministry in United Province before India’s Independence
Of these statements:
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1996] None of the above statements about Jawaharlal Nehru is correct because Jivatram Bhagwandas Kriplani was the president of the Congress Party in 1947 AD. The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly took place on 9th December 1946 AD. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was its interim president. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as its permanent president on 11th December, 1946 AD. He was not included in the first Congress Ministry in United Province before India’s independence.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The statement “I am a socialist and a republican and am no believer Kings and Princes” is associated with
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2011] “I am a socialist and a republican and do not believe in Kings and Princes” this statement is associated with Jawaharlal Nehru.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who among the following has been described as the high priest of Communism in India?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2013] Nehru’s ideas contained analysis and interpretation of socialism, including Marxism. An interesting role in this connection was played by the Publicity Department of the United Provinces which depicted Nehru as a communist. This was done through a pamphlet entitled ‘Communistic Likes and Dislikes.’ In this, Nehru was described as a high priest of Communism in India. But it was a propaganda against Nehru. In fact, the Government wanted to confuse the public about Nehru’s socialistic views. But the high ups in authority advised to stop such attempts and not to identify him with the Communists.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who became champion of socialism and wanted to overthrow British rule, Princely states, Landlordism and Capitalism in 1933?
options: None of the above/More than one of the above
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [Bihar P.C.S. (Pre) 2016] Jawaharlal Nehru was a supporter of socialism. Nehru wanted to overthrow British rule, Princely states, Landlordism and capitalism in 1933 AD. Nehru's socialism was infl uenced by the socialism of the Soviet Union. He visited the Soviet Union in November, 1927 AD.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who one of the following is the biographer of Jawahar Lal Nehru?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2014] Frank Moraes was the biographer of Jawaharlal Nehru.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Ambabai, a woman freedom fi ghter, belonged to which of the following States of India?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [69th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2023] Amba Bai was born in the erstwhile Mysore state (now in Karnataka). She became a widow at very young age. After getting inspiration from Gandhi, she picketed foreign cloth and liquor shops in Udipi during Salt Satyagraha.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The Sarabandi Campaign of 1922 was led by :
options: None of the above/More than one of the above
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [65th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2019] Bardoli in Gujarat (Surat District) became hub of political activities in 1928 AD. Bardoli's Mehta brothers (Kalyan ji and Kunwar Ji) and Dayalji Desai started a movement in support of farmers from 1928 AD. Afterward this movement was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Under the leadership of Patel, Sarabandi Campaign (No-tax) was also launched in 1928. Although the year 1922 AD is incorrectly given in the question.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Of the four forms of political protests mentioned below, which one is derived from the name of the person who used it as a political weapon for the first time?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1996] Boycott word is derived from the name of Captain Charles C. Boycott, an Irish land agent. He was the first one who used this as a political weapon in 1880 AD.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who of the following was sent as a representative of labourers by Indian Government to the Washington Summit of I.L.O. in the year 1919?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2020] International Labour Organisation (ILO) came into existence in the year 1919 AD. N.M. Joshi was sent as a representative of labourers to the first summit of I.L.O. held in the Washington in the year 1919 AD. B.P. Wadia was sent as his advisor to this summit.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Arya Samaj was founded in 1875.
2. ‘Al Hilal’ was published by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
3. Lala Lajpat Rai was not associated with the paper ‘The People.’
4. The famous Presidency College (formerly Hindu College) of Calcutta was established by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.
Of these statements :
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2013] The Arya Samaj was founded by Maharishi Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 AD. ‘Al Hilal’ was an Urdu weekly newspaper published by Maulana Abul Kalam in 1912 AD. The famous Presidency College (formerly Hindu College) of Calcutta was established by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in collaboration with David Hare in 1817 AD. Lala Lajpat Rai was associated with the paper 'The People'. Hence statement (c) is correct.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
Consider the following events and arrange these in chronological order
I. Assassination of Curzon Wyllie
II. Execution of Khudiram Bose
III. Starting of 'Kesari' newspaper by Bal Gangadhar Tilak
IV. Starting of 'Al Hilal' newspaper by Abul Kalam Azad
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation:
[U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Pre.) 2021] Assassination of Curzon Wyllie – 1909 AD
Execution of Khudiram Bose – 1908 AD
Starting of 'Kesari' by Bal Gangadhar Tilak – 1881 AD
Starting of 'Al Hilal' by Abul Kalam Azad – 1912 AD

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Of the following events, which stands third in chronological order?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation:
[U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1996] The correct chronological order of the events is :
Champaran Movement - 1917 AD
Non-Co-operation Movement - 1920-22 AD
Dandi March - 1930 AD
Quit India Movement - 1942 AD
Thus, Dandi March stands at the third position in chronological order.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
Which one of the following is not correctly matched?
Person Associated with
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [71st B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2025] James Augustus Hicky started a weekly newspaper in 1780 named “Hicky’s Bengal Gazette” (also known as “The Original Calcutta General Advertiser”). He was not associated with the Calcutta Chronicle. Dayanand Saraswati wrote the famous work ‘Satyarth Prakash’. E. V. Ramaswamy Naicker (Periyar Ramaswami Naicker) was a leader of the Dravidian movement and the ‘Self-Respect Movement’ in South India, and later joined the Justice Party. Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Phule founded the ‘Satyashodhak Samaj’ in 1873.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
With reference to the British Colonial rule in India, consider the following statements :
1. Mahatma Gandhi was instrumental in the abolition of the system of 'indentured labour'.
2. In Lord Chelmsford's 'War Conference', Mahatma Gandhi did not support the resolution on recruiting Indians for World War.
3. Consequent to the breaking of Salt Law by Indian people, the Indian National Congress was declared illegal by the colonial rulers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2019] Indentured labourers were those who were taken out of India as labourers for fi xed periods in the British colonies. Their condition was like that of bonded labourers. Gandhiji first raised his voice in favour of indentured labourers in South Africa in 1894 AD. In the year 1914 AD, by the Gandhi's Smuts Agreement, the tax of 3 pounds on these labourers ended. After coming back to India, Gandhi negotiated with Viceroy Lord Chelmsford to end the indentured system and fi nally in July 1917 AD the indentured system was banned. Thus statement (1) is correct. After Gandhiji's Dandi March and his breaking of salt law on April 6, 1930 AD, Indians across the country started violating the salt law. In response to this, many Congress leaders and Satyagrahis like Jawaharlal Nehru, Mahadev Desai etc. were sent to prison and Indian National Congress was declared illegal by British rule. Thus statement (3) is correct.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Which lady contributed the most to Indian politics after 1947?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [42nd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1997] Aruna Asaf Ali was an Indian independence activist and a freedom fi ghter. She participated in the Quit India Movement from underground. After India’s independence, she became associated with the left socialist group, which merged with the Communist Party of India in 1955 AD.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: “It will be our blunder if we leave people of Bihar and their Government unsafe before the violence and uncivilized attacks of league leaders.” In the year 1946 who told this?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [42nd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1997] The above statement was made by Sardar Patel in 1946, with reference to the riots in Bihar.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who raised the demand of ‘Complete Independence’ for the first time in 1921?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [56th to 59th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2015] Maulana Hasrat Mohani was one of the greatest leaders in India. He fought against the British Government for freedom. Maulana Hasrat Mohani raised the demand for Complete Independence for the first time in 1921.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who has hailed Mohd. Ali Jinnah most responsible for the partition of India?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Mains) 2002] Lord Mountbatten (1947-48) hailed Mohd. Ali Jinnah most responsible for the partition of India. Lord Curzon was the Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905. Lord Linlithgow was the Viceroy of India from 1936 to 1943. Lord Irwin was appointed as the Indian Viceroy in April, 1926 and continued his offi ce till 18 April 1931.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who amongst the following presided over the All Parties Muslim Conference held in Delhi on 31st December, 1928?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2015] Aga Khan, also known as Maulana Sultan Mohammed Shah presided over the All Parties Muslim Conference in Delhi from December 31, 1928 AD to 1 January 1929 AD. All India Muslim Conference was set up under the leadership of Aga Khan and demanded separate electorates for Muslims.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The Banaras Session of August, 1923 of the Hindu Mahasabha was presided over by :
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [43rd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1999] The Banaras Session of August, 1923 AD of the All India Hindu Mahasabha was presided over by Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya, which was attended by around 1500 delegates including Hindus, Jains, Sikhs and Parsis.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who is considered as the creator of Modern Bihar?
options: None of the above/More than one of the above
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [65th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2019] Sachchidananda Sinha was an Indian lawyer, parliamentarian & journalist. He was born in Arrah, then Bengal Presidency (in present-day Bihar). He began a movement for a separate province of Bihar with a small group of people. It was realized in 1912 AD with the formation of the Bihar (carved out of Bengal presidency).

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Identify the years those are closest to the founding of the Communist Party of India and the RSS respectively.
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [56th to 59th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2015] Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) was founded on September 27, 1925 AD in Nagpur by Keshav Baliram Hedgewar, while Communist Party of India was founded in December 1925 AD in Kanpur. Atal Bihari Vajpayee is the first Swayamsevak to become Prime Minister of India.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The real name of the ‘Frontier Gandhi’ is :
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [43rd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1999] Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan was a Pashtun independence activist and a spiritual leader nicknamed as “Frontier Gandhi” due to his political activities and close association with the Indian leader, Mahatma Gandhi. He was a lifelong pacifi st who advocated non-violent opposition and founded the Khudai Khidmatgar to protest against the British-controlled army using peaceful protests and political activism. He was awarded Bharat Ratna in 1987.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who is known as 'Frontier Gandhi'?
options: None of the above/More than one of the above
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [67th B.P.S.C. (Pre) (Re. Exam) 2022] See the explanation of the above question.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who among the following is popularly known as the ‘Frontier Gandhi?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2013] See the explanation of the above question.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who among the following are known as 'Bombay Trimurti'?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2017] Pherozeshah Mehta, K.T. Telang and Badruddin Tyabji were known as the 'Bombay Trimurti'. Together, in 1885 A.D., they founded Bombay Presidency Association.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: What was the name of the movement started by Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan against British?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2016] Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi) had organized a volunteer brigade 'Khudai Khidmatgars' popularly known as the 'Red Shirts' who were pledged to the freedom struggle and non-violence during civil Disobedience Movement.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: 'Khudai Khidmatgar' (Servants of God) was established by:
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2024] See the explanation of above question.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
Who of the following attacked on Dr. B.R. Ambedkar by saying:
Ambedkar has had his leadership thrust upon him by a benign British Government because his services were necessary to embarrass the Nationalist leaders.’
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2000] Dr. B.S. Moonje was a Hindu nationalist leader. He made the above-statement in 1932 AD, due to the demand for a separate electorate for Dalits raised by B.R. Ambedkar.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: How did the study of history help in creating a feeling of nationalism in India towards the end of the 19th century?
options: By urging people to struggle and change the miserable conditions of life under the British rule
By reinterpreting history and refuting the British portrayal of Indians as backward, primitive and incapable of governing themselves
By writing about India's glorious past and urging people to take pride in their achievements
More than one of the above
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [68th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2022] The study of history helped in creating a feeling of nationalism in India towards the end of 19th century by -- Urging people to struggle and change the miserable conditions of life under British rule.- Reinterpreting history and refuting the British portrayal of Indians as backward, primitive and incapable of governing themselves.- Writing about India's glorious past and urging people to take pride in their achievements.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The native State of Tripura became involved in the Freedom Movement early in the 20th century because:
options: The kings of Tripura were always anti-British
The Bengal revolutionaries took shelter in Tripura
The tribes of the state were fi ercely freedom loving
There were already some groups fi ghting against the kingship and its protector, the British
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2000] King of the princely State of Tripura involved educated Bengalis in his administration. Due to pressure from the Britishers in the early twentieth century, some of the Bengal revolutionaries had taken shelter in Tripura, which resulted in the expansion of Independence Movement in Tripura.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Rajendra Prasad belonged to :
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [44th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2000] Dr. Rajendra Prasad was born on December 3, 1884 in Ziradei village in Siwan district of Bihar. He was the first President of Independent India. He was the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly that drafted the Constitution.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Women Saint Daya Bai was a disciple of –
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 2018] Women saint Daya Bai was a disciple of Saint Charandas. She wrote a book named 'Dayabodh'.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The great poet Rabindranath Tagore emerged as a great painter, when he was
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2001] Great poet Rabindranath Tagore emerged as a great painter at the age of 70 years. Tagore was the first Indian artist to exhibit his works in 1930 across Europe, Russia, and the United States of America, earning him critical acclaim in the West.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
Consider the following statements :
1. St. Francis Xavier was one of the founding members of the Jesuit Order.
2. St. Francis Xavier died in Goa and a church is dedicated to him there.
3. The Feast of St. Francis Xavier is celebrated in Goa each year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre.) 2021] St. Francis Xavier arrived in Goa in 1542 AD. He was instrumental in spread of Christianity in India and was one of the founding members of Jesuit order. He died on December 3,1552 on a Shangchuan Island (China). Hence statement 2 is incorrect. The feast of St. Francis Xavier is celebrated every year on 3rd December in Goa.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Jagat Narain Lal was sent to :
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [45th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2001] Jagat Narain Lal was sent to Hazaribagh Jail during the freedom struggle. After the release of Jagat Narain Lal on July 14, 1929 AD, Rajendra Prasad addressed a meeting in Gulabbag, Patna.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The Samadhis of Kasturba and Mahadev Desai are situated in the premises of :
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011] The Samadhis of Kasturba and Mahadev Desai are situated in the premises of Aga Khan Palace, Pune.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The tomb of Kasturba Gandhi is situated in the premises of :
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2008] See the explanation of the above question.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Who among the following was the author of the offi cial history of Congress?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2002] Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was a nationalist and an important leader of the freedom struggle. He was the author of the offi cial history of Congress and 'Gandhi and Gandhism'. He is famous for his defeat by Subhash Chandra Bose in congress session of Tripuri, 1939 AD.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: During the colonial period in India, what was the purpose of the Whitley Commission?
options: To review the fi tness of India for further political reforms
To report on existing conditions of labour and to make recommendations
To draw up a plan for fi nancial reforms for India
To develop a comprehensive scheme for Civil Services in India.
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2003] The Royal Commission, better known as the Whitley Commission, was asked to report and make recommendations on “the existing conditions of Labour in industrial undertakings and plantations in British India, on the health, effi ciency and standard of living of the workers and on the relations between employers and employees.”

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: What was the common relationship between Katherine Mayo, Aldous Huxley, Charles Andrews and William Digby?
options: They wrote commentaries on the condition of India during the British rule
They were supporters of the Indian National Movement
They were opponents of the Indian National Movement
They were friends of Mahatma Gandhi
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [56th to 59th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2015] Katherine Mayo was an American historian and nativist known for her polemical book Mother India (1927). Aldous Huxley was an English writer and philosopher. Charles Freer Andrews was a social reformer in India. He was also one of the best friends of Mahatma Gandhi. William Digby (May 1, 1849 - 29 September, 1904) was a British author and journalist. The common relationship between all of them is that they wrote commentaries on the condition of India during the British rule.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The year of Bengal Famine in which millions of people died is :
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2013] The Bengal Famine of 1943 AD was a large famine in Bengal, a State in British-ruled India, claiming the lives of approximately 3.0 million people.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: To establish global peace and cooperation among the peoples, which of the following concepts was introduced by Jawaharlal Nehru?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [46 th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2004] The first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, played a crucial role in setting the national agenda. He introduced the concept of Non-Alignment to establish peace and cooperation among people. The three major objectives of Nehru’s foreign policy were to preserve the hard-earned sovereignty, protect territorial integrity and promote rapid economic development. Nehru wished to achieve these objectives through the strategy of Non-Alignment. The roots of Non-Alignment Movement (NAM) goes back to the friendship between three leaders – Yugoslavia’s Josip Broz Tito, India’s Jawaharlal Nehru, and Egypt’s leader Gamal Abdel Nasser. Indonesia’s Sukarno and Ghana’s Kwame Nkrumah strongly supported them. These fi ve leaders came to be known as the fi ve founders of NAM. The first non-aligned summit was held in Belgrade in 1961.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Which part of India remained under Portuguese control after 15th August, 1947?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2010] After 15 th August, 1947 AD, Goa remained under Portuguese control. In 1955 AD America supported the claim of the Portuguese Government over Goa. Operation Vijay was conducted by Indian forces to free Goa from Portuguese control. The armed action which involved the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force was a decisive victory for India, ending approximately 450 years of Portuguese rule in India on 19th of December, 1961 AD.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Against which colonial power did the freedom struggle have to continue in India even after 15 August, 1947?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [Uttarakhand Lower Sub. (Pre) 2010] See the explanation of the above question.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Which of the following statements is not true for Jawaharlal Nehru?
options: He was infl uenced by Socialism.
He was infl uenced by British liberalism.
He was infl uenced by Mahatma Gandhi.
He was infl uenced by German Nationalism.
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Mains) 2006] The first Prime Minister of India Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru was infl uenced by socialism, British liberalism and also by the thoughts of Mahatma Gandhi, but he was not infl uenced by the German Nationalism. His famous books, articles, and speeches showed his socialist views.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Which one of the following was not a dominant caste in Bihar during the pre-independent period?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [46th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2004] During the Pre-independence period, in Bihar Bhumihar, Rajput and Kayasthas were the dominant castes while Kurmi caste was not a dominant caste.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lord Mountbatten was the Viceroy when Shimla Conference took place.
2. Indian Navy Revolt, 1946 took place when the Indian sailors in the Royal Indian Navy at Bombay and Karachi rose against the Government.
Which one of the statements given above is/are correct?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2005] Lord Wavell was the Viceroy of India when Shimla Conference took place. Thus, statement 1 is false. One of the most spectacular episodes of the intense revolt against the British Raj was the uprising of the sailors of the British Indian Navy in 1946 AD. On February, 18 the sailors and shipmen of the Royal Indian Navy battleship 'HMIS Talwaar,' who were at the time posted to the Bombay harbour, went on strike. They were protesting against the bad food and adverse conditions. After the assurance of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel On 24 February, 1946 AD, the rebels were ready to surrender. Thus, statement 2 is correct.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar founded the Bethune School at Calcutta with the main aim of encouraging education for women.
2. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay was the first graduate of the Calcutta University.
3. Keshav Chandra Sen’s campaign against sati led to the enactment of law to ban sati by the then Governor-General.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2005] Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar encouraged women's education and opened 35 women's schools in Bengal. Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was the first secretary of Bethune School and its management committee was formed under his chairmanship. Thus statement 1 is correct. The famous Bengali novelist, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay was one of the first two graduates from Calcutta University in 1858. Thus, statement 2 is also correct. Due to the campaign of Raja Ram Mohan Roy against Sati system, Governor-General Lord William Bentinck banned the Sati system by The Bengal Sati Regulation, 1929. Thus, statement 3 is incorrect and the desired answer will be option (b).

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: Which among the following events happened earliest?

Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2018] Neeldarpan is a Bengali-language play written by Dinabandhu Mitra. The atrocities of Indigo plantation owners have been clearly described in this book. Satyendra Nath Tagore was the first Indian to qualify for the Civil Service Examination in 1864 AD. Bankimchandra Chatterjee wrote Anand Math in 1880, (published in 1882) the story of which is based on the Sanyasi revolt (1763-1800 AD). Dayanand Saraswati founded Arya Samaj in April 1875 in Bombay with the objective of re-establishing the ancient Vedic religion in pure forms.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [47th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2005] Abul Kalam Azad was the scholar related to Deoband. He published Mazameen Al-Nadwa magazine. He also served as the president of Congress from 1940 AD to 1946 AD. 'India Wins Freedom' is his famous book.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Spl) (Pre) 2008] The first Industrial Policy in independent India was propounded on April 6, 1948 AD in the proposal of industrial policy. The concept of a mixed economy for India was first framed in this policy. Under this, the public and private sectors were divided, and both were allocated different industries. The main aspect of the Industrial policy of 1948 AD was that it made an attempt to clarify the role of the public and private sector in industrial development.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The first communist Government of India was established in the province of:
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2010] The first Communist Government of India was established in the province of Kerala in 1957 AD.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.R.O./A.R.O. Elamkulam Manakkal Sankaran Namboodiripad was an Indian Communist politician and theorist, who served as the first Chief Minister of Kerala in 1957–59 AD and then again in 1967–69 AD.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [Uttarakhand U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2007] In India Teacher’s Day is celebrated on 5 September on the birthday of 2nd President and educationist Dr. Sarvapalli Radha Krishnan. World Teachers' Day is celebrated on 5 October.

Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. Modern History : Miscellaneous.q: The political strategy Struggle-Truce-Struggle or S-T-S came into prominence with a call for
Modern History : Miscellaneous.explanation: [70th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2024] The "Struggle-Truce-Struggle" (S-T-S) strategy, employed by Mahatma Gandhi during his participation in Indian freedom movement, involved a cyclical approach of alternating between phases of active resistance (struggle), temporary truces or negotiations, and resuming the struggle with renewed determination if the objectives remained unfulfi lled. Although BPSC has deleted this question in its fi nal answer key as it has accepted that during civil disobedience movement this strategy was most prominently used.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2015] Bipin Chandra was a historian of modern India. He wrote ‘Indian National Movement: The Long-Term Dynamics.’

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.q: Who is the author of the book “Out of Print: Newspapers, Journalism and the Business of News in the Digital Age”?
Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2012] The author of the book “Out of Print: Newspapers, Journalism and the Business of News in the Digital Age” is Professor George Brock.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2006] The book ‘Mother India’ was written by Catherine Mayo. ‘Unhappy India’ is the masterpiece of Lala Lajpat Rai, ‘Geeta Rahasya’ of Bal Gangadhar Tilak and ‘Memories of My Life and Times’ of Bipin Chandra Pal.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.q: Poet Iqbal, who wrote “Sare Jahan Se Achcha” was related to which State?
Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2003] Muhammad Iqbal, the renowned poet and lawyer by profession, was born on November 9, 1877 in Sialkot, Punjab of British India. He wrote “Saare Jahan Se Achcha” but later he joined Muslim League.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2004, M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1999] See the explanation of the above question.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1998] “Mazhab Nahi Sikhata Aapas Mein Bair Rakhna” is a portion of the famous song “Saare Jahan Se Achcha” written by Muhammad Iqbal.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.q: What was the name of the poet, who wrote the popular poem "Firangiya" in Bhojpuri against 'British Colonialism'?
Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Pre.) 2021] Manoranjan Prasad Singh wrote poem "Firangiya" in Bhojpuri against British Colonialism.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.q: The pamphlet entitled ‘Why I Am an Atheist?’ was written by :
Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2010] The pamphlet entitled ‘Why I Am an Atheist?’ was written by Bhagat Singh.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.q: The song ‘Amar Sonar Bangla’ written during the Swadeshi Movement of India inspired the liberation struggle of Bangladesh and was adopted as the National Anthem of Bangladesh. Who wrote this song?
Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2007] The song ‘Amar Sonar Bangla’ was written and composed by Rabindranath Tagore during the Bengal partition movement of 1905. The music of this song is inspired by the melody of the Hymn ‘Ami Kothay Pabo Tare’ written by Gagan Harkara. Bangladesh adopted the first 10 lines of this song as its National Anthem. Syed Ali Ahsan translated the song into English. It is noteworthy that Rabindranath Tagore wrote the National Anthem of India ‘Jana Gana Mana’. He is the only poet in the world whose compositions have been adopted as the national anthem of the two countries.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.q: Who composed ‘Jana Gana Mana’?
Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1990] See the explanation of the above question.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.q: Who of the following is the author of a collection of poems called ‘ Golden Threshold’?
Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2009] Sarojini Naidu is the author of the collection of poems called ‘The Golden Threshold.’

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.q: Who among the following is associated with ‘Songs from Prison’, a translation of ancient Indian religious lyrics in English?
Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre.) 2021] Songs from Prison is a book of translations from Sanskrit hymns and lyrics, from the Upanishads and other scriptures. Mahatma Gandhi made these translations during his incarceration in Yeravada Prison in 1932.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.q: Who is the author of the book, “Landmarks in Indian Constitutional and National Development”?
Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [Uttarakhand U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2007] The book “Landmarks in Indian Constitution and National Development” is a masterpiece of Gurmukh Nihal Singh. He also served as the first Governor of Rajasthan from 1956 to 1962.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.q: The editor of “Congress Presidential Addresses,” was:
Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [Uttarakhand U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2007] The editor of “Congress Presidential Addresses” was G.A. Natesan. The book was published in two parts. The first part of the book compiled the presidential addresses of Congress from 1885 to 1910 while the other part compiled the presidential addresses of Congress from 1911 to 1934.

Magazines, Books and Their Authors.q: ‘The Roots of Ancient India’ was written by
Magazines, Books and Their Authors.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2016] ‘The Roots of Ancient India’ was written by Walter Ashlin Fairservis Jr. In this book, the culture of inhabitants of Asian subcontinent during the prehistoric era is graphically introduced.

Art and Culture.q: The first Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, a music training school, was set up in 1901 by Vishnu Digambar Paluskar in
Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2025] Gandharva Mahavidyalaya was one of the earliest institutions established for the organized training in classical music through a modern method. Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar founded the first Gandharva Mahavidyalaya in Lahore in 1901, which was then a part of undivided India. Paluskar sought to take music education out of the exclusive hereditary domain of professional musicians and make it accessible to the wider public.

Art and Culture.q: In the context of the cultural history of India, a pose in dance and dramatics called Tribhanga has been a favourite of Indian artists from ancient times till today. Which one of the following statements best describes this pose?
options: One leg is bent and the body is slightly but oppositely curved at waist and neck
Facial expressions, hand gestures and make-up are combined to symbolize certain epic or historical characters
Movements of body, face and hands are used to express oneself or to tell a story
A little smile, slightly curved waist and certain hand gestures are emphasized to express the feelings of love or eroticism.
Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2013] Tribhanga (tri-bent pose) is a standing body position or stance used in the traditional Indian sculpture, art and Indian classical dance forms. Tribhanga is literally means three parts break, consisting of three bends in the body; at the neck, waist and knee which gives it a gentle ‘S’ shape. Hence option (a) is the correct answer.

Art and Culture.q:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A) : For education and culture a Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT) was set up in 1979.
Reason (R) : The objective of CCRT was to link education with culture.
Choose the correct answer from the codes given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) (Re-Exam) 2016] Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT) is a premier institution working in the field of linking education with culture. It was established in 1979, by Smt. Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay and Dr. Kapila Vatsyayan. It functions as an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. CCRT's commitment lies to holistic education, encompassing the cognitive, emotional and spiritual development of children. Hence it is clear that both A and R are correct and R is correct explanation of A.

Art and Culture.q: At which of the following places Kumbh Mela is not held?
Art and Culture.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1992] Kumbh Mela is a mass Hindu pilgrimage of faith in which Hindus gather to take a dip in a holy river. It is the world’s largest religious gathering. It is held every third year at one of the four places by rotation: Haridwar, Prayagraj, Nashik and Ujjain. Thus the Kumbh Mela is held at each of these four places every twelfth year. However, U.P. government has changed the name of Kumbh mela (every 12 years) to Mahakumbh and Ardh Kumbh mela (every 6 years) to Kumbh (at Prayagraj).

Art and Culture.q: After how many years is ‘Maha Kumbh’ held?
Art and Culture.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2013] Kumbh Mela is also known as Purna Kumbh takes place every twelfth year at following four places: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, and Nashik. However, U.P. government has changed the name of Kumbh Mela (every 12 years) to Mahakumbh and Ardh Kumbh Mela (every 6 years) to Kumbh (at Prayagraj).

Art and Culture.q: In which place is Kumbh Mela held every twelfth year?
Art and Culture.explanation: [M.P.P.S.C. (Pre) 1995] See the explanation of above question.

Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2002] See the explanation of above question.

Art and Culture.q: ‘Bihu’ is the folk dance of which of the following States?
Art and Culture.explanation: [Uttarakhand U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2007] The Bihu dance is a folk dance from the Indian State of Assam related to the Bihu festival. This joyous dance is performed by both young men and women and is characterized by brisk dance steps and rapid hand movements.

Art and Culture.q: ‘Pongal’ is the festival of which State?
Art and Culture.explanation: [Uttarakhand U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2007] Thai Pongal is a harvest festival of Tamil Nadu celebrated on Makar Sankranti by Tamil people at the end of the harvest season.

Art and Culture.q: South Indian Festival of ‘Onam’ is associated with which of the following?
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S (Pre) 2011] Onam is the biggest and the most important festival of the State of Kerala. It is a harvest festival and is celebrated with joy and enthusiasm all over the State by people of all communities. According to a popular legend, the festival is celebrated to welcome King Mahabali whose spirit is said to visit Kerala at the time of Onam.

Art and Culture.q: ‘Athapoo’ is associated with which of the following festivals?
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S (Pre) 2011] Pookalam, also called Athapoo, is an intricate floral mat laid in the front courtyard by maidens of the house during Onam festival.

Art and Culture.q: ‘Tamasha’ is the famous folk form of musical theatre in:
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2009, U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2006] ‘Tamasha’ is a traditional Marathi folk art form. It includes both singing and dancing forms. It is widely performed by theatre groups within the State of Maharashtra.

Art and Culture.q: The book ‘Venushilpa’ by Chitracharya Upendra Maharathi relates to which of the following form of arts?
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2019] The book 'Venushilpa' by Chitracharya Upendra Maharathi relates to bamboo art. Some of his other major works include 'Vaishali Ke Lichchhavi, 'Buddha Dharma Ka Abhuthan' and 'Indragupta".

Art and Culture.q: Name the holy place in which the main God is different from other three?
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2002] Amarnath, Kedarnath and Vishwanath are related to Lord Shiva while the main deity of Jagannath Dham is Lord Krishna.

Art and Culture.q: Four Mathas established by Adi Shankaracharya are :
Art and Culture.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2010] Adi Shankaracharya was one of the most notable philosophers as well as savants of India. He established four Peethas or Mathas in the four corners of India. The four Mathas established by him are- Jyotirmath or Joshimath in the north, Govardhan Math in Puri in the east, Dwarka Sharda Peeth in Dwarka in the west and Sringeri Sharada Peetham in Sringeri in the south.

Art and Culture.q: In India, many pilgrims travel to Srisailam, which is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, is located in
Art and Culture.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (J) (Pre) 2005] Srisaila Devasthanam, 'Srisaila' is in Kurnool district (Now-Nandyala district) of Andhra Pradesh. Lord Shiva is worshipped here as Sri Mallikarjuna Swamy along with goddess Parvati (Bhramaramba). It is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas (Mallikarjuna).

Art and Culture.q: In which State is the Buddhist site Tabo Monastery located?
Art and Culture.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2010] Tabo Monastery is located in the Tabo village of Spiti Valley, Himachal Pradesh. It was founded in 996 CE in the Tibetan year of the Fire Ape by the Tibetan Buddhist Rinchen Zangpo.

Art and Culture.q: Losoong is a festival which is celebrated in:
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S.(Pre) 2003, U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2002, U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2002, U.P.P.C.S.(Pre) 2001] The Losoong Festival is the most popular festival in Sikkim. It is usually celebrated at the end of the tenth Tibetan lunar month (usually December). It is the most important festival among the Bhutias and Lepcha Tribes in India.

Art and Culture.q: "Wangla Festival" is celebrated in the following state:
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) (Re-Exam) 2016] "Wangla Festival" is celebrated in the state of Meghalaya by Garo tribe. It is a harvest festival that is also called festival of "The Hundred Drums". In this post harvest festival, Misi Saljong (Sun god) is thanked for blessing people with a rich harvest.

Art and Culture.q: Chapchar Kut is a festival celebrated in the State of:
Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2002] Chapchar Kut is a festival celebrated in the State of Mizoram during the month of March.

Art and Culture.q: Ijtima Festival (Mela) is celebrated in
Art and Culture.explanation: [M.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1991] Tabligi Ijtima is an important festival of Muslims in Bhopal.

Art and Culture.q: "Navarathri" is celebrated as Saraswathi Pooja in the following state:
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Re-Exam) (Pre) 2016] Navarathri is celebrated as Saraswati Pooja in all 4 states of Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu & Telangana. In Tamil Nadu first three days of festival are dedicated to Goddess Lakshmi, next three days to Durga and last three to Saraswati. In Kerala Mahanavami is celebrated as Saraswati Pooja, same is the case with Telangana and Karnataka. However, Aayog has accepted (a) Kerala as right answer.

Art and Culture.q: Who was the grandfather of Arjun, the hero of Mahabharata?
Art and Culture.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2005] Vichitravirya was the grandfather of Arjun, who had two sons Pandu and Dhritarashtra. Arjun was the son of Pandu.

Art and Culture.q: What is ‘Kaaba’?
Art and Culture.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2010] Kaaba is a cuboid-shaped building located in Mecca of Saudi Arabia which is the holiest place for Muslims. According to Quran, Kaaba was founded by Ibrahim and his son Ismail. All the Muslims around the world face towards the Kaaba during the Namaz.

Art and Culture.q: What is the Jewish place of worship called?
Art and Culture.explanation: [M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1995] The Jewish place of worship is known as Synagogue.

Art and Culture.q: Where was the first Sanskrit University Chair established?
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Mains) 2007] At the famous Paris University first Sanskrit chair was established at College de France in 1814.

Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2000] Thyagaraja was born in Tiruvarur district, Tamil Nadu. Thyagaraja Aradhana is the annual festival of saint composer Thyagaraja regularly celebrated at Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu.

Art and Culture.q: ‘Sufi Kalam,’ a type of devotional music, is characteristic of:
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1994] ‘Sufi Kalam’ a type of devotional music is characteristic of Jammu and Kashmir.

Art and Culture.q: According to Mimamsa system of philosophy liberation is possible by means of:
Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2005] Mimamsa system of philosophy stresses on the doctrine of “Karma.” It says that liberation is possible by means of performing “Karma.”

Art and Culture.q: “Jagar” is a form of God worship ritual prevalent in :
Art and Culture.explanation: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2006] “Jagar” is a form of ancestor spirit worship practised in the hills of Uttarakhand, (Kumaon Garhwal). It is a medium or way in which Gods and local deities are called or invoked from their dormant stage and asked for favours or remedies for certain problems plaguing the person.

Art and Culture.q:
With reference to Dhrupad, one of the major traditions of India that has been kept alive for centuries, which of the following statements are correct?
1. Dhrupad originated and developed in the Rajput kingdoms during the Mughal period.
2. Dhrupad is primarily a devotional and spiritual music.
3. Dhrupad Alap uses Sanskrit syllables from Mantras.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2012] Dhrupad is the Indian classical music that traces its origin to the chanting of Vedic hymns and mantras. It was originated by King of Gwalior Man Singh Tomar (1486-1516). Hence, Dhrupad was originated way back before Mughal Period. Hence statement 1 is wrong. It is also primarily a form of worship, in which offerings are made to the divine through sound. Thus Statement 2 is correct. Dhrupad is performed in two parts- Alap and Bandish. In the Alap, the singer uses syllables from Sanskrit Mantras. Therefore, statement 3 is correct.

Art and Culture.q: The brothers Umakant and Ramakant Gundecha are:
Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2009] Umakant Gundecha and Ramakant Gundecha, known as the Gundecha Brothers, are leading Dagarvani dhrupad singers. Gundecha Brothers were born in Ujjain into a Jain family.

Art and Culture.q: The author of the ‘Raga Kallpadrum’ is
Art and Culture.explanation: [R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 1992] Rana Hammir authored ‘Sringarhar,’ Maharana Kumbha authored ‘Sangeetraj,’ Radhakrishna authored ‘Rag Ratnakar’ and Krishnanand Vyas authored ‘Raga Kallpadrum.’

Art and Culture.q: The ‘Raga’ which is sung early in the morning is :
Art and Culture.explanation: [Uttarakhand U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2007] Raga ‘Todi’ is sung during the morning while Raag ‘Darbari’ is sung at night, Raag ‘Bhopali during the evening and ‘Bhimpalasi’ is sung in the afternoon.

Art and Culture.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chakiarkoothu form of dance:
1. It is performed by Chakiar caste
2. It cannot be traditionally witnessed by the higher caste Hindus
3. Mizhavu is the accompanying instrument
4. Its theatre form is called Koothambalam
Which of these statements are correct?
Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2000] Chakiarkoothu is an art form in which the stories of Hindu mythology and epics are orally rendered primarily. Only the members of the Chakiar community performed this art form and hence the name Chakiarkoothu. This was performed in temple theatre called Koothambalam. An accompanying artist plays the percussion instrument mizhavu in the background.

Art and Culture.q:
With reference to Manipuri Sankirtana, consider the following statements:
1. It is a song and dance performance.
2. Cymbals are the only musical instruments used in the performance.
3. It is performed to narrate the life and deeds of Lord Krishna.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2017] Manipuri Sankirtana is one of the few important Indian heritage inscribed on the UNESCO representative list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity. It is a form of performing art involving virtual singing, drumming and dancing which are performed in the temples and domestic spaces in Manipur state. Through the performances which exhibit unparalleled religious devotion and energy, the performers narrates the life and deeds of Lord Krishna. So, statements 1 and 3 are correct. Since the Kartal and Pung are also used, statement 2 is incorrect.

Art and Culture.q: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi is related to :
Art and Culture.explanation: [Uttarakhand U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2007] Pandit Bhimsen Joshi was an Indian classical singer of the Kirana Gharana. Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2005] ‘Mohiniattam’ is a semi-classical dance form of Kerala. Women perform it. The word Mohini means a maiden who steals the heart of the onlooker. Art and Culture.q:
With reference to the famous Sattriya dance, consider the following statements:
1. Sattriya is a combination of music, dance and drama.
2. It is a centuries-old living tradition of Vaishnavites of Assam.
3. It is based on classical Ragas and Talas of devotional songs composed by Tulsidas, Kabir and Mirabai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2014] Sattriya dance is one of the eight principal classical Indian dance traditions. Recognized in 2000 as a classical dance by Sangeet Natak Akademi. The Sattriya is the most recent entrant on this list. The Sattriya dance form was introduced by the Great Vaishnava saint and reformer of Assam, Mahapurusha Sankaradeva as a powerful medium for the propagation of the Vaishnava faith. It is a centuries-old living tradition of Vaishnavites of Assam. Sattriya Nritya is accompanied by musical compositions called Borgeet (composed by Sankardeva and Shree Shree Madhavdev among others) which are based on classical ragas.

Art and Culture.q: Which one of the following dances involves solo performance?
Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1997] In the above options, Mohiniattam involves solo performance. Mohiniattam is a classical dance form from Kerala, India. It is considered as a graceful form of dance meant to be performed as solo recitals by women. The Mohiniattam dance focuses mainly on feminine moods and emotions. Usually, the theme of Mohiniattam dance is “sringara” or love. Subtle subjects of love are executed with suggestive abhinaya using subtle gestures, rhythmic footwork and lilting music. The legend of Vishnu as “Mohini,” (the enchantress) forms the core of Mohiniattam dance.

It is one of the eight Indian classical dance forms recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi. Yakshagana is a folk theatre form that combines dance, music, dialogue, costume, make-up, and stage techniques with a unique style and form. This folk theatre style is mainly found in the Karnataka, India. Thus, option (c) will be the correct answer as the second pair is not correctly matched.

Art and Culture.q: Which one of the following was the latest inclusion in the Intangible Cultural Heritage List of UNESCO?
Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2024] The latest cultural heritage of India included in the UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity is Garba, a traditional dance form from Gujarat in December, 2023. Garba is a ritualistic and devotional dance that is performed on the occasion of the Hindu festival of Navaratri, which is dedicated to the worship of the feminine energy or 'Shakti'. Chhau dance, Durga puja in Kolkata and Kumbh mela were included in the UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010, 2021 and 2017 respectively.

Art and Culture.q:
How do you distinguish between Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam dances?
1. Dancers occasionally speaking dialogues is found in Kuchipudi dance but not in Bharatanatyam.
2. Dancing on the brass plate by keeping the feet on its edges is a feature of Bharatanatyam, but Kuchipudi dance does not have such a form of movements.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2012] The first statement is correct as Kuchipudi is a famous folk dance of Andhra Pradesh. It presents more realistic acting occasionally including dialogue spoken by the dancers. Another unique feature of Kuchipudi is the Tarangam, in which the performer dances on the edges of a brass plate, executing complicated rhythmic patterns with dexterity, while sometimes also balancing a pot of water on the head. So, the second statement is incorrect. The correct answer is option (a).

Art and Culture.q:

4. Annamacharya kirtanas are devotional songs in praise of Lord Venkateshwara.

Art and Culture.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2018] Tyagaraja was a renounced composer of Carnatic music, a form of Indian classical music. Tyagaraja composed thousands of devotional compositions, most in Telugu and praise of Lord Rama. He created several new ragas. Annamacharya was a 15th century Hindu saint and is the earliest known Indian musician to compose songs called sankirtanas in praise of the God Venkateshwara, a form of Vishnu.

Art and Culture.q: In Indian architecture, ‘Surkhi’ was introduced by
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2014] The evidence of using ‘Surkhi’ has been found in the architecture built during the Kushana period. Art and Culture.q: Which one of the following is not the factor of ‘Cultural Lag’?
Art and Culture.explanation: [U.P.R.O./A.R.O (Mains) 2014] The term refers to the notion that culture takes the time to catch up with technological innovations and that social problems and conflicts are caused by this lag. According to Ogburn, cultural lag is a common societal phenomenon due to the tendency of the material culture to evolve and change rapidly. Cultural lag is seen as a critical ethical issue because failure to develop broad social consensus on appropriate applications of modern technology may lead to a breakdown in social solidarity and the rise of social conflict.

His tenure as Viceroy was marked by a controversial policy known as the Vernacular Press Act of 1878, which aimed to regulate the Indian vernacular press and limit its freedom of expression. The policies introduced included the Indian Arms Act of 1878, according to which, it was a criminal offence for Indians to carry arms without a license. The Act was discriminatory as it did not apply to the British, Anglo-Indians, Europeans, and certain government personnel. Famine Codes were given by the Famine Commission that was set up in 1878 under the Chairmanship of Sir Richard Strachey (Strachey Commission) during the tenure of Lord Lytton only. The infamous 'Famine Codes,' have been criticized for their handling of the 1876-1878 famine in India, which resulted in signifi cant loss of life. Ilbert Bill on the other hand was introduced in 1883 by Lord Ripon that allowed Indian Judges and Magistrates to try British Offenders in criminal cases at the district level.]

Remaining.q: With reference to revenue collection by Cornwallis, consider the following statements: 1. Under the Ryotwari Settlement of revenue collection, the peasants were exempted from revenue payment in case of bad harvests or natural calamities. 2. Under the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, if the Zamindar failed to pay his revenues to the state, on or before the fi xed date, he would be removed from his Zamindari. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Remaining.explanation: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2024. Under the Ryotwari Settlement of revenue collection, individual peasants (ryots) were directly responsible for paying land revenue to the government and peasants were not exempted from revenue payment in case of bad harvests or natural calamities. There were no explicit exemptions for bad harvests or natural calamities rather sometimes few remissions were provided and their rents were reduced. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect. Under the Permanent Settlement in Bengal, introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793 A.D., 'Zamindars' were established as the proprietors or owners of land. The state’s demand for land revenue was permanently fixed, but under the ‘Sunset clause’, if the Zamindar failed to pay tax due by sunset on a certain date, his Zamindari (landholding rights) would be taken over by the government and auctioned, and the rights would be transferred to the new owner. Hence, statement 2 is correct.]
