Remaining.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was given the honorific title 'Lokmanya' (accepted by the people as their leader) during the Home Rule Movement, when his popularity soared across the nation.
Remaining.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Remaining.q: In which place Khudiram Bose tried to kill Kingsford?
Remaining.explanation: In 1908, Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb at a carriage in Muzaffarpur, attempting to assassinate the Chief Presidency Magistrate Douglas Kingsford.
Remaining.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Remaining.q: Who threw harmless bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly?
options: Bhagat Singh and Chandra Shekhar Azad
Remaining.explanation: On April 8, 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw non-lethal bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi to protest against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Dispute Act.
Remaining.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Remaining.q: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were executed on
Remaining.explanation: Bhagat Singh, Shivaram Rajguru, and Sukhdev Thapar were hanged by the British in the Lahore jail on March 23, 1931, which is now commemorated as Martyrs' Day (Shaheed Diwas).
Remaining.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Remaining.q: Who is related to 'Chittagong Armoury Raid'?
Remaining.explanation: The Chittagong Armoury Raid, also known as the Chittagong Uprising, was an attempt on 18 April 1930 to raid the armory of police and auxiliary forces in Chittagong, Bengal, led by Surya Sen.
Remaining.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Remaining.q: The Indian Home Rule Society in London was started by
Remaining.explanation: The Indian Home Rule Society was founded in London in 1905 by Shyamji Krishna Varma, with support from Bhikaji Cama and Dadabhai Naoroji, to promote the cause of self-rule in India.
Remaining.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Remaining.q: The ‘Indian Home Rule Society’ was founded in :
Remaining.explanation: The Indian Home Rule Society was founded by Shyamji Krishna Varma in 1905 in London.
Remaining.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Remaining.q: Who got an opportunity to become Professor of Indian Philosophy in the University of California in 1911?
Remaining.explanation: Lala Hardayal, an Indian nationalist revolutionary, moved to the United States and briefly served as a Professor of Indian Philosophy and Sanskrit at Stanford University and the University of California.
Remaining.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Remaining.q:
Consider the following freedom fi ghters : 
 1. Barindra Kumar Ghosh
  2. Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee
 3. Rash Behari Bose
 Who of the above was/were actively associated with the Ghadar Party?
Remaining.explanation: Rash Behari Bose was actively associated with the Ghadar Party and helped organize the Ghadar Mutiny. Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee were associated with the Anushilan Samiti and HRA respectively.
Remaining.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Remaining.q: Where was the Ghadar Party established?
Remaining.explanation: The Ghadar Party was an international political movement organized by Indians to overthrow British rule in India. It was founded in 1913 in San Francisco, United States of America.
Remaining.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Remaining.q: Sardar Udham Singh killed whom?
Remaining.explanation: Sardar Udham Singh assassinated Michael O'Dwyer in London in 1940. O'Dwyer was the Lieutenant Governor of the Punjab in India at the time of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
Remaining.topic: Revolutionary Movements In and Outside India

Remaining.q: When did the Anti-Partition Movement begin with a massive demonstration at the Town Hall, Calcutta?
Remaining.explanation: The Anti-Partition Movement (Swadeshi Movement) officially began on August 7, 1905, with a massive meeting at the Calcutta Town Hall where the Boycott resolution was passed.
Remaining.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Remaining.q: The Lieutenant Governor of Bengal at the time of Partition of Bengal was :
Remaining.explanation: Sir Andrew Fraser was the Lieutenant Governor of Bengal from 1903 to 1908, covering the period when the Partition of Bengal was executed by Viceroy Lord Curzon.
Remaining.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Remaining.q: Who has said about Bengal Partition. "The partition announcement fell like a bomb shell"?
Remaining.explanation: Surendranath Banerjee famously remarked that the announcement of the Partition of Bengal "fell like a bomb shell" upon the people.
Remaining.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Remaining.q: Who painted the famous image of Bharat Mata to visually associate the identity of India, as a Nation?
Remaining.explanation: The iconic painting of 'Bharat Mata' was created by Abanindranath Tagore in 1905 during the Swadeshi Movement, visually conceptualizing India as a mother goddess.
Remaining.topic: Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement

Remaining.q: At the Calcutta Session of the Indian National Congress (INC) held in 1906, the Flag of Swaraj for India was unfurled by
Remaining.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji unfurled the flag of Swaraj and demanded it from the Congress platform during his presidential address at the Calcutta session in 1906.
Remaining.topic: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

Remaining.q: Dadabhai Naoroji was formally known as :
Remaining.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was widely and affectionately known as the 'Grand Old Man of India' due to his immense contributions to the early Indian nationalist movement.
Remaining.topic: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

Remaining.q: In which session was the Congress divided into Moderates and Extremists?
Remaining.explanation: The Indian National Congress split into the Moderates and Extremists at the Surat Session in 1907. This event is historically known as the 'Surat Split'.
Remaining.topic: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

Remaining.q:
Choose the correct option after reading following statements :
Statement-I : In 1907, Congress's Annual Session was presided by Rash Behari Ghosh
Statement-II : In this session, Congress got divided into two groups (Moderates and Extremists)
Statement-III : In Congress's Annual Session of 1916, two groups (Moderates and Extremists) got united. This session was presided by S.P. Sinha
Remaining.explanation: Statements I and II are correct. The 1907 Surat session was presided over by Rash Behari Ghosh, where the split occurred. Statement III is incorrect because the 1916 Lucknow Session was presided over by Ambica Charan Mazumdar, not S.P. Sinha.
Remaining.topic: Congress: Benaras, Calcutta, and Surat Session

Remaining.q: Seeds of discord were in which event during National Movement and which eventually divided the country, was
options: Introduction of separate electorates for Muslims in the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909
Remaining.explanation: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced the system of separate electorates for Muslims, which sowed the seeds of communal discord and ultimately led to the partition of India.
Remaining.topic: Morley-Minto Reforms,Delhi Darabar and Capital Change, Lucknow Session of Congress And HRM

Remaining.q: When did Britishers shifted the capital to Delhi ?
Remaining.explanation: The decision to shift the capital of British India from Calcutta to Delhi was announced during the Delhi Durbar on December 12, 1911. The actual transfer was officially completed in 1912.
Remaining.topic: Morley-Minto Reforms,Delhi Darabar and Capital Change, Lucknow Session of Congress And HRM

Remaining.q: At which Viceroy was a bomb thrown on the occasion of his state entry into Delhi?
Remaining.explanation: A bomb was thrown at Viceroy Lord Hardinge during his state entry into Delhi in December 1912. The conspiracy was masterminded by Rash Behari Bose.
Remaining.topic: Morley-Minto Reforms,Delhi Darabar and Capital Change, Lucknow Session of Congress And HRM

Remaining.q: Which among the following organisations was responsible for throwing a bomb at Viceroy Lord Hardinge in Delhi?
Remaining.explanation: Members associated with the Yugantar group and revolutionaries inspired by Rash Behari Bose were responsible for the Delhi Conspiracy Case (the bomb thrown at Lord Hardinge).
Remaining.topic: Morley-Minto Reforms,Delhi Darabar and Capital Change, Lucknow Session of Congress And HRM

Remaining.q: When was Bihar first separated from the Bengal Presidency under the British-ruled India?
Remaining.explanation: Bihar and Orissa were separated from the Bengal Presidency and formed into a new province in 1912 following the announcements made at the 1911 Delhi Durbar.
Remaining.topic: Morley-Minto Reforms,Delhi Darabar and Capital Change, Lucknow Session of Congress And HRM

Remaining.q: Which decision was taken in Lucknow session of Congress in 1916 with long term implications?
options: Acceptance of the demand for separate electorates for Muslims
Remaining.explanation: The most significant long-term decision of the 1916 Lucknow Session was the Congress formally accepting the Muslim League's demand for separate electorates (the Lucknow Pact), which legitimized communal politics.
Remaining.topic: Morley-Minto Reforms,Delhi Darabar and Capital Change, Lucknow Session of Congress And HRM

Remaining.q: Which Congress leader visited Bihar in 1918 in order to strengthen the activities of Home Rule League?
Remaining.explanation: Annie Besant visited Bihar in 1918 to promote and strengthen the activities of the Home Rule League among the local population.
Remaining.topic: Morley-Minto Reforms,Delhi Darabar and Capital Change, Lucknow Session of Congress And HRM

Remaining.q: Karamchand Gandhi was Diwan of-:
Remaining.explanation: Karamchand Gandhi, the father of Mahatma Gandhi, served as the Diwan (Prime Minister) of Porbandar state, and later served in the same capacity in Rajkot and Bankaner.

Remaining.q: The cook from Bihar who saved Mahatma Gandhi's life from a murder attempt by food poisoning in 1917 was
Remaining.explanation: Batak Mian, a cook employed by a British planter in Champaran, famously saved Mahatma Gandhi's life by refusing to serve him poisoned milk in 1917.

Remaining.q: Who saved the life of Gandhiji in Bihar during Champaran Satyagraha?
Remaining.explanation: Batak Mian saved Gandhiji's life during the Champaran Satyagraha by foiling an assassination attempt via poisoned food.

Remaining.q: During the Champaran Satyagraha, the cultivation of Indigo was known as _________.
Remaining.explanation: The cultivation of indigo in Champaran was known as the Tinkathia system, where European planters forced Indian peasants to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land.

Remaining.q: Who opposed Planned Development in India?
Remaining.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi opposed planned development and heavy industrialization in India. He believed in the decentralization of the economy and advocated for village-based cottage industries and a self-reliant rural economy (Gram Swaraj).

Remaining.q: Who is not related to the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 AD?
Remaining.explanation: Jayaprakash Narayan was not associated with the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917. Leaders who actively assisted Mahatma Gandhi in Champaran included Rajendra Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha, J.B. Kripalani, and Mahadev Desai.

Remaining.q: Champaran Agrarian Committee was appointed in agreement between:
options: Mahatma Gandhi and the British Parliament
Remaining.explanation: The Champaran Agrarian Committee was appointed by the British Government to inquire into the grievances of the indigo cultivators. Mahatma Gandhi was also made a member of this committee.

Remaining.q: In response to the mass agitation of the Champaran Movement, the British Government took which step to address the issue?
Remaining.explanation: In response to the mass agitation during the Champaran Movement, the British Government formed the Champaran Agrarian Committee to investigate the complaints of the farmers against the European planters.

Remaining.q: Who led the Champaran Satyagraha in 1917 ?
Remaining.explanation: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was led by Mahatma Gandhi. It was his first major Satyagraha movement in India, organized to fight for the rights of the indigo farmers against the oppressive Tinkathia system.

Remaining.q: Who invited Gandhiji to come to Champaran?
Remaining.explanation: Raj Kumar Shukla, a local farmer from Champaran, met Mahatma Gandhi during the 1916 Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress and invited him to visit Champaran to see the plight of the indigo cultivators.

Remaining.q: In 1918, the United Provinces Kisan Sabha was formed by which of the following leaders?
options: Gauri Shankar Mishra, Indra Narayan Dwivedi, and Madan Mohan Malviya
Swami Sahajanand Saraswati and N.G. Ranga
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Mahatma Gandhi
Remaining.explanation: The United Provinces (UP) Kisan Sabha was set up in February 1918 by Gauri Shankar Mishra and Indra Narayan Dwivedi with the active support of Madan Mohan Malviya.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q: ‘Nai-Dhobi Bandh’ was a form of Social boycott in 1919 which
options: was started by the farmers of Pratapgarh district.
was an organized campaign against the British.
was initiated by the landlords against the peasants.
Remaining.explanation: 'Nai-Dhobi Bandh' (barber and washerman boycott) was a form of social boycott organized by the farmers in the Pratapgarh district of UP in 1919 against oppressive landlords.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q: "A Sanyasi who came to that district after a spell as an indentured labourer in Fiji carrying a copy of Tulsidas Ramayana on his back from which he would recite verses to rural audience." The peasant leader referred to here is
Remaining.explanation: The passage refers to Baba Ramchandra. He was an indentured laborer in Fiji who later came to Awadh (UP) and organized the peasants against the oppressive landlords, often reciting from the Ramcharitmanas to gather and inspire crowds.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q: To highlight the hardships faced by the peasants, Sahajanand Saraswati published which newspaper?
Remaining.explanation: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati started the publication of 'Hunkar', a Hindi weekly, in 1940 to give a voice to the peasant movement and highlight the hardships faced by them.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q: Swami Sahajanand was related to
Remaining.explanation: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati was the most prominent leader of the peasant movement in Bihar. He formed the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (BPKS) in 1929 to mobilize peasant grievances.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati formed the All India United Kisan Sabha with the demand for the ‘nationalization of land and waterways’ :
options: Just before his death in the late 1940s
At the time of India's independence
Remaining.explanation: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati formed the All India United Kisan Sabha just before his death (he died in 1950), emphasizing the demand for the nationalization of land and waterways.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q: Who successfully led the Bardoli Satyagraha?
Remaining.explanation: The Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) in Gujarat was a successful anti-tax movement led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Following its success, the women of Bardoli bestowed the title 'Sardar' upon him.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q: All India Trade Union Congress was formed in the year
Remaining.explanation: The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was founded on 31 October 1920 in Bombay. Lala Lajpat Rai was its first President.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q: Who presided over the inaugural session of the 'All India Trade Union Congress' held in 1920?
Remaining.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the inaugural session of the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) which was held in Bombay in 1920.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q:
Consider the following statements with reference to Trade Union Movement in India :
1. All India Trade Union Congress was founded in 1920.
2. Lala Lajpat Rai was elected its first President.
3. All India Trade Union Federation was formed by S.A. Dange in 1929.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Remaining.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The AITUC was founded in 1920, and Lala Lajpat Rai was its first president. Statement 3 is incorrect because the All India Trade Union Federation (AITUF) was formed in 1929 by N.M. Joshi after a split in the AITUC.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q: In October, 1920, who among the following headed a group of Indians gathered at Tashkent to set up a Communist Party of India?
Remaining.explanation: In October 1920, a group of Indians led by M.N. Roy (Manabendra Nath Roy), Abani Mukherji, and others gathered in Tashkent (now in Uzbekistan) and established the Communist Party of India.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q: The year 1919 in Indian history is related to :
Remaining.explanation: The year 1919 in Indian history is notoriously known for the tragic Jallianwala Bagh Massacre, which occurred on April 13, 1919, in Amritsar.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q: Who returned the ‘Knighthood’ title to the British Government in reaction against Jallianwala Bagh Massacre ?
Remaining.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore surrendered his Knighthood on May 31, 1919, to the British Viceroy as a mark of protest against the brutal Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.
Remaining.topic: Peasant Movement and Kisan Sabha,Trade Union and Communist Party,Rowllact Act and Jalliayawala Bagh Massacre

Remaining.q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was started in
Remaining.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was officially launched by Mahatma Gandhi on August 1, 1920, and was later endorsed by the Indian National Congress in its special session in Calcutta in September 1920.

Remaining.q: With the failure of 1919 reforms to meet the aspirations of the Indians, the Indian National Congress sought 'Swaraj' or 'Self-government' under the leadership of :
Remaining.explanation: Following the disappointment with the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919) and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, the Indian National Congress adopted the goal of 'Swaraj' under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi during the Non-Cooperation Movement.

Remaining.q: Gandhiji's Non-Cooperation Movement urged people to avoid alcohol. This resulted in a serious loss of revenue for the government. The government of a province circulated a list of prominent individuals who drank alcohol as a device to persuade people to start drinking again. Name the province.
Remaining.explanation: During the Non-Cooperation movement, anti-liquor campaigns drastically reduced government revenue in Bihar. In an attempt to encourage people to drink, the Bihar government circulated a list of historical and prominent figures (like Moses, Alexander, and Shakespeare) who consumed alcohol.

Remaining.q: In which state is 'Chauri Chaura', where in February 1922 AD a police station was set on fi re?
Remaining.explanation: Chauri Chaura is located in the Gorakhpur district of Uttar Pradesh. The violent incident there on February 4, 1922, led Mahatma Gandhi to call off the Non-Cooperation Movement.

Remaining.q: Who provided legal defence to the people arrested in the aftermath of Chauri Chaura incident?
Remaining.explanation: Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya provided strong legal defence to the individuals arrested and accused in the Chauri Chaura incident, saving many of them from the death penalty.

Remaining.q: During which movement did Gandhiji call for the boycott of Prince Wales?
Remaining.explanation: The Prince of Wales visited India in 1921. Mahatma Gandhi called for a nationwide boycott of his visit, which took place during the peak of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

Remaining.q:
Consider the following subjects with regard to Non Cooperation Programme :
 I. Boycott of law-courts and foreign cloth
 II. Observance of strict non-violence
 III. Retention of titles and honours without using them in public
 IV. Establishment of Panchayats for settling disputes
 How many of the above were parts of Non-Cooperation Programme?
Remaining.explanation: The Non-Cooperation programme explicitly included the boycott of law courts and foreign cloth, strict non-violence, the establishment of national schools and Panchayats, and importantly, the *surrender* of titles and honours. If 'retention without using them' is presented as an option, it is generally considered part of the overarching boycott framework, making all elements relevant to the structural program.

Remaining.q: Who wrote to Mahatma Gandhi that it was 'a ruthless waste' when foreign clothes were burnt during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
Remaining.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore wrote to Mahatma Gandhi criticizing the burning of foreign clothes during the Non-Cooperation Movement, calling it a 'ruthless waste' (Nishthur barbadi).

Remaining.q: Who left Patna College with just 20 days remaining for his examination during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
Remaining.explanation: Jayaprakash Narayan (JP) left Patna College just 20 days before his examinations to join the Non-Cooperation Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi.

Remaining.q: The Congress took a critical stand over the Montford Reforms in 1918, which led to break up with the old moderate remnants (Sapru, Jayakar and Chintamani) who formed the
Remaining.explanation: When the Congress rejected the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms in 1918, prominent moderate leaders like Tej Bahadur Sapru, M.R. Jayakar, and C.Y. Chintamani left the Congress and formed the Indian National Liberal Federation.
Remaining.topic: Formation of Swaraj Party (1923),Simon Commission,Lahore Session of Congress, Proposal  of Complete Independence (1929)

Remaining.q: Which Commission accentuated the discontent in all the political groups and parties for not associating any Indian member in it?
Remaining.explanation: The Simon Commission (1927) was an all-white commission with no Indian members. This caused widespread anger and led to boycotts by all major Indian political parties under the slogan 'Simon Go Back'.
Remaining.topic: Formation of Swaraj Party (1923),Simon Commission,Lahore Session of Congress, Proposal  of Complete Independence (1929)

Remaining.q:
Consider the following statements with reference to Simon Commission
1. It made two visits to India.
2. Its second visit was from October 11, 1929 to April 13, 1930.
Select the correct answer the code given below :
Code
Remaining.explanation: The Simon Commission visited India twice. The first visit was from February to March 1928, and the second visit was from October 11, 1929, to April 13, 1930. Thus, both statements are correct.
Remaining.topic: Formation of Swaraj Party (1923),Simon Commission,Lahore Session of Congress, Proposal  of Complete Independence (1929)

Remaining.q: In which session of the Congress was the “Purna Swaraj” resolution passed?
Remaining.explanation: The historic 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution was passed during the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.
Remaining.topic: Formation of Swaraj Party (1923),Simon Commission,Lahore Session of Congress, Proposal  of Complete Independence (1929)

options: Gauri Shankar Mishra, Indra Narayan Dwivedi, and Madan Mohan Malviya
Swami Sahajanand Saraswati and N.G. Ranga
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and Mahatma Gandhi
Remaining.explanation: The United Provinces (UP) Kisan Sabha was set up in February 1918 by Gauri Shankar Mishra and Indra Narayan Dwivedi with the active support of Madan Mohan Malviya.

Consider the following statements with reference to Simon Commission
1. It made two visits to India.
2. Its second visit was from October 11, 1929 to April 13, 1930.
Select the correct answer the code given below :
Code

Remaining.q: In which session of the Congress was the “Purna Swaraj” resolution passed?
Remaining.explanation: The historic 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution was passed during the Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress in December 1929.

Remaining.q: In August 1932, British Prime Minister announced the scheme for representation of depressed classes. This was called Communal Award. Gandhiji started fast unto death in opposition to this scheme in which jail?

Remaining.q: On defeating which politician, did Subhas Chandra Bose become the President of the Indian National Congress?
Remaining.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose defeated Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya (the candidate supported by Mahatma Gandhi) in the election for the presidency of the INC at the Tripuri Session in 1939.

Subhas Chandra Bose during INA march

Remaining.q: By which one of the following Acts was the Governor General of Bengal designated as the Governor General of India?
Remaining.explanation: The Charter Act of 1833 centralized administration by elevating the Governor-General of Bengal to the position of Governor-General of India. Lord William Bentinck was the first to hold this new title.

Remaining.q: Which of the among following had recommended to hold the Indian Civil Service Examination simultaneously in India & England?
Remaining.explanation: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report (1918) advised that the Civil Service examinations should be held simultaneously in both India and England to facilitate greater Indian representation in the administration.

Remaining.q:
With reference to Indian Civil Services, which of the following statement/s is/are correct?  
 1. Government of India Act, 1919 provided for a separate examination for the Indian Civil Service, which was to be held in India. 
 2. In the Indian Civil Service in 1941, the percentage of Indians was more as compared to the Europeans.   
 Select the correct answer using the code given below :
Remaining.explanation: Both statements are historically accurate. The 1919 Act paved the way for simultaneous exams in India, and by 1941, due to a steady increase in recruitment, Indian officers in the ICS outnumbered their European counterparts.

Remaining.q: Who is known as father of Dyarchy?
Remaining.explanation: Sir Lionel Curtis, a British official and author, is widely recognized as the primary architect of the 'Dyarchy' system, which divided executive powers into 'reserved' and 'transferred' subjects.

Remaining.q: In which Constitutional document was Dyarchy System introduced in Indian provinces?
Remaining.explanation: The Government of India Act of 1919 formally introduced the system of Dyarchy at the provincial level, allowing Indian ministers limited control over certain administrative departments.

Remaining.q: In the Federation established by The Government of India Act of 1935, residuary powers were given to the:
Remaining.explanation: Under the framework of the Government of India Act 1935, any legislative powers not explicitly listed in the Federal, Provincial, or Concurrent lists (residuary powers) were granted solely to the Governor-General.

Remaining.q:
Consider the following wars and arrange them in correct chronological order.
1. First Anglo-Mysore War
2. Second Anglo-French War
3. First Anglo-Sikh War
4. First Anglo-Afghan War
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Code:
Remaining.explanation: The proper timeline is: Second Anglo-French (Carnatic) War (1749-1754), First Anglo-Mysore War (1767-1769), First Anglo-Afghan War (1839-1842), and finally the First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-1846).

Remaining.q:
Which of the following commissions are related to famine in British India ?
1. Campbell Commission
2. Lyall Commission
3. Strachey Commission
4. Hunter Commission
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
Remaining.explanation: The Campbell, Lyall, and Strachey commissions were all established to investigate and manage famines during British rule. The Hunter Commission is primarily associated with education reforms and investigating the Jallianwala Bagh incident.

Remaining.q:
Consider the following events of Modern Indian History
1. Death sentence to Raja Nand Kumar
2. Treaty of Salbai
3. Battle of Wandiwash
4. Death of Tipu Sultan
Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the above events?
Remaining.explanation: The Battle of Wandiwash occurred in 1760. Raja Nand Kumar was executed in 1775. The Treaty of Salbai was signed in 1782. Tipu Sultan died in battle in 1799.

Remaining.q:
Examine the following statements.
1. Kunwar Singh led the struggle in Bihar against British while Khan Bahadur Khan led in Ruhelkhand in First Independence Struggle, 1857.
2. Muslim League was observed Deliverance Day on 22 December, 1939.
3. Tatya Topey took the lead of armies in Kanpur for the patronage of Nana Saheb and Zeenat Mahal assumed leadership in Faizabad.
4. Ghadar Party was founded Sardar Bhagat Singh.
Select the correct answer by using codes given below:
Remaining.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are historically correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because Begum Hazrat Mahal, not Zeenat Mahal, led in Lucknow/Awadh, and Maulvi Ahmadullah led in Faizabad. Statement 4 is incorrect as the Ghadar Party was founded by leaders like Lala Hardayal, not Bhagat Singh.

Remaining.q: “The British Government is not responsible for the partition of India.” The above statement is attributed to :
Remaining.explanation: Clement Attlee, the British Prime Minister during India's independence, made statements distancing the British administration from the direct responsibility of the communal partition, attributing it instead to domestic political disagreements.

Remaining.q: Regarding William A.J. Archibald, which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: He served as a principal of M.A.O. College.
He was sympathetic to Indian nationalist aspirations.
He played a role in advising Muslim leaders prior to the Simla Deputation.
He maintained close ties with British administrative officials.
Remaining.explanation: While Archibald was Principal of the Aligarh College and advised the Simla Deputation, historical consensus indicates he was an imperialist who encouraged loyalism rather than being broadly sympathetic to anti-British nationalist aspirations.

Remaining.q: In which year, did Rabindranath Tagore die?
Remaining.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore, the Nobel laureate poet and philosopher, passed away on August 7, 1941, in Calcutta.

Remaining.q: Bhartiya Kisan Sangh was established in which year?
Remaining.explanation: The Bharatiya Kisan Sangh, a prominent Indian farmers' organization, was established in the year 1979 by Dattopant Thengadi.

Remaining.q: Ambabai, a woman freedom fi ghter, belonged to which of the following States of India?
Remaining.explanation: Ambabai was a notable female freedom fighter who actively participated in the nationalist struggle from the Udupi region in present-day Karnataka.

Remaining.q: Which lady contributed the most to Indian politics after 1947?
Remaining.explanation: Among the options listed, Aruna Asaf Ali continued to have a profound impact on post-independence Indian politics, remaining active in left-wing politics and media organization.

Remaining.q: Who is known as 'Frontier Gandhi'?
Remaining.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, a Pashtun independence activist and close associate of Mahatma Gandhi, was affectionately known as 'Frontier Gandhi' (Sarhadi Gandhi).

Remaining.q: Who among the following are known as 'Bombay Trimurti'?
options: Pherozeshah Mehta, K.T. Telang, and Badruddin Tyabji
Bal Gangadhar Tilak, G.K. Gokhale, and M.G. Ranade
Dadabhai Naoroji, Dinshaw Wacha, and S.N. Banerjee
Remaining.explanation: Pherozeshah Mehta, K.T. Telang, and Badruddin Tyabji were collectively referred to as the 'Bombay Trimurti' (the Trinity of Bombay) for their collaborative role in establishing the Bombay Presidency Association in 1885.

Remaining.q: How did the study of history help in creating a feeling of nationalism in India towards the end of the 19th century?
options: By rediscovering India's glorious past and challenging the colonial narrative of Indian backwardness.
By focusing entirely on European historical achievements.
By emphasizing regional differences to divide communities.
By promoting the cultural superiority of British rule.
Remaining.explanation: Nationalist historians and scholars researched ancient Indian history to highlight the subcontinent's past achievements in science, art, and administration, thereby instilling a sense of national pride and countering British claims of cultural superiority.

Remaining.q: Jagat Narain Lal was sent to :
Remaining.explanation: During the nationalist uprisings, prominent Bihar leader Jagat Narain Lal was imprisoned in the Hazaribagh Jail by the colonial administration.

Remaining.q: The year of Bengal Famine in which millions of people died is :
Remaining.explanation: The tragic Bengal Famine, which resulted in the deaths of millions due to starvation, malnutrition, and disease, occurred primarily during the year 1943 amidst the backdrop of World War II.

Remaining.q: Against which colonial power did the freedom struggle have to continue in India even after 15 August, 1947?
Remaining.explanation: Even after gaining independence from the British in 1947, India had to continue its political and eventually military struggles against the Portuguese to liberate territories like Goa, Daman, and Diu, which were finally integrated in 1961.

Remaining.q: The political strategy Struggle-Truce-Struggle or S-T-S came into prominence with a call for
options: Mass mobilization phased with periods of negotiation and consolidation
Immediate unconditional surrender to colonial demands
Strict adherence to constitutional reforms only
Remaining.explanation: The 'Struggle-Truce-Struggle' (S-T-S) strategy was a core component of Mahatma Gandhi's political approach. It involved alternating periods of active mass agitation with phases of constructive work and negotiation to allow the masses to rest and consolidate gains.

Remaining.q:
Match the following and choose the correct answer.
Political Organisation Founder
I. Khaksars A. Subhash Chandra Bose
II. Socialist Party B. Inayatullah Mashriqui
III. Independent Labour Party C. Jayaprakash Narayan 
IV. Forward Bloc D. B.R. Ambedkar
Remaining.explanation: The correct pairings are: The Khaksar movement was founded by Allama Mashriqi (B); The Socialist Party is associated with JP Narayan (C); The Independent Labour Party was founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (D); and the Forward Bloc was established by Subhas Chandra Bose (A).

Remaining.q: The objective of the Butler Committee of 1927 was to :
options: Define the jurisdiction of the Central and Provincial Governments
Define the powers of the Secretary of State for India
Improve the relationship between the Government of India and the Indian Princely States
Remaining.explanation: The Harcourt Butler Committee (Indian States Committee) was appointed in 1927 primarily to investigate and clarify the relationship between the Paramount Power (the British Crown) and the rulers of the Indian Princely States.

Remaining.q: Alipore Central Jail is situated at
Remaining.explanation: Alipore Central Jail, a historic prison where numerous prominent political prisoners and freedom fighters were held during British rule, is located in Kolkata (formerly Calcutta), West Bengal.

Remaining.q: Which one of the famous buildings in New Delhi has been converted into Prime Ministers Museum?
Remaining.explanation: Teen Murti Bhavan, which originally served as the official residence of India's first Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, was recently redeveloped into the Pradhanmantri Sangrahalaya (Prime Ministers' Museum).

Remaining.q: The people known as 'Kallar' in the context of the rebellions in British India belonged to which of the following regions?
Remaining.explanation: The Kallars are a community primarily concentrated in the southern districts of Tamil Nadu, such as Madurai. They were notably categorized under the controversial Criminal Tribes Act by the British administration.

Remaining.q: The Act of 1909 was associated with :
Remaining.explanation: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, is most historically significant for introducing the system of separate electorates for Muslims in India.

Remaining.q: The nomenclature of rural local governments as 'Panchayati Raj' was the result of the suggestion of which Indian leader?
Remaining.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi was a staunch advocate for rural empowerment and village self-governance. He championed the concept of 'Gram Swaraj', which heavily influenced the formal adoption of the term and system of 'Panchayati Raj'.

Remaining.q: Who has authored 'Gandhian Constitution for Free India'?
Remaining.explanation: The book 'Gandhian Constitution for Free India' was written by Shriman Narayan Agarwal in 1946, outlining a decentralized village-based framework inspired by Gandhi's ideals.

Remaining.q: Whose famous literary work is "Mukul"?
Remaining.explanation: 'Mukul' is a famous poetry collection authored by the renowned Hindi poetess Subhadra Kumari Chauhan, published in 1930.

Remaining.q: Who authored the book "The Challenge of World Poverty"?
Remaining.explanation: 'The Challenge of World Poverty' is a widely recognized book written by Swedish economist and Nobel laureate Gunnar Myrdal.

Remaining.q: Who is the ghostwriter of Parvez Musharraf’s biography “In the Line of Fire”?
Remaining.explanation: Humayun Gauhar, a prominent Pakistani journalist and writer, was the ghostwriter for former Pakistani President Pervez Musharraf's memoir 'In the Line of Fire'.

Remaining.q: Which of the following columns is not correctly matched?
options: Bhagat Singh - Why I am an Atheist
M.K. Gandhi - My Experiments with Truth
Remaining.explanation: The incorrect match is 'Jawaharlal Nehru - Hind Swaraj'. The book 'Hind Swaraj' was written by Mahatma Gandhi, not Jawaharlal Nehru.

Remaining.q: Which of the following (Poetess-Compositions) is not correctly matched?
Remaining.explanation: 'Urvashi' is a famous work by Ramdhari Singh Dinkar, not Subhadra Kumari Chauhan. Therefore, this option is incorrectly matched.

Remaining.q: In which language the famous work of Raja Rammohan Roy 'Gift to Monotheists' was written?
Remaining.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy's famous work 'Gift to Monotheists' (Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin) was originally written in the Persian language with an Arabic introduction in 1803-04.

Remaining.q: In 1809, Raja Ram Mohan Roy wrote his famous book "Gift to Monotheist" in which of the following language?
Remaining.explanation: The book 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin' (A Gift to Monotheists) was written by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Persian.

Remaining.q: The memoir titled ‘Bapu: My Mother’ was written by:
Remaining.explanation: The memoir 'Bapu: My Mother' was written by Manubehn Gandhi (Mridula Gandhi), the grandniece of Mahatma Gandhi who cared for him in his final years.

Remaining.q: On whom did Balkrishna Sharma Naveen write two kavyas –– 'Pranarpan' and 'Atmosarga'?
Remaining.explanation: The renowned Hindi poet Balkrishna Sharma 'Naveen' wrote 'Pranarpan' and 'Atmosarga' in memory of the great freedom fighter and journalist Ganesh Shankar Vidyarthi.

Remaining.q: Who wrote "New Lamps For The Old"?
Remaining.explanation: 'New Lamps for Old' was a series of critical articles written by Aurobindo Ghosh in the Indu Prakash in 1893, fiercely criticizing the moderate politics of the Indian National Congress.

Remaining.q: In 1929 at which place Mahatma Gandhi complete his translation of Anasakti Yoga?
Remaining.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi stayed at the Anasakti Ashram in Kausani (Uttarakhand) for 14 days in 1929, where he penned his famous commentary on the Bhagavad Gita titled 'Anasakti Yoga'.

Remaining.q:
Match the List - I of authors with List-II of the books on 1857 and choose answers from the code given below:
List - I
(A) V. D. Savarkar
(B) S. N. Sen
(C) Eric Stokes
(D) S.B. Chaudhuri
List - II
(i) The First War of Independence
(ii) The Peasant and the Raj
(iii) Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies
(iv) Eighteen Fifty-Seven
Code : A B C D
Remaining.explanation: V.D. Savarkar wrote 'The First War of Independence' (i). S.N. Sen authored 'Eighteen Fifty-Seven' (iv). Eric Stokes wrote 'The Peasant and the Raj' (ii). S.B. Chaudhuri authored 'Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies' (iii).

Remaining.q: The book “Guilty Men of India’s Partition” was authored by:
Remaining.explanation: 'Guilty Men of India's Partition' was written by the socialist leader Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia, critiquing the events and leaders responsible for the partition.

Remaining.q: Nobel Prize was awarded to Rabindranath Nath Tagore in the year :
Remaining.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore became the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his profoundly sensitive, fresh and beautiful collection of poetry, 'Gitanjali'.

Remaining.q: The song ‘Amar Sonar Bangla’ written during the Swadeshi Movement of India inspired the liberation struggle of Bangladesh and was adopted as the National Anthem of Bangladesh. Who wrote this song?
Remaining.explanation: 'Amar Sonar Bangla' was composed by Rabindranath Tagore in 1905 to protest the Partition of Bengal. It was later adopted by Bangladesh as its national anthem in 1971.

Remaining.q: The first Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, a music training school, was set up in 1901 by Vishnu Digambar Paluskar in
Remaining.explanation: Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar established the first Gandharva Mahavidyalaya in Lahore on 5th May 1901 to formalize and popularize Indian classical music training.

Remaining.q: After how many years is ‘Maha Kumbh’ held?
Remaining.explanation: While the regular Purna Kumbh Mela takes place every 12 years, the 'Maha Kumbh Mela' occurs only once every 144 years (after 12 Purna Kumbhs) at Prayagraj.

Remaining.q: In which place is Kumbh Mela held every twelfth year?
Remaining.explanation: The Kumbh Mela is held at four places: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, and Nashik. It returns to each of these locations every twelfth year.

Remaining.q: The book ‘Venushilpa’ by Chitracharya Upendra Maharathi relates to which of the following form of arts?
Remaining.explanation: Chitracharya Upendra Maharathi extensively studied and documented traditional bamboo crafts. His renowned book 'Venushilpa' deals with Bamboo Art (Venu means bamboo).

Remaining.q: Where was the first Sanskrit University Chair established?
Remaining.explanation: The first University Chair of Sanskrit in Europe was established at the Collège de France in Paris, France, in 1814, with Antoine-Léonard de Chézy as the first professor.

Remaining.q: The earliest reference to ‘Magnetic Compass’ is found in:
Remaining.explanation: The earliest Persian reference to the use of a magnetic compass for navigation in the Indian Ocean is found in the 'Jawami ul-Hikayat' written by Sadiduddin Muhammad Awfi in 1232 AD.

Remaining.q: Identify one of the following who is not associated with Kathak dance
Remaining.explanation: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra is a legendary maestro associated with Odissi dance, not Kathak. The others are all renowned exponents of the Kathak dance form.

Remaining.q: What is Monalisa?
Remaining.explanation: The Mona Lisa is a famous half-length portrait painting created by the Italian Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci.

Remaining.q: The famous 'Gangasagar Mela' is held in which of the following states of India?
Remaining.explanation: The Gangasagar Mela is an annual gathering of Hindu pilgrims on Sagar Island in West Bengal, where the River Ganges meets the Bay of Bengal.

Remaining.q: In which country is the three-day celebration of Thadingyut festival celebrated?
Remaining.explanation: The Thadingyut Festival, also known as the Lighting Festival of Myanmar, is celebrated widely in Myanmar to mark the end of the Buddhist lent.

Remaining.q: What amount goes with Arjuna Award :
Remaining.explanation: As of recent revisions by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in India, the cash prize for the Arjuna Award has been increased to ₹15 Lakhs.

Important Questions.q: 12. Match List-I (Doab) with List-II (Rivers): A. Bist Doab B. Bari Doab C. Rachna Doab D. Chaj Doab | i. Between Ravi and Chenab ii. Between Ravi and Beas iii. Between Beas and Sutlej iv. Between Chenab and Jhelum
Important Questions.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— (Doab) Bist Doab Bari Doab – (Rivers)– Between the Beas and the Sutlej– Between the Ravi and the Beas Rachna Doab – Between the Ravi and the Chenab Chaj Doab – Between the Chenab and the Jhelum

Important Questions.q: 27. Consider the following historical sites— 1. Ajanta Caves 2. Lepakshi Temple 3. Sanchi Stupa. Which of the above sites is/are also known for mural paintings?
Important Questions.explanation: The evidence of mural painting is very clear in the Ajanta Caves and the Lepakshi Temple; however, the evidence of mural painting is not clear in the Sanchi Stupa. The toranas placed around the stupa are full of depictions of events from the life of Buddha and Jataka stories, and are decorated from bottom to top. Since the toranas cannot be considered a part of the stupa, option (b) will be the intended answer.

Important Questions.q: 38. With reference to Indian history, consider the following statements— 1. The first Mongol invasion of India took place during the reign of Jalaluddin Khalji. 2. During the reign of Alauddin Khalji, a Mongol invasion reached Delhi and besieged the city. 3. Muhammad bin Tughlaq temporarily lost some north-western parts of his kingdom to the Mongols.
Important Questions.explanation: The first Mongol invasion of India did not take place during the time of Jalaluddin Khilji. The Mongol threat had appeared much earlier during the reign of Iltutmish, when the Mongols reached the Indus region while pursuing Jalaluddin Mangbarni. During the period of Alauddin Khilji, the Mongol invader Targhi/Taraghai attacked Delhi in around 1303 AD. At that time, Alauddin Khilji was engaged in the Chittor campaign. During the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq, a Mongol campaign took place under the leadership of Tarmashirin. However, Muhammad bin Tughlaq captured Kalanaur and Peshawar and foiled the Mongol campaign.

Important Questions.q: 40. Which of the following Brahmana texts is related to the Rigveda?
Important Questions.explanation: The Brahmana texts are prose texts related to the rituals, sacrificial procedures and their meanings/interpretations associated with the Vedas. The Aitareya Brahmana and the Kaushitaki/ Shankhayana Brahmana are related to the Rigveda. The Panchavimsha or Tandya Brahmana and the Jaiminiya Brahmana are related to the Samaveda. The Shatapatha Brahmana is related to the Shukla Yajurveda, while the Taittiriya Brahmana is related to the Krishna Yajurveda. The Gopatha Brahmana is the Brahmana text of the Atharvaveda. Therefore, among the given options, the Brahmana text related to the Rigveda is the Aitareya Brahmana.
The Mughal-period text ‘Maasir i-Alamgiri’ was written by Saqi Mustaid Khan. Written in the Persian language, this text provides details of the reign of Aurangzeb.

Important Questions.q: 45. “If Muslims are happy and satisfied, they will be the greatest safeguard of British power in India.” Who wrote this statement?
Important Questions.explanation: W. W. Hunter wrote in his book ‘The Indian Musalmans’ that “if the Muslims are happy and satisfied, it will be the greatest safeguard of British power in India.”

Important Questions.q: 86. Whom did Iltutmish appoint as the first Subedar of Bihar?
Important Questions.explanation: Iltutmish captured Bihar Sharif and Barh and defeated Husamuddin Iwaz Khalji near Teliagarhi in the Rajmahal hills. Iwaz accepted the authority of Iltutmish. Iltutmish appointed Malik Alauddin Jani as the governor of Bihar in place of Iwaz.
